And Sumukha, Durmukha and the monkey, vegadarcin (resembling) Death himself, were for certain begot by the Self-create in the shape of a monkey.* *Another meaning is, “The monkey, Vegadarsi who is death himself in the shape of a monkey." But I give the acceptable sense.

पुत्रो हुतवहस्याथ नीलः सेनापतिः स्वयम्
अनिलस्य च पुत्रोऽत्र हनूमानिति विश्रुतः

putro hutavahasyātha nīlaḥ senāpatiḥ svayam
anilasya ca putro'tra hanūmāniti viśrutaḥ
Nila himself is the son of the bearer of sacrificial oblations;* and Hanuman is famed as the son of the Wind-god. * Fire.

नप्ता शक्रस्य दुर्धर्षो बलवानङ्गदो युवा
मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चोभौ बलिनावश्विसंभवौ

naptā śakrasya durdharṣo balavānaṅgado yuvā
maindaśca dvividaścobhau balināvaśvisaṁbhavau
The irrepressible and youthful Angada is the grandson of Sakra. And the lusty Mainda and Dvivida are sprung from Asvi.

पुत्रा वैवस्वतस्यात्र पञ्चकालान्तकोपमाः
गजो गवाक्षो गवयः शरभो गन्धमादनः

putrā vaivasvatasyātra pañcakālāntakopamāḥ
gajo gavākṣo gavayaḥ śarabho gandhamādanaḥ
And five are the sons of Vaivasvata, resembling the Reaper himself, Gaya, Gavaks a, gavaya, Sarabha and Gandhamadana.

श्वेतो ज्योतिर्मुखश्चात्र भास्करस्यात्मसंभवौ
वरुणस्य च पुत्रोऽथ हेमकूटः प्लवंगमः

śveto jyotirmukhaścātra bhāskarasyātmasaṁbhavau
varuṇasya ca putro'tha hemakūṭaḥ plavaṁgamaḥ
And here are sveta and Jyotirmukha, sprung from Vaskara's self; and the monkey Hemakuta is the son of Varuna.

विश्वकर्मसुतो वीरो नलः प्लवगसत्तमः
विक्रान्तो वेगवानत्र वसुपुत्रः सुदुर्धरः

viśvakarmasuto vīro nalaḥ plavagasattamaḥ
vikrānto vegavānatra vasuputraḥ sudurdharaḥ
The heroic Nalabest of monkeys, is the son of Visvakarma. And powerful and impetuous, Durdhara is the son of Vasu.

दशवानरकोट्यश्च शूराणां युद्धकाङ्क्षिणाम्
श्रीमतां देवपुत्राणां शेषान्नाख्यातुमुत्सहे

daśavānarakoṭyaśca śūrāṇāṁ yuddhakāṅkṣiṇām
śrīmatāṁ devaputrāṇāṁ śeṣānnākhyātumutsahe
But I can not enumerate the rest, ten kotis of heroic monkeys-all sons of deities—burning for battle.

पुत्रो दशरथस्यैष सिंहसंहननो युवा
दूषणो निहतो येन खरश्च त्रिशिरास्तथा

putro daśarathasyaiṣa siṁhasaṁhanano yuvā
dūṣaṇo nihato yena kharaśca triśirāstathā
And this is Dasaratha's son—this you resembling a lion, who slew Dusana and Khara and Trisiras.

नास्ति रामस्य सदृशो विक्रमे भुवि कश्चन
विराधो निहतो येन कबन्धश्चान्तकोपमः

nāsti rāmasya sadṛśo vikrame bhuvi kaścana
virādho nihato yena kabandhaścāntakopamaḥ
There breathes none on Earth that is like to Rama in prowess, by whom was slain Viradha and Kabandha, resembling the Destroyer.

वक्तुं न शक्तो रामस्य नरः कश्चिद्गुणान्क्षितौ
जनस्थानगता येन तावन्तो राक्षसा हताः

vaktuṁ na śakto rāmasya naraḥ kaścidguṇānkṣitau
janasthānagatā yena tāvanto rākṣasā hatāḥ
No person can on earth describe the virtues of Rama; by whom have been slain all those Raksasas that had gone to Janasthana.

लक्ष्मणश्चात्र धर्मात्मा मातंगानामिवर्षभः
यस्य बाणपथं प्राप्य न जीवेदपि वासवः

lakṣmaṇaścātra dharmātmā mātaṁgānāmivarṣabhaḥ
yasya bāṇapathaṁ prāpya na jīvedapi vāsavaḥ
Here also is the virtuous Laksmana, like to the foremost of elephants, coming in the way of whose shafts, even Vasava does not live.

राक्षसानां वरिष्ठश्च तव भ्राता विभीषणः
परिगृह्य पुरीं लङ्कां राघवस्य हिते रतः

rākṣasānāṁ variṣṭhaśca tava bhrātā vibhīṣaṇaḥ
parigṛhya purīṁ laṅkāṁ rāghavasya hite rataḥ
That foremost of Raksasas, Vibhisana, your brother, engaged in the welfare of Raghava, has laid seige to Lanka.

इति सर्वं समाख्यातं तवेदं वानरं बलम्
सुवेलेऽधिष्ठितं शैले शेषकार्ये भवान्गतिः

iti sarvaṁ samākhyātaṁ tavedaṁ vānaraṁ balam
suvele'dhiṣṭhitaṁ śaile śeṣakārye bhavāngatiḥ
Thus have I described to you the entire monkey host stationed in mount Suvela. As for what remain to be done, you are the master.

चाराणां रावणः श्रुत्वा प्राप्तं रामं महाबलम्
जातोद्वेगोऽभवत्किंचित्सचिवांश्चेदमब्रवीत्

cārāṇāṁ rāvaṇaḥ śrutvā prāptaṁ rāmaṁ mahābalam
jātodvego'bhavatkiṁcitsacivāṁścedamabravīt

Then the spies of the king informed him of the forces of Raghava, incapable of being agitated, which had stationed themselves on Suvela. Hearing the arrival of Rama's mighty army from the spies, Ravana was a little agitated, and he spoke to the ministers.

मन्त्रिणः शीघ्रमायान्तु सर्वे वै सुसमाहिताः
अयं नो मन्त्रकालो हि संप्राप्त इव राक्षसाः

mantriṇaḥ śīghramāyāntu sarve vai susamāhitāḥ
ayaṁ no mantrakālo hi saṁprāpta iva rākṣasāḥ
Let the ministers speedily present themselves, having their wits about them, the time forsooth has come for counsel.

तस्य तच्छासनं श्रुत्वा मन्त्रिणोऽभ्यागमन्द्रुतम्
ततः संमन्त्रयामास सचिवै राक्षसैः सह

tasya tacchāsanaṁ śrutvā mantriṇo'bhyāgamandrutam
tataḥ saṁmantrayāmāsa sacivai rākṣasaiḥ saha
Hearing his mandate, those Raksasas, his counsellors, swiftly presented themselves. And then he consulted with his Raksasa counsellors.

मन्त्रयित्वा स दुर्धर्षः क्षमं यत्समनन्तरम्
विसर्जयित्वा सचिवान्प्रविवेश स्वमालयम्

mantrayitvā sa durdharṣaḥ kṣamaṁ yatsamanantaram
visarjayitvā sacivānpraviveśa svamālayam
Having deliberated duly, that resistless one, dismissing his ministers, entered his own abode.

ततो राक्षसमाहूय विद्युज्जिह्वं महाबलम्
मायाविदं महामायः प्राविशद्यत्र मैथिली

tato rākṣasamāhūya vidyujjihvaṁ mahābalam
māyāvidaṁ mahāmāyaḥ prāviśadyatra maithilī
Then, taking with him the highly strong Vidyujjihva, huge bodied and gifted with the powers of illusion, he entered where Mithila's daughter was.

विद्युज्जिह्वं च मायाज्ञमब्रवीद्राक्षसाधिपः
मोहयिष्यामहे सीतां मायया जनकात्मजाम्

vidyujjihvaṁ ca māyājñamabravīdrākṣasādhipaḥ
mohayiṣyāmahe sītāṁ māyayā janakātmajām
The lord of Raksasas said to Vidyujjihva, skilled in illusion, Do you bring Janaka's daughter under the sway of illusion.

शिरो मायामयं गृह्य राघवस्य निशाचर
मां त्वं समुपतिष्ठस्व महच्च सशरं धनुः

śiro māyāmayaṁ gṛhya rāghavasya niśācara
māṁ tvaṁ samupatiṣṭhasva mahacca saśaraṁ dhanuḥ
O ranger of the night, do you, taking an illusory head of Raghava, as well as a mighty bow with the shaft (set), present yourself before me.

एवमुक्तस्तथेत्याह विद्युज्जिह्वो निशाचरः
तस्य तुष्टोऽभवद्राजा प्रददौ च विभूषणम्

evamuktastathetyāha vidyujjihvo niśācaraḥ
tasya tuṣṭo'bhavadrājā pradadau ca vibhūṣaṇam
Thus accosted, the night-ranger, Vidyujjibha, saying, So be it, displayed that desired illusion to Ravana.

अशोकवनिकायां तु प्रविवेश महाबलः
ततो दीनामदैन्यार्हां ददर्श धनदानुजः
अधोमुखीं शोकपरामुपविष्टां महीतले

aśokavanikāyāṁ tu praviveśa mahābalaḥ
tato dīnāmadainyārhāṁ dadarśa dhanadānujaḥ
adhomukhīṁ śokaparāmupaviṣṭāṁ mahītale

Then the exceedingly powerful lord of the Naistas, the younger brother of the Dispenser of riches, entered (into that place) and saw (there Sita) distressed, albeit unworthy of distress, with her head hung down, overwhelmed with woe, sitting on the ground, staying at the asoka woods, engaged in the contemplation of her lord, conciliated by dreadful Raksasis remaining near. then, drawing near Sita, Ravana, proclaiming his exultation, said these haughty words to the daughter of Janaka.

सान्त्व्यमाना मया भद्रे यमुपाश्रित्य वल्गसे
खर हन्ता स ते भर्ता राघवः समरे हतः

sāntvyamānā mayā bhadre yamupāśritya valgase
khara hantā sa te bhartā rāghavaḥ samare hataḥ
O gentle one, he depending on whom you, being soothed by (me), slight me-that slayer of Khara, your husband, Raghava, has fallen in battle.

छिन्नं ते सर्वतो मूलं दर्पस्ते निहतो मया
व्यसनेनात्मनः सीते मम भार्या भविष्यसि

chinnaṁ te sarvato mūlaṁ darpaste nihato mayā
vyasanenātmanaḥ sīte mama bhāryā bhaviṣyasi

Your roots have been completely severed, and your pride has been destroyed by me. In consequence of this calamity, O Sita, you shall become my wife. O foolish (girl), renounce this idea. What will you do with that is dead?

अल्पपुण्ये निवृत्तार्थे मूढे पण्डितमानिनि
शृणु भर्तृबधं सीते घोरं वृत्रवधं यथा

alpapuṇye nivṛttārthe mūḍhe paṇḍitamānini
śṛṇu bhartṛbadhaṁ sīte ghoraṁ vṛtravadhaṁ yathā

O meek (wench), be you the mistress of all my wives. O you of slender religious merit! O you whose object has been defeated! O you that presumes to be wise! Hearken to the destruction of your lord, like the dreadful destruction of Vrtra!

समायातः समुद्रान्तं मां हन्तुं किल राघवः
वानरेन्द्रप्रणीतेन बलेन महता वृतः

samāyātaḥ samudrāntaṁ māṁ hantuṁ kila rāghavaḥ
vānarendrapraṇītena balena mahatā vṛtaḥ
Surrounded by a vast army gathered by the sovereign of the monkeys, Raghava had presented himself on the shore of the sea, for compassing my destruction.

संनिविष्टः समुद्रस्य तीरमासाद्य दक्षिणम्
बलेन महता रामो व्रजत्यस्तं दिवाकरे

saṁniviṣṭaḥ samudrasya tīramāsādya dakṣiṇam
balena mahatā rāmo vrajatyastaṁ divākare
And on the sun have set, Rama stationed himself with his mighty army, oppressing the northern shore (of the sea).

अथाध्वनि परिश्रान्तमर्धरात्रे स्थितं बलम्
सुखसुप्तं समासाद्य चारितं प्रथमं चरैः

athādhvani pariśrāntamardharātre sthitaṁ balam
sukhasuptaṁ samāsādya cāritaṁ prathamaṁ caraiḥ
Then at midnight (my) spies coming to that host, thus stationed, fatigued from travel, and sleeping soundly (in consequence), first ranged it.

तत्प्रहस्तप्रणीतेन बलेन महता मम
बलमस्य हतं रात्रौ यत्र रामः सुलक्ष्मणः

tatprahastapraṇītena balena mahatā mama
balamasya hataṁ rātrau yatra rāmaḥ sulakṣmaṇaḥ
Then my mighty forces led by Prahasta slew his host overnight, where was present Rama along with Laksmana.

यष्टीश्च तोमरान्प्रासंश्चक्राणि मुसलानि च
उद्यम्योद्यम्य रक्षोभिर्वानरेषु निपातिताः

yaṣṭīśca tomarānprāsaṁścakrāṇi musalāni ca
udyamyodyamya rakṣobhirvānareṣu nipātitāḥ

And repeatedly upraising pattisas and bludgeons, swords, rods and other mighty weapons; and (discharging) showers of arrows, and darts, and daggers and maces and sticks and crows and bearded darts and discuses and clubs; the Raksasas discharged these among the monkeys.

अथ सुप्तस्य रामस्य प्रहस्तेन प्रमाथिना
असक्तं कृतहस्तेन शिरश्छिन्नं महासिना

atha suptasya rāmasya prahastena pramāthinā
asaktaṁ kṛtahastena śiraśchinnaṁ mahāsinā
While Rama was sleeping, the furious Prahasta by means of a mighty falchion, with speed cut off his head clean.

विभीषणः समुत्पत्य निगृहीतो यदृच्छया
दिशः प्रव्राजितः सर्वैर्लक्ष्मणः प्लवगैः सह

vibhīṣaṇaḥ samutpatya nigṛhīto yadṛcchayā
diśaḥ pravrājitaḥ sarvairlakṣmaṇaḥ plavagaiḥ saha
Vibhisana, who was flying at his will, was taken captive. And Laksmana along with the monkeys army has departed somewhere.

सुग्रीवो ग्रीवया शेते भग्नया प्लवगाधिपः
निरस्तहनुकः शेते हनूमान्राक्षसैर्हतः

sugrīvo grīvayā śete bhagnayā plavagādhipaḥ
nirastahanukaḥ śete hanūmānrākṣasairhataḥ
O Sita, Sugriva lord of monkeys-has his neck broken; and, O Sita, with his jaw fractured, Hanuman has been slaughtered by the Raksasas.

जाम्बवानथ जानुभ्यामुत्पतन्निहतो युधि
पट्टसैर्बहुभिश्छिन्नो निकृत्तः पादपो यथा

jāmbavānatha jānubhyāmutpatannihato yudhi
paṭṭasairbahubhiśchinno nikṛttaḥ pādapo yathā
And Jambavan, endeavouring to spring up bearded darts, even as a tree cut off.

मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चोभौ निहतौ वानरर्षभौ
निःश्वसन्तौ रुदन्तौ च रुधिरेण समुक्षितौ

maindaśca dvividaścobhau nihatau vānararṣabhau
niḥśvasantau rudantau ca rudhireṇa samukṣitau
The stalwart Mainda and Dvivida-those foremost of monkeyssighing and lamenting, bathed in blood, destroyers of foes-were cut off with a sword.

नाराचैर्बहुभिश्छिन्नः शेते दर्यां दरीमुखः
कुमुदस्तु महातेजा निष्कूजन्सायकैर्हतः

nārācairbahubhiśchinnaḥ śete daryāṁ darīmukhaḥ
kumudastu mahātejā niṣkūjansāyakairhataḥ
Panasa is rolling on the earth like a (veritable) Panasa. And mangled by many iron arrows, Darimukha lies in a cave. And the exceedingly energetic Kumuda, dumb, is slain by shafts.

अङ्गदो बहुभिश्छिन्नः शरैरासाद्य राक्षसैः
पातितो रुधिरोद्गारी क्षितौ निपतितोऽङ्गदः

aṅgado bahubhiśchinnaḥ śarairāsādya rākṣasaiḥ
pātito rudhirodgārī kṣitau nipatito'ṅgadaḥ
And torn by innumerable (arrows) discharged on all sides by Raksasas. Angada, vomiting blood, Leith on the ground.

हरयो मथिता नागै रथजालैस्तथापरे
शायिता मृदितास्तत्र वायुवेगैरिवाम्बुदाः

harayo mathitā nāgai rathajālaistathāpare
śāyitā mṛditāstatra vāyuvegairivāmbudāḥ
The monkeys, hard pressed by elephants, and others by networks of cars, lie low in the field, having been agitated like clouds by winds.

प्रद्रुताश्च परे त्रस्ता हन्यमाना जघन्यतः
अभिद्रुतास्तु रक्षोभिः सिंहैरिव महाद्विपाः

pradrutāśca pare trastā hanyamānā jaghanyataḥ
abhidrutāstu rakṣobhiḥ siṁhairiva mahādvipāḥ
And others afflicted with affright, flee, attacked (by the enemy) in the rear, and followed by the Raksasas, like mighty elephants pursued by lions.

सागरे पतिताः केचित्केचिद्गगनमाश्रिताः
ऋक्षा वृक्षानुपारूढा वानरैस्तु विमिश्रिताः

sāgare patitāḥ kecitkecidgaganamāśritāḥ
ṛkṣā vṛkṣānupārūḍhā vānaraistu vimiśritāḥ
Some have fallen into the sea, and some have taken refuge in the sky; and the bears have mounted up trees along with the monkeys.

सागरस्य च तीरेषु शैलेषु च वनेषु च
पिङ्गाक्षास्ते विरूपाक्षैर्बहुभिर्बहवो हताः

sāgarasya ca tīreṣu śaileṣu ca vaneṣu ca
piṅgākṣāste virūpākṣairbahubhirbahavo hatāḥ
And on the shore of the sea, and in mountains and woods many are the tawny-hued monkeys that have been slain by Raksasas of frightful forms.

एवं तव हतो भर्ता ससैन्यो मम सेनया
क्षतजार्द्रं रजोध्वस्तमिदं चास्याहृतं शिरः

evaṁ tava hato bhartā sasainyo mama senayā
kṣatajārdraṁ rajodhvastamidaṁ cāsyāhṛtaṁ śiraḥ
Thus has your lord been slain by my forces, along with his army; and I have his head, washed in blood and besmeared with dust.

ततः परमदुर्धर्षो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
सीतायामुपशृण्वन्त्यां राक्षसीमिदमब्रवीत्

tataḥ paramadurdharṣo rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
sītāyāmupaśṛṇvantyāṁ rākṣasīmidamabravīt
Thereat, the exceedingly irrepressible lord of Raksasas, Ravana, spoke to a Raksasi, in the hearing of Sita.

राक्षसं क्रूरकर्माणं विद्युज्जिह्वं त्वमानय
येन तद्राघवशिरः संग्रामात्स्वयमाहृतम्

rākṣasaṁ krūrakarmāṇaṁ vidyujjihvaṁ tvamānaya
yena tadrāghavaśiraḥ saṁgrāmātsvayamāhṛtam
Bring (hither) the Raksasa, Vidyujjibha of cruel deeds, who has personally brought Raghava's head from the field.

विद्युज्जिह्वस्ततो गृह्य शिरस्तत्सशरासनम्
प्रणामं शिरसा कृत्वा रावणस्याग्रतः स्थितः

vidyujjihvastato gṛhya śirastatsaśarāsanam
praṇāmaṁ śirasā kṛtvā rāvaṇasyāgrataḥ sthitaḥ

Thereat, Vidyujjibha, taking the head along with the bow, bowing down the head (to Ravana), stood before him. Then spoke king Ravana to the Raksasa, Vidyujjibha of the long tongue, who was staying by.

अग्रतः कुरु सीतायाः शीघ्रं दाशरथेः शिरः
अवस्थां पश्चिमां भर्तुः कृपणा साधु पश्यतु

agrataḥ kuru sītāyāḥ śīghraṁ dāśaratheḥ śiraḥ
avasthāṁ paścimāṁ bhartuḥ kṛpaṇā sādhu paśyatu
Do you at once hold before Sita the head of Dasaratha's son. Let her clearly behold the ultimate sad plight of her lord.

एवमुक्तं तु तद्रक्षः शिरस्तत्प्रियदर्शनम्
उपनिक्षिप्य सीतायाः क्षिप्रमन्तरधीयत

evamuktaṁ tu tadrakṣaḥ śirastatpriyadarśanam
upanikṣipya sītāyāḥ kṣipramantaradhīyata
Thus addressed, that Raksasa, throwing that graceful head before Sita, swiftly vanished,

रावणश्चापि चिक्षेप भास्वरं कार्मुकं महत्
त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातं सीतामिदमुवाच ह

rāvaṇaścāpi cikṣepa bhāsvaraṁ kārmukaṁ mahat
triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātaṁ sītāmidamuvāca ha
Ravana cast down the mighty blazing bow, famed through the three worlds, saying.

इदं तत्तव रामस्य कार्मुकं ज्यासमन्वितम्
इह प्रहस्तेनानीतं हत्वा तं निशि मानुषम्

idaṁ tattava rāmasya kārmukaṁ jyāsamanvitam
iha prahastenānītaṁ hatvā taṁ niśi mānuṣam
This is Rama's. This is the bow of your Rama with the string fixed. Slaying that man over night, Prahasta brought it hither.

स विद्युज्जिह्वेन सहैव तच्छिरो; धनुश्च भूमौ विनिकीर्य रावणः
विदेहराजस्य सुतां यशस्विनीं; ततोऽब्रवीत्तां भव मे वशानुगा

sa vidyujjihvena sahaiva tacchiro; dhanuśca bhūmau vinikīrya rāvaṇaḥ
videharājasya sutāṁ yaśasvinīṁ; tato'bravīttāṁ bhava me vaśānugā
When Vidyujjibha placed the head of that man, Ravana poured the bow on earth. Then he spoke to illustrious Sita, the daughter of king Videha to submit to his desire.

सा सीता तच्छिरो दृष्ट्वा तच्च कार्मुकमुत्तमम्
सुग्रीवप्रतिसंसर्गमाख्यातं च हनूमता

sā sītā tacchiro dṛṣṭvā tacca kārmukamuttamam
sugrīvapratisaṁsargamākhyātaṁ ca hanūmatā

Seeing that head and that excellent bow, and (remembering) the union of (Rama) and Sugriva related by Hanuman, and (seeing) those eyes, and the complexion of that face, and that countenance like to that of her lord, and that hair and that forehead; and that beautiful jewel forming the crest; and recognizing (Rama) by all these tokens combined, (Sita), exceedingly aggrieved, rebuked Kaikeyi, lamenting like a female osprey.

सकामा भव कैकेयि हतोऽयं कुलनन्दनः
कुलमुत्सादितं सर्वं त्वया कलहशीलया

sakāmā bhava kaikeyi hato'yaṁ kulanandanaḥ
kulamutsāditaṁ sarvaṁ tvayā kalahaśīlayā
O Kaikeys, have your wishes attained. Slain has been the son of the race; and the entire race is exterminated by you, partial to dissension.

आर्येण किं नु कैकेय्याः कृतं रामेण विप्रियम्
यद्गृहाच्चीरवसनस्तया प्रस्थापितो वनम्

āryeṇa kiṁ nu kaikeyyāḥ kṛtaṁ rāmeṇa vipriyam
yadgṛhāccīravasanastayā prasthāpito vanam
What evil had been done to Kaikeyi by the revered Rama, that along with me, he had been banished into the woods, with rags given him (for his covering)?

एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेही वेपमाना तपस्विनी
जगाम जगतीं बाला छिन्ना तु कदली यथा

evamuktvā tu vaidehī vepamānā tapasvinī
jagāma jagatīṁ bālā chinnā tu kadalī yathā
Having said this, Vaidehi, forlorm and trembling (all over), dropped to the earth, like a plantain cut off.

सा मुहूर्तात्समाश्वस्य प्रतिलभ्य च चेतनाम्
तच्छिरः समुपाघ्राय विललापायतेक्षणा

sā muhūrtātsamāśvasya pratilabhya ca cetanām
tacchiraḥ samupāghrāya vilalāpāyatekṣaṇā
Then, recovering after a while, and having regained her consciousness, the large-eyed one, placing the head in her front, gave way to grief.

हा हतास्मि महाबाहो वीरव्रतमनुव्रता
इमां ते पश्चिमावस्थां गतास्मि विधवा कृता

hā hatāsmi mahābāho vīravratamanuvratā
imāṁ te paścimāvasthāṁ gatāsmi vidhavā kṛtā
Ah! I am undone, O mighty-armed one! ) you that did follow stern vows! From your (death), I have come by this final plight, having been rendered a widow.

प्रथमं मरणं नार्या भर्तुर्वैगुण्यमुच्यते
सुवृत्तः साधुवृत्तायाः संवृत्तस्त्वं ममाग्रतः

prathamaṁ maraṇaṁ nāryā bharturvaiguṇyamucyate
suvṛttaḥ sādhuvṛttāyāḥ saṁvṛttastvaṁ mamāgrataḥ

The greatest calamity (that can befall a woman), is said to be the death of her husband. And, possessor of an excellent character, you have departed before me, who have ever trod the path of the righteous; but who have come by a mighty grief and am plunged in a sea of sorrow.

सा श्वश्रूर्मम कौसल्या त्वया पुत्रेण राघव
वत्सेनेव यथा धेनुर्विवत्सा वत्सला कृता

sā śvaśrūrmama kausalyā tvayā putreṇa rāghava
vatseneva yathā dhenurvivatsā vatsalā kṛtā

And you, who was engaged in delivering me, have yourself fallen! And my mother-in-law, Kausalya, attached (to you), through the death of you, her son, at the hands of Raksasas, has been reduced to the condition of a cow that has been deprived of her calf.

आदिष्टं दीर्घमायुस्ते यैरचिन्त्यपराक्रम
अनृतं वचनं तेषामल्पायुरसि राघव

ādiṣṭaṁ dīrghamāyuste yairacintyaparākrama
anṛtaṁ vacanaṁ teṣāmalpāyurasi rāghava
O Raghava, even the astrologers had predicted long life for you. But their words are false, you, O Raghava, wast short-lived. me

अथ वा नश्यति प्रज्ञा प्राज्ञस्यापि सतस्तव
पचत्येनं तथा कालो भूतानां प्रभवो ह्ययम्

atha vā naśyati prajñā prājñasyāpi satastava
pacatyenaṁ tathā kālo bhūtānāṁ prabhavo hyayam
Or did your wisdom, wise and good as you were, come to naught? For God, who is the origin of all beings, make (every one) reap the fruit of his own acts.

अदृष्टं मृत्युमापन्नः कस्मात्त्वं नयशास्त्रवित्
व्यसनानामुपायज्ञः कुशलो ह्यसि वर्जने

adṛṣṭaṁ mṛtyumāpannaḥ kasmāttvaṁ nayaśāstravit
vyasanānāmupāyajñaḥ kuśalo hyasi varjane
And why, versed in polity as you wast, did you come by death, unforeseen? You were acquainted with the means of warding off misfortune, and skilled in doing so.

उपशेषे महाबाहो मां विहाय तपस्विनीम्
प्रियामिव शुभां नारीं पृथिवीं पुरुषर्षभ

upaśeṣe mahābāho māṁ vihāya tapasvinīm
priyāmiva śubhāṁ nārīṁ pṛthivīṁ puruṣarṣabha

Having been brought hither by representing the Fatal Night, fierce and fell, after (being) embraced, and by force, the lotus-eyed one has met with his death. Here lie you, O longarmed one, leaving me lone, and embracing the Earth like your beloved fair.

अर्चितं सततं यत्नाद्गन्धमाल्यैर्मया तव
इदं ते मत्प्रियं वीर धनुः काञ्चनभूषितम्

arcitaṁ satataṁ yatnādgandhamālyairmayā tava
idaṁ te matpriyaṁ vīra dhanuḥ kāñcanabhūṣitam
Ever carefully worshipped with perfumed wreaths, this bow of your, O hero, embellished with gold, is dear to me.

पित्रा दशरथेन त्वं श्वशुरेण ममानघ
पूर्वैश्च पितृभिः सार्धं नूनं स्वर्गे समागतः

pitrā daśarathena tvaṁ śvaśureṇa mamānagha
pūrvaiśca pitṛbhiḥ sārdhaṁ nūnaṁ svarge samāgataḥ
O sinless one, you have surely gone to heaven, and (are there) in the company of your sire and my father-in-law, Dasaratha, and all your ancestors.

दिवि नक्षत्रभूतस्त्वं महत्कर्म कृतं प्रियम्
पुण्यं राजर्षिवंशं त्वमात्मनः समुपेक्षसे

divi nakṣatrabhūtastvaṁ mahatkarma kṛtaṁ priyam
puṇyaṁ rājarṣivaṁśaṁ tvamātmanaḥ samupekṣase
You have become a star of the firmament as the fruit of your great act.* You have disregarded your righteous race of Rajarsis. *The carrying out the command of your sire.

किं मान्न प्रेक्षसे राजन्किं मां न प्रतिभाषसे
बालां बालेन संप्राप्तां भार्यां मां सहचारिणीम्

kiṁ mānna prekṣase rājankiṁ māṁ na pratibhāṣase
bālāṁ bālena saṁprāptāṁ bhāryāṁ māṁ sahacāriṇīm
O king, why do you not look at me? And why is it that you do not answer me, who am a girl, hardly arrived at youth, and who am your wife and companion?

संश्रुतं गृह्णता पाणिं चरिष्यामीति यत्त्वया
स्मर तन्मम काकुत्स्थ नय मामपि दुःखिताम्

saṁśrutaṁ gṛhṇatā pāṇiṁ cariṣyāmīti yattvayā
smara tanmama kākutstha naya māmapi duḥkhitām
That you at the time of your espousing my hand had vowed, I will practise (righteousness) with you, do you, O Kakutstha, recollect the same, and take me, who am overwhelmed with distrees.

कस्मान्मामपहाय त्वं गतो गतिमतां वर
अस्माल्लोकादमुं लोकं त्यक्त्वा मामिह दुःखिताम्

kasmānmāmapahāya tvaṁ gato gatimatāṁ vara
asmāllokādamuṁ lokaṁ tyaktvā māmiha duḥkhitām
Why, O best of goers, have you gone from this world to that other, leaving behind me, overwhelmed with distress?

कल्याणैरुचितं यत्तत्परिष्वक्तं मयैव तु
क्रव्यादैस्तच्छरीरं ते नूनं विपरिकृष्यते

kalyāṇairucitaṁ yattatpariṣvaktaṁ mayaiva tu
kravyādaistaccharīraṁ te nūnaṁ viparikṛṣyate
That person of your which, decked out with auspicious things, I used to embrace, beasts of prey will for certain tear the same.

अग्निष्टोमादिभिर्यज्ञैरिष्टवानाप्तदक्षिणैः
अग्निहोत्रेण संस्कारं केन त्वं तु न लप्स्यसे

agniṣṭomādibhiryajñairiṣṭavānāptadakṣiṇaiḥ
agnihotreṇa saṁskāraṁ kena tvaṁ tu na lapsyase
Having performed the Agnishtoma and other sacrifices with Daksinas (dispensed, why had not you attained purity by means of the sacrificial fire?

प्रव्रज्यामुपपन्नानां त्रयाणामेकमागतम्
परिप्रक्ष्यति कौसल्या लक्ष्मणं शोकलालसा

pravrajyāmupapannānāṁ trayāṇāmekamāgatam
pariprakṣyati kausalyā lakṣmaṇaṁ śokalālasā
Kaucalya, over-whelmed with sorrow, shall only behold one of the three that had gone away to distant lands, come (back)-Laksmana.

स तस्याः परिपृच्छन्त्या वधं मित्रबलस्य ते
तव चाख्यास्यते नूनं निशायां राक्षसैर्वधम्

sa tasyāḥ paripṛcchantyā vadhaṁ mitrabalasya te
tava cākhyāsyate nūnaṁ niśāyāṁ rākṣasairvadham
On being asked by her, he shall relate your as well as the deaths of your friend's troops over night at the hands of the Raksasas.

सा त्वां सुप्तं हतं श्रुत्वा मां च रक्षोगृहं गताम्
हृदयेन विदीर्णेन न भविष्यति राघव

sā tvāṁ suptaṁ hataṁ śrutvā māṁ ca rakṣogṛhaṁ gatām
hṛdayena vidīrṇena na bhaviṣyati rāghava
O Raghava, hearing you slain while asleep, and me staying in the abode of the Raksasa, she with her heart cleft (in twain), shall cease to exist.

साधु पातय मां क्षिप्रं रामस्योपरि रावणः
समानय पतिं पत्न्या कुरु कल्याणमुत्तमम्

sādhu pātaya māṁ kṣipraṁ rāmasyopari rāvaṇaḥ
samānaya patiṁ patnyā kuru kalyāṇamuttamam
Do you, O Ravana, speedily slay me upon Rama; and, bringing the wife to the husband, compass my best benefit.

शिरसा मे शिरश्चास्य कायं कायेन योजय
रावणानुगमिष्यामि गतिं भर्तुर्महात्मनः
मुहूर्तमपि नेच्छामि जीवितुं पापजीविना

śirasā me śiraścāsya kāyaṁ kāyena yojaya
rāvaṇānugamiṣyāmi gatiṁ bharturmahātmanaḥ
muhūrtamapi necchāmi jīvituṁ pāpajīvinā
Do you join my head to his and my body to his body. I will, O Ravana, follow the way of my high-souled lord.

इति सा दुःखसंतप्ता विललापायतेक्षणा
भर्तुः शिरो धनुस्तत्र समीक्ष्य जनकात्मजा

iti sā duḥkhasaṁtaptā vilalāpāyatekṣaṇā
bhartuḥ śiro dhanustatra samīkṣya janakātmajā
Thus, burning in grief, did that large-eyed one indulge in lamentations; and Janaka's daughter kept fast gazing at the head and bow of her lord.

एवं लालप्यमानायां सीतायां तत्र राक्षसः
अभिचक्राम भर्तारमनीकस्थः कृताञ्जलिः

evaṁ lālapyamānāyāṁ sītāyāṁ tatra rākṣasaḥ
abhicakrāma bhartāramanīkasthaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ
As the Raksasa was by while Sita was thus bewailing, there appeared before his lord, with joined hands, the warder, saying.

विजयस्वार्यपुत्रेति सोऽभिवाद्य प्रसाद्य च
न्यवेदयदनुप्राप्तं प्रहस्तं वाहिनीपतिम्

vijayasvāryaputreti so'bhivādya prasādya ca
nyavedayadanuprāptaṁ prahastaṁ vāhinīpatim
May the worshipful one be victorious! And saluting and propitiating him, (Ravana), he told him that Prahasta, general of the forces, had arrived.

अमात्यैः सहितः सर्वैः प्रहस्तः समुपस्थितः
किंचिदात्ययिकं कार्यं तेषां त्वं दर्शनं कुरु

amātyaiḥ sahitaḥ sarvaiḥ prahastaḥ samupasthitaḥ
kiṁcidātyayikaṁ kāryaṁ teṣāṁ tvaṁ darśanaṁ kuru
Prahasta has come to you, surrounded by all the courtiers. And, O lord, I was despatched by him, desirous of seeing you.

एतच्छ्रुत्वा दशग्रीवो राक्षसप्रतिवेदितम्
अशोकवनिकां त्यक्त्वा मन्त्रिणां दर्शनं ययौ

etacchrutvā daśagrīvo rākṣasaprativeditam
aśokavanikāṁ tyaktvā mantriṇāṁ darśanaṁ yayau
Hearing these words of the Raksasa, the Tennecked one, leaving the Asoka wood, went to see the counsellors.

स तु सर्वं समर्थ्यैव मन्त्रिभिः कृत्यमात्मनः
सभां प्रविश्य विदधे विदित्वा रामविक्रमम्

sa tu sarvaṁ samarthyaiva mantribhiḥ kṛtyamātmanaḥ
sabhāṁ praviśya vidadhe viditvā rāmavikramam
Having decided his entire course of action in consultation with his competent advisers, (Ravana), entering his court, well knowing Rama's prowess, set about his work.

राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तैः सार्धं मन्त्रिभिर्भीमविक्रमैः
समर्थयामास तदा रामकार्यविनिश्चयम्

rākṣasendrastu taiḥ sārdhaṁ mantribhirbhīmavikramaiḥ
samarthayāmāsa tadā rāmakāryaviniścayam
As soon as Ravana left that place, that head and that bow vanished. And in company with the councillors of dreadful power, (Ravana) decided his course with reference to Rama.

अविदूरस्थितान्सर्वान्बलाध्यक्षान्हितैषिणः
अब्रवीत्कालसदृशो रावणो राक्षसाधिपः

avidūrasthitānsarvānbalādhyakṣānhitaiṣiṇaḥ
abravītkālasadṛśo rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
Then the lord of Raksasas, Ravana, resembling the day of doom, addressed his generals, all well-wishers-staying hard by, saying.

शीघ्रं भेरीनिनादेन स्फुटकोणाहतेन मे
समानयध्वं सैन्यानि वक्तव्यं च न कारणम्

śīghraṁ bherīninādena sphuṭakoṇāhatena me
samānayadhvaṁ sainyāni vaktavyaṁ ca na kāraṇam
Do you speedily summon my forces with the beat of drums—not do you give out the reason (of the summons).

ततस्तथेति प्रतिगृह्य तद्वचो; बलाधिपास्ते महदात्मनो बलम्
समानयंश्चैव समागतं च ते; न्यवेदयन्भर्तरि युद्धकाङ्क्षिणि

tatastatheti pratigṛhya tadvaco; balādhipāste mahadātmano balam
samānayaṁścaiva samāgataṁ ca te; nyavedayanbhartari yuddhakāṅkṣiṇi
Then assenting to his speech with So be it, the envoys immediately summoned that mighty force; and, when in had arrived, they informed their master, eager for conflict, of its arrival.

सीतां तु मोहितां दृष्ट्वा सरमा नाम राक्षसी
आससादाशु वैदेहीं प्रियां प्रणयिनी सखी

sītāṁ tu mohitāṁ dṛṣṭvā saramā nāma rākṣasī
āsasādāśu vaidehīṁ priyāṁ praṇayinī sakhī
Seeing Sita overwhelmed with grief, a Raksasi, named Sarama, who was the beloved companion (of Sita), drew near to his dear (friend), Vaidehi.

सा हि तत्र कृता मित्रं सीतया रक्ष्यमाणया
रक्षन्ती रावणादिष्टा सानुक्रोशा दृढव्रता

sā hi tatra kṛtā mitraṁ sītayā rakṣyamāṇayā
rakṣantī rāvaṇādiṣṭā sānukrośā dṛḍhavratā

Sita, who was protected there (by Sarama), had been made a friend by her. And, protecting her at the command of Ravana, that kind-hearted companion, firm in vows, saw Sita, deprived of her consciousness. And she' comforted with a friend's affection that one of fair vows, who was rolling in the dust and rising up from it like a mare. 1. Sarama. 2. The commentator intelligently remarks. As a mare does, to remove fatigue.

तां समाश्वासयामास सखी स्नेहेन सुव्रता
उक्ता यद्रावणेन त्वं प्रत्युक्तं च स्वयं त्वया

tāṁ samāśvāsayāmāsa sakhī snehena suvratā
uktā yadrāvaṇena tvaṁ pratyuktaṁ ca svayaṁ tvayā

Having come to the solitary wood for protecting you, I, renouncing all fear of Ravana, have, remaining hid, heard everything that he addressed to you, as well as what you had replied to him. For you, O you of expansive eyes, I have no fear of Ravana.

स संभ्रान्तश्च निष्क्रान्तो यत्कृते राक्षसाधिपः
तच्च मे विदितं सर्वमभिनिष्क्रम्य मैथिलि

sa saṁbhrāntaśca niṣkrānto yatkṛte rākṣasādhipaḥ
tacca me viditaṁ sarvamabhiniṣkramya maithili
And, O Maithili, I, coming out, have also learnt well as to why the lord of Raksasas has gone out hence hurriedly.

न शक्यं सौप्तिकं कर्तुं रामस्य विदितात्मनः
वधश्च पुरुषव्याघ्रे तस्मिन्नेवोपपद्यते

na śakyaṁ sauptikaṁ kartuṁ rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
vadhaśca puruṣavyāghre tasminnevopapadyate
Rama, acquainted with self, is incapable of being surprised in sleep; nor does the slaying of that tiger-like one commend itself to me as probable.

न चैव वानरा हन्तुं शक्याः पादपयोधिनः
सुरा देवर्षभेणेव रामेण हि सुरक्षिताः

na caiva vānarā hantuṁ śakyāḥ pādapayodhinaḥ
surā devarṣabheṇeva rāmeṇa hi surakṣitāḥ
The monkeys fighting with trees, well protected by Raghava, like the gods protected by the foremost of the celestials, are incapable of being slain.

विक्रान्तो रक्षिता नित्यमात्मनश्च परस्य च
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा कुशली नयशास्त्रवित्

vikrānto rakṣitā nityamātmanaśca parasya ca
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā kuśalī nayaśāstravit

And, possessed of arms long and rounded; graceful, broad-breasted; powerful; accoutred with the bow; and mailed; righteous; and famous over the earth; endowed with energy; and along with his brother, Laksmana, ever protecting himself and others; of noble descent; and versed in polity; the destroyer of the hostile ranks; and of inconceivable strength and manhood, the graceful Raghava, O Sita, slayer of foes, is not slain.

अयुक्तबुद्धिकृत्येन सर्वभूतविरोधिना
इयं प्रयुक्ता रौद्रेण माया मायाविदा त्वयि

ayuktabuddhikṛtyena sarvabhūtavirodhinā
iyaṁ prayuktā raudreṇa māyā māyāvidā tvayi
This illusion has been spread around you by that fierce, illusion-creating one, whose mind over runs upon improper acts and who oppose himself to all creatures.

शोकस्ते विगतः सर्वः कल्याणं त्वामुपस्थितम्
ध्रुवं त्वां भजते लक्ष्मीः प्रियं प्रीतिकरं शृणु

śokaste vigataḥ sarvaḥ kalyāṇaṁ tvāmupasthitam
dhruvaṁ tvāṁ bhajate lakṣmīḥ priyaṁ prītikaraṁ śṛṇu
All your sorrow has departed, and your good day has dawned. Certainly Laksmi seek you. And, O lady, hearken to what is dear to you!

उत्तीर्य सागरं रामः सह वानरसेनया
संनिविष्टः समुद्रस्य तीरमासाद्य दक्षिणम्

uttīrya sāgaraṁ rāmaḥ saha vānarasenayā
saṁniviṣṭaḥ samudrasya tīramāsādya dakṣiṇam
Having crossed over the ocean, along with the monkey-host, Rama has encamped himself on the southern shore of the sea.

दृष्टो मे परिपूर्णार्थः काकुत्स्थः सहलक्ष्मणः
सहितैः सागरान्तस्थैर्बलैस्तिष्ठति रक्षितः

dṛṣṭo me paripūrṇārthaḥ kākutsthaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
sahitaiḥ sāgarāntasthairbalaistiṣṭhati rakṣitaḥ
By me has been seen the complete Kakutstha along with Laksmana, accompanied by the forces, stationed on the marge of the main, protected (by his native might).

अनेन प्रेषिता ये च राक्षसा लघुविक्रमः
राघवस्तीर्ण इत्येवं प्रवृत्तिस्तैरिहाहृता

anena preṣitā ye ca rākṣasā laghuvikramaḥ
rāghavastīrṇa ityevaṁ pravṛttistairihāhṛtā
Those Raksasas of fleet vigour who had been despatched by this one, have brought the news that Raghava has crossed.

स तां श्रुत्वा विशालाक्षि प्रवृत्तिं राक्षसाधिपः
एष मन्त्रयते सर्वैः सचिवैः सह रावणः

sa tāṁ śrutvā viśālākṣi pravṛttiṁ rākṣasādhipaḥ
eṣa mantrayate sarvaiḥ sacivaiḥ saha rāvaṇaḥ
And, O large-eyed lady, having learnt this news, Ravana-lord of Raksasas, is consulting with all his counsellors.

इति ब्रुवाणा सरमा राक्षसी सीतया सह
सर्वोद्योगेन सैन्यानां शब्दं शुश्राव भैरवम्

iti bruvāṇā saramā rākṣasī sītayā saha
sarvodyogena sainyānāṁ śabdaṁ śuśrāva bhairavam
As the Raksasi, Sarama, was relating this to Sita, she heard the leonine roars of the army, emitted with the greatest energy.

दण्डनिर्घातवादिन्याः श्रुत्वा भेर्या महास्वनम्
उवाच सरमा सीतामिदं मधुरभाषिणी

daṇḍanirghātavādinyāḥ śrutvā bheryā mahāsvanam
uvāca saramā sītāmidaṁ madhurabhāṣiṇī
Hearing the mighty sounds of kettledrums produced by sticks struck (thereon), the honeytongued Sarama spoke thus to Sita.

संनाहजननी ह्येषा भैरवा भीरु भेरिका
भेरीनादं च गम्भीरं शृणु तोयदनिस्वनम्

saṁnāhajananī hyeṣā bhairavā bhīru bherikā
bherīnādaṁ ca gambhīraṁ śṛṇu toyadanisvanam
These dreadful sounds of the kettledrum, O mother, call to arms. And hark to the solemn notes of the kettledrums, resembling the rumbling of clouds!

कल्प्यन्ते मत्तमातंगा युज्यन्ते रथवाजिनः
तत्र तत्र च संनद्धाः संपतन्ति पदातयः

kalpyante mattamātaṁgā yujyante rathavājinaḥ
tatra tatra ca saṁnaddhāḥ saṁpatanti padātayaḥ
The mad elephants are caparisoned and the car-horses are yoked; and thousands of warriors) are seen, mounted on steeds, with bearded darts in their hands.

आपूर्यन्ते राजमार्गाः सैन्यैरद्भुतदर्शनैः
वेगवद्भिर्नदद्भिश्च तोयौघैरिव सागरः

āpūryante rājamārgāḥ sainyairadbhutadarśanaiḥ
vegavadbhirnadadbhiśca toyaughairiva sāgaraḥ
As waters fill up the ocean, mailed warriors of wonderful forms, vehement and roaring, by thousands rush out on all aides and fill the highways.

शास्त्राणां च प्रसन्नानां चर्मणां वर्मणां तथा
रथवाजिगजानां च भूषितानां च रक्षसाम्

śāstrāṇāṁ ca prasannānāṁ carmaṇāṁ varmaṇāṁ tathā
rathavājigajānāṁ ca bhūṣitānāṁ ca rakṣasām

And mark the splendour spread around by the polished arins and bucklers and mail, and by the cars, horses and elephants of the followers of the Raksasa-chief, consisting of many hues shooting up, like to the appearance of a fire in summer, burning a forest, and also mark the excitement of the high-spirited and fast-coursing Raksasa! * *This line of verse defies all attempts to make it fall into syntactical order with the rest of the sentence. It is a hideous hiatus in the passage.

श्रीस्त्वां भजति शोकघ्नी रक्षसां भयमागतम्
रामात्कमलपत्राक्षि दैत्यानामिव वासवात्

śrīstvāṁ bhajati śokaghnī rakṣasāṁ bhayamāgatam
rāmātkamalapatrākṣi daityānāmiva vāsavāt

And fierce is the excitement of these Raksasas— followers of the Raksasa-cheif, with their hands bearing upraised arms, capable of making people's hair stand on end. The sorrow removing Sree espouse you, and the fear of the Raksasa is come.

अवजित्य जितक्रोधस्तमचिन्त्यपराक्रमः
रावणं समरे हत्वा भर्ता त्वाधिगमिष्यति

avajitya jitakrodhastamacintyaparākramaḥ
rāvaṇaṁ samare hatvā bhartā tvādhigamiṣyati
As Vasava did to the Daityas, the lotus-eyed Rama, your lord-of controlled anger, and of inconceivable prowess, slaying Ravana in battle and thus delivering you, shall approach you.

विक्रमिष्यति रक्षःसु भर्ता ते सहलक्ष्मणः
यथा शत्रुषु शत्रुघ्नो विष्णुना सह वासवः

vikramiṣyati rakṣaḥsu bhartā te sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
yathā śatruṣu śatrughno viṣṇunā saha vāsavaḥ
And, as Vasava put forth his prowess among his foes, in company with the foe-destroying Visnu, your lord, along with Laksmana, shall display his prowess among the Raksasa.

आगतस्य हि रामस्य क्षिप्रमङ्कगतां सतीम्
अहं द्रक्ष्यामि सिद्धार्थां त्वां शत्रौ विनिपातिते

āgatasya hi rāmasya kṣipramaṅkagatāṁ satīm
ahaṁ drakṣyāmi siddhārthāṁ tvāṁ śatrau vinipātite
On the enemy having fallen, I shall behold you, devoted to your lord, with your desire attained, soon lying on the lap of Rama.

अश्रूण्यानन्दजानि त्वं वर्तयिष्यसि शोभने
समागम्य परिष्वक्ता तस्योरसि महोरसः

aśrūṇyānandajāni tvaṁ vartayiṣyasi śobhane
samāgamya pariṣvaktā tasyorasi mahorasaḥ
And, O Janaki, embracing (your lord) you shall shed tears of joy on his mighty breast.

अचिरान्मोक्ष्यते सीते देवि ते जघनं गताम्
धृतामेतां बहून्मासान्वेणीं रामो महाबलः

acirānmokṣyate sīte devi te jaghanaṁ gatām
dhṛtāmetāṁ bahūnmāsānveṇīṁ rāmo mahābalaḥ
O Sita, soon shall the highly powerful Rama loosen this braid of your reaching to your hips, which you have been wearing for many a month.

तस्य दृष्ट्वा मुखं देवि पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम्
मोक्ष्यसे शोकजं वारि निर्मोकमिव पन्नगी

tasya dṛṣṭvā mukhaṁ devi pūrṇacandramivoditam
mokṣyase śokajaṁ vāri nirmokamiva pannagī
O exalted one, seeing his face like the full moon risen, you shall shed water begot of ruth, even as a she-serpent casts off her slough.

रावणं समरे हत्वा नचिरादेव मैथिलि
त्वया समग्रं प्रियया सुखार्हो लप्स्यते सुखम्

rāvaṇaṁ samare hatvā nacirādeva maithili
tvayā samagraṁ priyayā sukhārho lapsyate sukham
O Mithila's daughter, speedily slaying Ravana in battle, that one worthy of happiness shall reap felicity in the company of you, his beloved.

समागता त्वं रामेण मोदिष्यसि महात्मना
सुवर्षेण समायुक्ता यथा सस्येन मेदिनी

samāgatā tvaṁ rāmeṇa modiṣyasi mahātmanā
suvarṣeṇa samāyuktā yathā sasyena medinī
And, loved by the high-souled Rama, you, shall be happy, even as the Earth furnished with crops brought forth by plenteous showers.

गिरिवरमभितोऽनुवर्तमानो; हय इव मण्डलमाशु यः करोति
तमिह शरणमभ्युपेहि देवि; दिवसकरं प्रभवो ह्ययं प्रजानाम्

girivaramabhito'nuvartamāno; haya iva maṇḍalamāśu yaḥ karoti
tamiha śaraṇamabhyupehi devi; divasakaraṁ prabhavo hyayaṁ prajānām

Do you, O exalted one, take refuge with him, who, going round the foremost of mountains, speedily assume a steed-like circular movement; for even the maker of day is the source of people's joy and grief.

अथ तां जातसंतापां तेन वाक्येन मोहिताम्
सरमा ह्लादयामास पृतिवीं द्यौरिवाम्भसा

atha tāṁ jātasaṁtāpāṁ tena vākyena mohitām
saramā hlādayāmāsa pṛtivīṁ dyaurivāmbhasā
Burning with grief on account of those words,* Sarama gladdened and cheered her, even as masses of clouds (cheer up) the burning Earth. *i.e.the words of Ravana.

ततस्तस्या हितं सख्याश्चिकीर्षन्ती सखी वचः
उवाच काले कालज्ञा स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिणी

tatastasyā hitaṁ sakhyāścikīrṣantī sakhī vacaḥ
uvāca kāle kālajñā smitapūrvābhibhāṣiṇī
Then, desirous of doing her good, (Sita's) friend, conversant with season, and ever precluding her speech with a smile, spoke to her seasonably.

उत्सहेयमहं गत्वा त्वद्वाक्यमसितेक्षणे
निवेद्य कुशलं रामे प्रतिच्छन्ना निवर्तितुम्

utsaheyamahaṁ gatvā tvadvākyamasitekṣaṇe
nivedya kuśalaṁ rāme praticchannā nivartitum
O you having dark eyes, I can, secretly going to Rama and communicating to him your auspicious words, come back clandestinely.

न हि मे क्रममाणाया निरालम्बे विहायसि
समर्थो गतिमन्वेतुं पवनो गरुडोऽपि वा

na hi me kramamāṇāyā nirālambe vihāyasi
samartho gatimanvetuṁ pavano garuḍo'pi vā
Nor, when I course the supportless sky, can even the Wind or Garuda follow me.

एवं ब्रुवाणां तां सीता सरमां पुनरब्रवीत्
मधुरं श्लक्ष्णया वाचा पूर्वशोकाभिपन्नया

evaṁ bruvāṇāṁ tāṁ sītā saramāṁ punarabravīt
madhuraṁ ślakṣṇayā vācā pūrvaśokābhipannayā
As she said this, Sita with her grief a little lightened, said to Sarama in sweet and smooth words.

समर्था गगनं गन्तुमपि वा त्वं रसातलम्
अवगच्छाम्यकर्तव्यं कर्तव्यं ते मदन्तरे

samarthā gaganaṁ gantumapi vā tvaṁ rasātalam
avagacchāmyakartavyaṁ kartavyaṁ te madantare
You are capable of even going to the nethermost regions. But do you on my behalf that which is fit to be done by you.

मत्प्रियं यदि कर्तव्यं यदि बुद्धिः स्थिरा तव
ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तं गत्वा किं करोतीति रावणः

matpriyaṁ yadi kartavyaṁ yadi buddhiḥ sthirā tava
jñātumicchāmi taṁ gatvā kiṁ karotīti rāvaṇaḥ
If you intend doing me a good turn, and if your sense be steady, I would know what Ravana is doing after having left this place.

स हि मायाबलः क्रूरो रावणः शत्रुरावणः
मां मोहयति दुष्टात्मा पीतमात्रेव वारुणी

sa hi māyābalaḥ krūro rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ
māṁ mohayati duṣṭātmā pītamātreva vāruṇī
That guileful and wicked-minded one, Ravana, destroyer of enemies, having powers of illusion, overwhelms me even as the Varuni just drunk.

तर्जापयति मां नित्यं भर्त्सापयति चासकृत्
राक्षसीभिः सुघोराभिर्या मां रक्षन्ति नित्यशः

tarjāpayati māṁ nityaṁ bhartsāpayati cāsakṛt
rākṣasībhiḥ sughorābhiryā māṁ rakṣanti nityaśaḥ
Confining me here for ever and a day, (Ravana) sets on dreadful Raksnasas to alike threaten and scold me constantly.

उद्विग्ना शङ्किता चास्मि न च स्वस्थं मनो मम
तद्भयाच्चाहमुद्विग्ना अशोकवनिकां गताः

udvignā śaṅkitā cāsmi na ca svasthaṁ mano mama
tadbhayāccāhamudvignā aśokavanikāṁ gatāḥ
And I am agitated and alarmed and my mind is (always) uneasy. And I, dwelling in the Asoka wood, is ever agitated.

यदि नाम कथा तस्य निश्चितं वापि यद्भवेत्
निवेदयेथाः सर्वं तत्परो मे स्यादनुग्रहः

yadi nāma kathā tasya niścitaṁ vāpi yadbhavet
nivedayethāḥ sarvaṁ tatparo me syādanugrahaḥ
If there is any talk (of delivering me), or keeping me confined, you should communicate to me the decision arrived at.

सा त्वेवं ब्रुवतीं सीतां सरमा वल्गुभाषिणी
उवाच वचनं तस्याः स्पृशन्ती बाष्पविक्लवम्

sā tvevaṁ bruvatīṁ sītāṁ saramā valgubhāṣiṇī
uvāca vacanaṁ tasyāḥ spṛśantī bāṣpaviklavam
This is the highest favour that I seek (at hands). Thereat, the mild-speeched Sarama, wiping (Sita's) face washed in tears, spoke to her, as she said this.

एष ते यद्यभिप्रायस्तस्माद्गच्छामि जानकि
गृह्य शत्रोरभिप्रायमुपावृत्तां च पश्य माम्

eṣa te yadyabhiprāyastasmādgacchāmi jānaki
gṛhya śatrorabhiprāyamupāvṛttāṁ ca paśya mām
If this is your wish, I will go, O Janaki. O Mithila's daughter, having possessed myself of the intent of the enemy, I shall come back.

एवमुक्त्वा ततो गत्वा समीपं तस्य रक्षसः
शुश्राव कथितं तस्य रावणस्य समन्त्रिणः

evamuktvā tato gatvā samīpaṁ tasya rakṣasaḥ
śuśrāva kathitaṁ tasya rāvaṇasya samantriṇaḥ
Having said this, (Sarama), repairing to the Raksasa, heard Raksa, heard Ravana's converse with his counsellors.

सा श्रुत्वा निश्चयं तस्य निश्चयज्ञा दुरात्मनः
पुनरेवागमत्क्षिप्रमशोकवनिकां तदा

sā śrutvā niścayaṁ tasya niścayajñā durātmanaḥ
punarevāgamatkṣipramaśokavanikāṁ tadā
Having heard of the decision of that wickedminded one, she, understanding decisions, swiftly retraced her steps to the fair Asoka forest.

सा प्रविष्टा पुनस्तत्र ददर्श जनकात्मजाम्
प्रतीक्षमाणां स्वामेव भ्रष्टपद्मामिव श्रियम्

sā praviṣṭā punastatra dadarśa janakātmajām
pratīkṣamāṇāṁ svāmeva bhraṣṭapadmāmiva śriyam
Then, entering there, she saw Janaka's daughter, expecting (her) like a very Sri,, bereft of her lotus.

तां तु सीता पुनः प्राप्तां सरमां वल्गुभाषिणीम्
परिष्वज्य च सुस्निग्धं ददौ च स्वयमासनम्

tāṁ tu sītā punaḥ prāptāṁ saramāṁ valgubhāṣiṇīm
pariṣvajya ca susnigdhaṁ dadau ca svayamāsanam
And, the fair-spoken Sarama, on getting back (near her), Sita, embracing her affectionately, herself gave her a seat.

इहासीना सुखं सर्वमाख्याहि मम तत्त्वतः
क्रूरस्य निश्चयं तस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः

ihāsīnā sukhaṁ sarvamākhyāhi mama tattvataḥ
krūrasya niścayaṁ tasya rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
Sitting down here at ease, do you relate to me faithfully all about the determination of the wicked-minded and guileful Ravana.

एवमुक्ता तु सरमा सीतया वेपमानया
कथितं सर्वमाचष्ट रावणस्य समन्त्रिणः

evamuktā tu saramā sītayā vepamānayā
kathitaṁ sarvamācaṣṭa rāvaṇasya samantriṇaḥ
Thus accosted by the trembling Sita, Sarama related everything that had been said by Ravana and his counsellors.

जनन्या राक्षसेन्द्रो वै त्वन्मोक्षार्थं बृहद्वचः
अविद्धेन च वैदेहि मन्त्रिवृद्धेन बोधितः

jananyā rākṣasendro vai tvanmokṣārthaṁ bṛhadvacaḥ
aviddhena ca vaidehi mantrivṛddhena bodhitaḥ
O Vaidehi, the Raksasa lord was advised by his mother and the aged counsellors in pregnant words informed with affection, having your deliverance for their object.

दीयतामभिसत्कृत्य मनुजेन्द्राय मैथिली
निदर्शनं ते पर्याप्तं जनस्थाने यदद्भुतम्

dīyatāmabhisatkṛtya manujendrāya maithilī
nidarśanaṁ te paryāptaṁ janasthāne yadadbhutam
Do you make over Maithili to the king of men, paying him homage due. You have in Janasthana profusely witnessed wonderful instances (of his prowess).

लङ्घनं च समुद्रस्य दर्शनं च हनूमतः
वधं च रक्षसां युद्धे कः कुर्यान्मानुषो भुवि

laṅghanaṁ ca samudrasya darśanaṁ ca hanūmataḥ
vadhaṁ ca rakṣasāṁ yuddhe kaḥ kuryānmānuṣo bhuvi
The crossing of the ocean, Hanuman's sight (of Sita) and the slaughter of the Raksasa in fight, what person is capable of doing all this in battle?

एवं स मन्त्रिवृद्धैश्च मात्रा च बहु भाषितः
न त्वामुत्सहते मोक्तुमर्तह्मर्थपरो यथा

evaṁ sa mantrivṛddhaiśca mātrā ca bahu bhāṣitaḥ
na tvāmutsahate moktumartahmarthaparo yathā
Thus long exhorted by his counsellors as well as his mother, Ravana does not make up his mind to emancipate you, even as a covetous person is loath to pare with wealth (appropriated).

तदेषा सुस्थिरा बुद्धिर्मृत्युलोभादुपस्थिता
भयान्न शक्तस्त्वां मोक्तुमनिरस्तस्तु संयुगे
राक्षसानां च सर्वेषामात्मनश्च वधेन हि

tadeṣā susthirā buddhirmṛtyulobhādupasthitā
bhayānna śaktastvāṁ moktumanirastastu saṁyuge
rākṣasānāṁ ca sarveṣāmātmanaśca vadhena hi

O Maithili, without renouncing his life in battle, he does not intend to liberate you. Even this is the determination which that cruel one has arrived at along with his advisers. This intent is in consequence of their coveting surcease. He can not yield you up from sheer fear; not is he backward in battle, or shirk his own destruction or that of all the Raksasas.

निहत्य रावणं संख्ये सर्वथा निशितैः शरैः
प्रतिनेष्यति रामस्त्वामयोध्यामसितेक्षणे

nihatya rāvaṇaṁ saṁkhye sarvathā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
pratineṣyati rāmastvāmayodhyāmasitekṣaṇe
O dark-eyed lady slaying Ravana in battle with sharp shafts, Rama shall take the back to Ayodhya.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शब्दो भेरीशङ्खसमाकुलः
श्रुतो वै सर्वसैन्यानां कम्पयन्धरणीतलम्

etasminnantare śabdo bherīśaṅkhasamākulaḥ
śruto vai sarvasainyānāṁ kampayandharaṇītalam
In the meanwhile there was heard a mighty uproar occasioned by the whole host, and drums and conchs, which shook the earth.

श्रुत्वा तु तं वानरसैन्यशब्दं; लङ्कागता राक्षसराजभृत्याः
नष्टौजसो दैन्यपरीतचेष्टाः; श्रेयो न पश्यन्ति नृपस्य दोषैः

śrutvā tu taṁ vānarasainyaśabdaṁ; laṅkāgatā rākṣasarājabhṛtyāḥ
naṣṭaujaso dainyaparītaceṣṭāḥ; śreyo na paśyanti nṛpasya doṣaiḥ

Hearing that hubbub of the monkey-army, the servants of the Raksasa monarch, ran who were in Lanka, growing dispirited, and bereft of energy, with weakness overcoming their powers, did not see any good, in consequence of the fault of the ruler.

तेन शङ्खविमिश्रेण भेरीशब्देन राघवः
उपयतो महाबाहू रामः परपुरंजयः

tena śaṅkhavimiśreṇa bherīśabdena rāghavaḥ
upayato mahābāhū rāmaḥ parapuraṁjayaḥ
That captor of hostile capitals, the mightarmed Rama, was advancing (upon Larika) with the sounds of drums mixed with the blares of conchs.

तं निनादं निशम्याथ रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
मुहूर्तं ध्यानमास्थाय सचिवानभ्युदैक्षत

taṁ ninādaṁ niśamyātha rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
muhūrtaṁ dhyānamāsthāya sacivānabhyudaikṣata
Hearing this noise, Ravana-lord of Raks asas-reflecting for a while, cast his eyes upon his counsellors.

अथ तान्सचिवांस्तत्र सर्वानाभाष्य रावणः
सभां संनादयन्सर्वामित्युवाच महाबलः

atha tānsacivāṁstatra sarvānābhāṣya rāvaṇaḥ
sabhāṁ saṁnādayansarvāmityuvāca mahābalaḥ

Addressing there all those counsellors, that afflictor of the world—the crooked and highly powerful lord of the Raksasas, Ravana, making his court resound, running down (Rama's) crossing the main, as well as his vigour, strength and manhood, said to them.

तरणं सागरस्यापि विक्रमं बलसंचयम्
यदुक्तवन्तो रामस्य भवन्तस्तन्मया श्रुतम्
भवतश्चाप्यहं वेद्मि युद्धे सत्यपराक्रमान्

taraṇaṁ sāgarasyāpi vikramaṁ balasaṁcayam
yaduktavanto rāmasya bhavantastanmayā śrutam
bhavataścāpyahaṁ vedmi yuddhe satyaparākramān
What you have said touching Rama's (prowess), has been heard by me. And I also know you to be of sterling valour in the field. Yet why, knowing Rama's prowess, do you silently look at each other?

ततस्तु सुमहाप्राज्ञो माल्यवान्नाम राक्षसः
रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा मातुः पैतामहोऽब्रवीत्

tatastu sumahāprājño mālyavānnāma rākṣasaḥ
rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā mātuḥ paitāmaho'bravīt
Then the maternal grand sire (of Ravana), possessed of exceeding wisdom, named Malyavan, hearing his words, said.

विद्यास्वभिविनीतो यो राजा राजन्नयानुगः
स शास्ति चिरमैश्वर्यमरींश्च कुरुते वशे

vidyāsvabhivinīto yo rājā rājannayānugaḥ
sa śāsti ciramaiśvaryamarīṁśca kurute vaśe

The king that is accomplished in the various kinds of learning,* and that follow polity, ever command affluence and bring his enemies under his subjection. *The commentator says there are four and ten kinds of learning; but unfortunately he does not enumerate them.

संदधानो हि कालेन विगृह्णंश्चारिभिः सह
स्वपक्षवर्धनं कुर्वन्महदैश्वर्यमश्नुते

saṁdadhāno hi kālena vigṛhṇaṁścāribhiḥ saha
svapakṣavardhanaṁ kurvanmahadaiśvaryamaśnute
He that seasonably concludes peace and carries on war with his enemies, and who advances his own party, attain great affluence.

हीयमानेन कर्तव्यो राज्ञा संधिः समेन च
न शत्रुमवमन्येत ज्यायान्कुर्वीत विग्रहम्

hīyamānena kartavyo rājñā saṁdhiḥ samena ca
na śatrumavamanyeta jyāyānkurvīta vigraham
A king should enter into peace, if he be an equal or inferior of his adversary, and engage in war, if be more powerful, but an enemy should never be disergarded.

तन्मह्यं रोचते संधिः सह रामेण रावण
यदर्थमभियुक्ताः स्म सीता तस्मै प्रदीयताम्

tanmahyaṁ rocate saṁdhiḥ saha rāmeṇa rāvaṇa
yadarthamabhiyuktāḥ sma sītā tasmai pradīyatām
Therefore, O Ravana, peace with Rama is what commends itself to me; and do you render to him that for which you have been invaded (by him), viz., Sita.

तस्य देवर्षयः सर्वे गन्धर्वाश्च जयैषिणः
विरोधं मा गमस्तेन संधिस्ते तेन रोचताम्

tasya devarṣayaḥ sarve gandharvāśca jayaiṣiṇaḥ
virodhaṁ mā gamastena saṁdhiste tena rocatām
All the Devarsis and Gandharvas wish for (Rama's) victory. Therefore, do not enter into hostilities with him; but do you bend your mind to the conclusion of peace with him.

असृजद्भगवान्पक्षौ द्वावेव हि पितामहः
सुराणामसुराणां च धर्माधर्मौ तदाश्रयौ

asṛjadbhagavānpakṣau dvāveva hi pitāmahaḥ
surāṇāmasurāṇāṁ ca dharmādharmau tadāśrayau
That possessor of the six attributes, the Greatfather, has appointed two courses, (respectively) for the Asuras and the celestials, having for their eousness.

धर्मो हि श्रूयते पक्षः सुराणां च महात्मनाम्
अधर्मो रक्षसं पक्षो ह्यसुराणां च रावण

dharmo hi śrūyate pakṣaḥ surāṇāṁ ca mahātmanām
adharmo rakṣasaṁ pakṣo hyasurāṇāṁ ca rāvaṇa
Righteousness, we hear, is the course of the high-souled celestials, as, O. Raksasa, unrighteousness is that of Raksasa and Asuras.

धर्मो वै ग्रसतेऽधर्मं ततः कृतमभूद्युगम्
अधर्मो ग्रसते धर्मं ततस्तिष्यः प्रवर्तते

dharmo vai grasate'dharmaṁ tataḥ kṛtamabhūdyugam
adharmo grasate dharmaṁ tatastiṣyaḥ pravartate
During the Ktta Yuga, righteousness swallow up sin; and during Tisya,* unrighteousness swallow up virtue. *The Kali Yuga.

तत्त्वया चरता लोकान्धर्मो विनिहतो महान्
अधर्मः प्रगृहीतश्च तेनास्मद्बलिनः परे

tattvayā caratā lokāndharmo vinihato mahān
adharmaḥ pragṛhītaśca tenāsmadbalinaḥ pare

You, ranging the three worlds, worlds, had extinguished pregnant piety, and reaped unrighteousness; and it is for this that your foes have waxed potent. *While ranging the three worlds on a career of conquest, you didst, disturbing sacrifices, etc., wrong righteousness.

स प्रमादाद्विवृद्धस्तेऽधर्मोऽहिर्ग्रसते हि नः
विवर्धयति पक्षं च सुराणां सुरभावनः

sa pramādādvivṛddhaste'dharmo'hirgrasate hi naḥ
vivardhayati pakṣaṁ ca surāṇāṁ surabhāvanaḥ
Having grown through through your your neglect, unrighteousness devour us, and that protector of the gods, (righteousness), is strengthening the side of the celestials.

विषयेषु प्रसक्तेन यत्किंचित्कारिणा त्वया
ऋषीणामग्निकल्पानामुद्वेगो जनितो महान्
तेषां प्रभावो दुर्धर्षः प्रदीप्त इव पावकः

viṣayeṣu prasaktena yatkiṁcitkāriṇā tvayā
ṛṣīṇāmagnikalpānāmudvego janito mahān
teṣāṁ prabhāvo durdharṣaḥ pradīpta iva pāvakaḥ
You, addicted to carnal pleasures and acting in defiance of duty, had aroused the high wrath of the saints resembling fire.

तपसा भावितात्मानो धर्मस्यानुग्रहे रताः
मुख्यैर्यज्ञैर्यजन्त्येते नित्यं तैस्तैर्द्विजातयः

tapasā bhāvitātmāno dharmasyānugrahe ratāḥ
mukhyairyajñairyajantyete nityaṁ taistairdvijātayaḥ
The power of these possessed of souls sanctified through asceticism, and ever engaged in invoking the aid of righteousness, is incapable of being resisted and is like flaming fire.

जुह्वत्यग्नींश्च विधिवद्वेदांश्चोच्चैरधीयते
अभिभूय च रक्षांसि ब्रह्मघोषानुदैरयन्
दिशो विप्रद्रुताः सर्वे स्तनयित्नुरिवोष्णगे

juhvatyagnīṁśca vidhivadvedāṁścoccairadhīyate
abhibhūya ca rakṣāṁsi brahmaghoṣānudairayan
diśo vipradrutāḥ sarve stanayitnurivoṣṇage

The twice-born ones engage in contemplation with intent minds, offer oblations into the fire according to the ordinance, and loudly recite the Vedas. They overpower the Raksasa, uttering the Vedas; and thereat they fly in all directions like clouds scattered in summer.

ऋषीणामग्निकल्पानामग्निहोत्रसमुत्थितः
आदत्ते रक्षसां तेजो धूमो व्याप्य दिशो दश

ṛṣīṇāmagnikalpānāmagnihotrasamutthitaḥ
ādatte rakṣasāṁ tejo dhūmo vyāpya diśo daśa
The smoke that arise from the Agnihotra sacrifices of saints resembling fire, enveloping the energy of the Raksasas, spreads over the ten cardinal quarters.

तेषु तेषु च देशेषु पुण्येषु च दृढव्रतैः
चर्यमाणं तपस्तीव्रं संतापयति राक्षसान्

teṣu teṣu ca deśeṣu puṇyeṣu ca dṛḍhavrataiḥ
caryamāṇaṁ tapastīvraṁ saṁtāpayati rākṣasān
The fierce austerities of vow-observing saints, performed at particular sacred spots, try the Raks asas sore.

उत्पातान्विविधान्दृष्ट्वा घोरान्बहुविधांस्तथा
विनाशमनुपश्यामि सर्वेषां रक्षसामहम्

utpātānvividhāndṛṣṭvā ghorānbahuvidhāṁstathā
vināśamanupaśyāmi sarveṣāṁ rakṣasāmaham
Witnessing various and many dire portents, I perceive the destruction of all the Raksasas.

खराभिस्तनिता घोरा मेघाः प्रतिभयंकरः
शोणितेनाभिवर्षन्ति लङ्कामुष्णेन सर्वतः

kharābhistanitā ghorā meghāḥ pratibhayaṁkaraḥ
śoṇitenābhivarṣanti laṅkāmuṣṇena sarvataḥ
Dreadful and terrific clouds, uttering harsh sounds, are showering blood all around Lanka.

रुदतां वाहनानां च प्रपतन्त्यस्रबिन्दवः
ध्वजा ध्वस्ता विवर्णाश्च न प्रभान्ति यथापुरम्

rudatāṁ vāhanānāṁ ca prapatantyasrabindavaḥ
dhvajā dhvastā vivarṇāśca na prabhānti yathāpuram
And (live) vehicles are dropping profuse tears. And all sides, covered with dust, do not appear bright as formerly.

व्याला गोमायवो गृध्रा वाशन्ति च सुभैरवम्
प्रविश्य लङ्कामनिशं समवायांश्च कुर्वते

vyālā gomāyavo gṛdhrā vāśanti ca subhairavam
praviśya laṅkāmaniśaṁ samavāyāṁśca kurvate
And beasts of prey, jackals and vultures, are emitting frightful cries, and, entering into the garden of Lanka, form themselves into bands.

कालिकाः पाण्डुरैर्दन्तैः प्रहसन्त्यग्रतः स्थिताः
स्त्रियः स्वप्नेषु मुष्णन्त्यो गृहाणि प्रतिभाष्य च

kālikāḥ pāṇḍurairdantaiḥ prahasantyagrataḥ sthitāḥ
striyaḥ svapneṣu muṣṇantyo gṛhāṇi pratibhāṣya ca
In dreams mighty dark-hued women in front of dwellings, seizing at (the furniture) thereof, and speaking inauspiciously, laugh displaying their sable teeth.

गृहाणां बलिकर्माणि श्वानः पर्युपभुञ्जते
खरा गोषु प्रजायन्ते मूषिका नकुलैः सह

gṛhāṇāṁ balikarmāṇi śvānaḥ paryupabhuñjate
kharā goṣu prajāyante mūṣikā nakulaiḥ saha
In houses dogs are feasting on the articles of worship. And cows bring forth asses, and mungooses, mice.

मार्जारा द्वीपिभिः सार्धं सूकराः शुनकैः सह
किंनरा राक्षसैश्चापि समेयुर्मानुषैः सह

mārjārā dvīpibhiḥ sārdhaṁ sūkarāḥ śunakaiḥ saha
kiṁnarā rākṣasaiścāpi sameyurmānuṣaiḥ saha
And cats are pairing with leopards, and swine with dogs, and Kinnaras with Raksasas and human being.

पाण्डुरा रक्तपादाश्च विहगाः कालचोदिताः
राक्षसानां विनाशाय कपोता विचरन्ति च

pāṇḍurā raktapādāśca vihagāḥ kālacoditāḥ
rākṣasānāṁ vināśāya kapotā vicaranti ca
are And red-footed white sky-coursing pigeons, urged on by Doom, are going about for the destruction of the Raksasas.

चीकी कूचीति वाशन्त्यः शारिका वेश्मसु स्थिताः
पतन्ति ग्रथिताश्चापि निर्जिताः कलहैषिणः

cīkī kūcīti vāśantyaḥ śārikā veśmasu sthitāḥ
patanti grathitāścāpi nirjitāḥ kalahaiṣiṇaḥ
And female-parrots in houses, wounded and worsted by other birds delighting in discord, are dropping down, emitting indistinct notes.

करालो विकटो मुण्डः पुरुषः कृष्णपिङ्गलः
कालो गृहाणि सर्वेषां काले कालेऽन्ववेक्षते
एतान्यन्यानि दुष्टानि निमित्तान्युत्पतन्ति च

karālo vikaṭo muṇḍaḥ puruṣaḥ kṛṣṇapiṅgalaḥ
kālo gṛhāṇi sarveṣāṁ kāle kāle'nvavekṣate
etānyanyāni duṣṭāni nimittānyutpatanti ca

All the birds and beasts crying (distressfully) with their faces turned towards the sun. And at dusk a frightful, withered, tawnyhued male figure, looking like Death himself, with his head shaven, peer into the houses (of people).

इदं वचस्तत्र निगद्य माल्यव;न्परीक्ष्य रक्षोऽधिपतेर्मनः पुनः
अनुत्तमेषूत्तमपौरुषो बली; बभूव तूष्णीं समवेक्ष्य रावणम्

idaṁ vacastatra nigadya mālyava;nparīkṣya rakṣo'dhipatermanaḥ punaḥ
anuttameṣūttamapauruṣo balī; babhūva tūṣṇīṁ samavekṣya rāvaṇam
Having said this to that vile one, and known the intention of the lord of Raksasa, that strong Malyavan, of exceeding prowess, became silent, eying Ravana.

तत्तु माल्यवतो वाक्यं हितमुक्तं दशाननः
न मर्षयति दुष्टात्मा कालस्य वशमागतः

tattu mālyavato vākyaṁ hitamuktaṁ daśānanaḥ
na marṣayati duṣṭātmā kālasya vaśamāgataḥ
The Ten-necked one, come under the control of Time, did not brook the beneficial speech, spoken by Malyavan.

स बद्ध्वा भ्रुकुटिं वक्त्रे क्रोधस्य वशमागतः
अमर्षात्परिवृत्ताक्षो माल्यवन्तमथाब्रवीत्

sa baddhvā bhrukuṭiṁ vaktre krodhasya vaśamāgataḥ
amarṣātparivṛttākṣo mālyavantamathābravīt
Contracting his face into a frown, he, coming under the masterdom of passion, with his eyes rolling in wrath, addressed Mayavan, saying.

हितबुद्ध्या यदहितं वचः परुषमुच्यते
परपक्षं प्रविश्यैव नैतच्छ्रोत्रगतं मम

hitabuddhyā yadahitaṁ vacaḥ paruṣamucyate
parapakṣaṁ praviśyaiva naitacchrotragataṁ mama
The words which, deeming the strength of the enemy as superior, you have harshly spoken, considering it as beneficial, had never before entered my ears.

मानुषं कृपणं राममेकं शाखामृगाश्रयम्
समर्थं मन्यसे केन त्यक्तं पित्रा वनालयम्

mānuṣaṁ kṛpaṇaṁ rāmamekaṁ śākhāmṛgāśrayam
samarthaṁ manyase kena tyaktaṁ pitrā vanālayam

A (mere) man, and feeble, and alone, and having monkeys for his support, why do you deem Rama, who has (further) been cast off by his sire, and has in consequence taken refuge in the woods, as competent (to cope with me)?

रक्षसामीश्वरं मां च देवतानां भयंकरम्
हीनं मां मन्यसे केन अहीनं सर्वविक्रमैः

rakṣasāmīśvaraṁ māṁ ca devatānāṁ bhayaṁkaram
hīnaṁ māṁ manyase kena ahīnaṁ sarvavikramaiḥ
Why do you consider me, who am the lord of the Raksasa, and feared even by the immortals, as weak and reft of all power?

वीरद्वेषेण वा शङ्के पक्षपातेन वा रिपोः
त्वयाहं परुषाण्युक्तः परप्रोत्साहनेन वा

vīradveṣeṇa vā śaṅke pakṣapātena vā ripoḥ
tvayāhaṁ paruṣāṇyuktaḥ paraprotsāhanena vā
You, I suspect, speak (thus) roughly either from jealousy of my heroism, or for inciting me.

प्रभवन्तं पदस्थं हि परुषं कोऽभिधास्यति
पण्डितः शास्त्रतत्त्वज्ञो विना प्रोत्साहनाद्रिपोः

prabhavantaṁ padasthaṁ hi paruṣaṁ ko'bhidhāsyati
paṇḍitaḥ śāstratattvajño vinā protsāhanādripoḥ
Who that is wise and learned, ever address him roughly that is at once puissant and of (high) station, if not to spur him on?

आनीय च वनात्सीतां पद्महीनामिव श्रियम्
किमर्थं प्रतिदास्यामि राघवस्य भयादहम्

ānīya ca vanātsītāṁ padmahīnāmiva śriyam
kimarthaṁ pratidāsyāmi rāghavasya bhayādaham
Why, having brought Sita like a Sri shorn of her lotus, shall I give her up, from fear of Raghava?

वृतं वानरकोटीभिः ससुग्रीवं सलक्ष्मणम्
पश्य कैश्चिदहोभिस्त्वं राघवं निहतं मया

vṛtaṁ vānarakoṭībhiḥ sasugrīvaṁ salakṣmaṇam
paśya kaiścidahobhistvaṁ rāghavaṁ nihataṁ mayā
Behold Raghava, environed by Kotis of monkeys, with Sugriva and Laksmana, slain on of these days!

द्वन्द्वे यस्य न तिष्ठन्ति दैवतान्यपि संयुगे
स कस्माद्रावणो युद्धे भयमाहारयिष्यति

dvandve yasya na tiṣṭhanti daivatānyapi saṁyuge
sa kasmādrāvaṇo yuddhe bhayamāhārayiṣyati
He before whom even the gods cannot stay in the battle field, how can that Ravana ever come by fear?

द्विधा भज्येयमप्येवं न नमेयं तु कस्यचित्
एष मे सहजो दोषः स्वभावो दुरतिक्रमः

dvidhā bhajyeyamapyevaṁ na nameyaṁ tu kasyacit
eṣa me sahajo doṣaḥ svabhāvo duratikramaḥ
Better that I should be riven in twain, but bend I never will. This is my native fault; and nature is incapable of being overcome.

यदि तावत्समुद्रे तु सेतुर्बद्धो यदृच्छया
रामेण विस्मयः कोऽत्र येन ते भयमागतम्

yadi tāvatsamudre tu seturbaddho yadṛcchayā
rāmeṇa vismayaḥ ko'tra yena te bhayamāgatam
If Rama bath at his pleasure constructed a bridge over the ocean, what is the wonder in this that you have conceived such a fear?

स तु तीर्त्वार्णवं रामः सह वानरसेनया
प्रतिजानामि ते सत्यं न जीवन्प्रतियास्यति

sa tu tīrtvārṇavaṁ rāmaḥ saha vānarasenayā
pratijānāmi te satyaṁ na jīvanpratiyāsyati
And although Rama has crossed the ocean along with the monkey-army, yet I swear to you truly, living, he shall not back hence.

एवं ब्रुवाणं संरब्धं रुष्टं विज्ञाय रावणम्
व्रीडितो माल्यवान्वाक्यं नोत्तरं प्रत्यपद्यत

evaṁ bruvāṇaṁ saṁrabdhaṁ ruṣṭaṁ vijñāya rāvaṇam
vrīḍito mālyavānvākyaṁ nottaraṁ pratyapadyata
When Ravana, wrought up with passion, had spoken thus, Malyavan, knowing him wroth, did not return a reply.

जयाशिषा च राजानं वर्धयित्वा यथोचितम्
माल्यवानभ्यनुज्ञातो जगाम स्वं निवेशनम्

jayāśiṣā ca rājānaṁ vardhayitvā yathocitam
mālyavānabhyanujñāto jagāma svaṁ niveśanam
And, duly tendering blessings to the king, Malyavan, taking his permission, went to his own abode.

रावणस्तु सहामात्यो मन्त्रयित्वा विमृश्य च
लङ्कायामतुलां गुप्तिं कारयामास राक्षसः

rāvaṇastu sahāmātyo mantrayitvā vimṛśya ca
laṅkāyāmatulāṁ guptiṁ kārayāmāsa rākṣasaḥ
The Raksasa, Ravana, along with his courtiers, having consulted together as to what was fit to be done, set about the defence of Lanka.

व्यादिदेश च पूर्वस्यां प्रहस्तं द्वारि राक्षसं
दक्षिणस्यां महावीर्यौ महापार्श्व महोदरौ

vyādideśa ca pūrvasyāṁ prahastaṁ dvāri rākṣasaṁ
dakṣiṇasyāṁ mahāvīryau mahāpārśva mahodarau

He commanded the Raksasa Prahasta (to guard) the Eastern gate; and the exceedingly powerful Mahaparsva and Mahodara (to guard) the Southern gate; and he ordered his son Indrajit, possessing mighty powers of illusion, girt by innumerable Raksasas, to guard the Western gate.

उत्तरस्यां पुरद्वारि व्यादिश्य शुकसारणौ
स्वयं चात्र भविष्यामि मन्त्रिणस्तानुवाच ह

uttarasyāṁ puradvāri vyādiśya śukasāraṇau
svayaṁ cātra bhaviṣyāmi mantriṇastānuvāca ha
He commanded Suka and Sarana to defend the Northern gate. But he said to the counsellors, I will myself go thither.* *i.e. to defend the Northerm gate.

राक्षसं तु विरूपाक्षं महावीर्यपराक्रमम्
मध्यमेऽस्थापयद्गुल्मे बहुभिः सह राक्षसैः

rākṣasaṁ tu virūpākṣaṁ mahāvīryaparākramam
madhyame'sthāpayadgulme bahubhiḥ saha rākṣasaiḥ
And he posted in the middle in the garrison the Raksasa, Virupaksa, endowed with exceeding prowess and energy, backed by countless raksasas.

एवंविधानं लङ्कायां कृत्वा राक्षसपुंगवः
मेने कृतार्थमात्मानं कृतान्तवशमागतः

evaṁvidhānaṁ laṅkāyāṁ kṛtvā rākṣasapuṁgavaḥ
mene kṛtārthamātmānaṁ kṛtāntavaśamāgataḥ
Having taken these measures in Lanka, the raksasa-chief, urged by Fate, deemed himself as having achieved success.

विसर्जयामास ततः स मन्त्रिणो; विधानमाज्ञाप्य पुरस्य पुष्कलम्
जयाशिषा मन्त्रगणेन पूजितो; विवेश सोऽन्तःपुरमृद्धिमन्महत्

visarjayāmāsa tataḥ sa mantriṇo; vidhānamājñāpya purasya puṣkalam
jayāśiṣā mantragaṇena pūjito; viveśa so'ntaḥpuramṛddhimanmahat

Having thus completely provided for the defence of the city, he dismissed the ministers; and, honoured by the counsellors with blessings of victory, (then) entered his magnificent and splendid inner apartment.

अङ्गदो वालिपुत्रश्च सौमित्रिः शरभः कपिः
सुषेणः सहदायादो मैन्दो द्विविद एव च

aṅgado vāliputraśca saumitriḥ śarabhaḥ kapiḥ
suṣeṇaḥ sahadāyādo maindo dvivida eva ca

Those, kings, man and monkey, that monkey the Wind-god's son, Jambavan-sovereign of bears—the Raksasa, Vibhisana, the son of Vali, Angada, Sumitra's son, the monkey, Sarabha, Susena along with his friends, Kumuda, Nala, and Panasa, arriving at the dominions of the enemy, assembled together, began to deliberate.

इयं सा लक्ष्यते लङ्का पुरी रावणपालिता
सासुरोरगगन्धर्वैरमरैरपि दुर्जया

iyaṁ sā lakṣyate laṅkā purī rāvaṇapālitā
sāsuroragagandharvairamarairapi durjayā
Yonder is that Lanka ruled by Ravana, invincible even to the celestials, serpents and Gandharvas.

कार्यसिद्धिं पुरस्कृत्य मन्त्रयध्वं विनिर्णये
नित्यं संनिहितो ह्यत्र रावणो राक्षसाधिपः

kāryasiddhiṁ puraskṛtya mantrayadhvaṁ vinirṇaye
nityaṁ saṁnihito hyatra rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
Let us, keeping before us success in the enterprise, consult together for the purpose of arriving at a decision.

तथा तेषु ब्रुवाणेषु रावणावरजोऽब्रवीत्
वाक्यमग्राम्यपदवत्पुष्कलार्थं विभीषणः

tathā teṣu bruvāṇeṣu rāvaṇāvarajo'bravīt
vākyamagrāmyapadavatpuṣkalārthaṁ vibhīṣaṇaḥ
We are here daily nearing Ravana, lord of Raksasas. As they were speaking thus, Ravana's younger brother, Vibhisana, said in a pregnant speech free from provinicialism.

अनलः शरभश्चैव संपातिः प्रघसस्तथा
गत्वा लङ्कां ममामात्याः पुरीं पुनरिहागताः

analaḥ śarabhaścaiva saṁpātiḥ praghasastathā
gatvā laṅkāṁ mamāmātyāḥ purīṁ punarihāgatāḥ
Anala, Panasa, Sampati and Pramati— all courtiers of mine-having gone up to Lanka, have come back here.

भूत्वा शकुनयः सर्वे प्रविष्टाश्च रिपोर्बलम्
विधानं विहितं यच्च तद्दृष्ट्वा समुपस्थिताः

bhūtvā śakunayaḥ sarve praviṣṭāśca riporbalam
vidhānaṁ vihitaṁ yacca taddṛṣṭvā samupasthitāḥ
Wearing the forms of birds, they entered into the hostile forces; and, having seen the measures that had been adopted (by them, have come (back).

संविधानं यथाहुस्ते रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
राम तद्ब्रुवतः सर्वं यथातथ्येन मे शृणु

saṁvidhānaṁ yathāhuste rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
rāma tadbruvataḥ sarvaṁ yathātathyena me śṛṇu
O Rama, hearken to me as I tell you truly anent the provisions which they have related, made by the wicked-minded Ravana.

इन्द्रजित्पश्चिमद्वारं राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृतः
पट्टसासिधनुष्मद्भिः शूलमुद्गरपाणिभिः

indrajitpaścimadvāraṁ rākṣasairbahubhirvṛtaḥ
paṭṭasāsidhanuṣmadbhiḥ śūlamudgarapāṇibhiḥ

In the Eastern gate stay Prahasta along with his forces; in the Southern, the exceedingly powerful Mahaparsva and Mahodara, and in the Western. Ravana's son, Indrajit, supported by innumerable Raksasas, equipped with pattisas, swords and bows, and bearing darts and maces in their hands, surrounded by heroes carrying various weapons.

युक्तः परमसंविग्नो राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृतः
उत्तरं नगरद्वारं रावणः स्वयमास्थितः

yuktaḥ paramasaṁvigno rākṣasairbahubhirvṛtaḥ
uttaraṁ nagaradvāraṁ rāvaṇaḥ svayamāsthitaḥ
And, backed by many thousands of Raksasas wielding weapons, and accompanied by Raksasas conversant with counsel, Ravana himself, his heart agitated to the height, gaurd the Northern gate of the city.

विरूपाक्षस्तु महता शूलखड्गधनुष्मता
बलेन राक्षसैः सार्धं मध्यमं गुल्ममास्थितः

virūpākṣastu mahatā śūlakhaḍgadhanuṣmatā
balena rākṣasaiḥ sārdhaṁ madhyamaṁ gulmamāsthitaḥ
Virupaksa with a powerful force accoutred in javelins, clubs and bows, protects the garrison in the centre.

एतानेवंविधान्गुल्माँल्लङ्कायां समुदीक्ष्य ते
मामकाः सचिवाः सर्वे शीघ्रं पुनरिहागताः

etānevaṁvidhāngulmā̐llaṅkāyāṁ samudīkṣya te
māmakāḥ sacivāḥ sarve śīghraṁ punarihāgatāḥ
Having seen these hosts thus disposed in Lanka, my counsellors have speedily come back here.

गजानां च सहस्रं च रथानामयुतं पुरे
हयानामयुते द्वे च साग्रकोटी च रक्षसाम्

gajānāṁ ca sahasraṁ ca rathānāmayutaṁ pure
hayānāmayute dve ca sāgrakoṭī ca rakṣasām
There are ten thousand elephants, an Ayuta cars, two of horses, and abouta koti of Raksasas, powerful and strong, and equipped with arms in conflict.* *These are, remarks the commentator, the leader.

विक्रान्ता बलवन्तश्च संयुगेष्वाततायिनः
इष्टा राक्षसराजस्य नित्यमेते निशाचराः

vikrāntā balavantaśca saṁyugeṣvātatāyinaḥ
iṣṭā rākṣasarājasya nityamete niśācarāḥ
These night-rangers are ever the favourites of the Raksasa ruler. And, O kine, a koti of forces accompany each of these Raksasas in battle.

एतां प्रवृत्तिं लङ्कायां मन्त्रिप्रोक्तं विभीषणः
रामं कमलपत्राक्षमिदमुत्तरमब्रवीत्

etāṁ pravṛttiṁ laṅkāyāṁ mantriproktaṁ vibhīṣaṇaḥ
rāmaṁ kamalapatrākṣamidamuttaramabravīt

In company with his counsellors, Ravana's graceful younger brother, ever striving for the welfare of Rama, by way of answer communicated everything that was going forward in Lanka to Rama, having eyes resembling lotus leaves.

कुबेरं तु यदा राम रावणः प्रत्ययुध्यत
षष्टिः शतसहस्राणि तदा निर्यान्ति राक्षसाः

kuberaṁ tu yadā rāma rāvaṇaḥ pratyayudhyata
ṣaṣṭiḥ śatasahasrāṇi tadā niryānti rākṣasāḥ

O Rama, when Ravana battled with Kuvera, sixty lacs of Raksasas marched forth (to meet him). In prowess, energy, vigour, exceeding fortitude, and hauteur, they resembled the wicked-minded Ravana himself.

अत्र मन्युर्न कर्तव्यो रोषये त्वां न भीषये
समर्थो ह्यसि वीर्येण सुराणामपि निग्रहे

atra manyurna kartavyo roṣaye tvāṁ na bhīṣaye
samartho hyasi vīryeṇa surāṇāmapi nigrahe

In this matter, you ought not to grow wroth, I only arouse your wrath, and do not endeavour to frighten you. You can subdue even the celestials by your prowess. *i.e. You ought not to be angry with me; for I do not frighten you, but rouse your wrath against Ravana.

तद्भवांश्चतुरङ्गेण बलेन महता वृतः
व्यूह्येदं वानरानीकं निर्मथिष्यसि रावणम्

tadbhavāṁścaturaṅgeṇa balena mahatā vṛtaḥ
vyūhyedaṁ vānarānīkaṁ nirmathiṣyasi rāvaṇam
Therefore you, environed by a mighty army, having arrayed the monkey-forces in order of battle, shall thrash Ravana (in battle)

रावणावरजे वाक्यमेवं ब्रुवति राघवः
शत्रूणां प्रतिघातार्थमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्

rāvaṇāvaraje vākyamevaṁ bruvati rāghavaḥ
śatrūṇāṁ pratighātārthamidaṁ vacanamabravīt
When Ravana's younger brother had spoken thus, Raghava, said these words with reference to his beating the foe.

पूर्वद्वारे तु लङ्काया नीलो वानरपुंगवः
प्रहस्तं प्रतियोद्धा स्याद्वानरैर्बहुभिर्वृतः

pūrvadvāre tu laṅkāyā nīlo vānarapuṁgavaḥ
prahastaṁ pratiyoddhā syādvānarairbahubhirvṛtaḥ
Let that foremost of monkey, Nila, surrounded to by an immense number of monkeys, cope with Prahasta at the Eastern gate of Lanka.

अङ्गदो वालिपुत्रस्तु बलेन महता वृतः
दक्षिणे बाधतां द्वारे महापार्श्वमहोदरौ

aṅgado vāliputrastu balena mahatā vṛtaḥ
dakṣiṇe bādhatāṁ dvāre mahāpārśvamahodarau
And, engirt by a mighty force, let Angada, son of Vali, resist Mahaparsva and Mahodara at the Southern gate (thereof).

हनूमान्पश्चिमद्वारं निपीड्य पवनात्मजः
प्रविशत्वप्रमेयात्मा बहुभिः कपिभिर्वृतः

hanūmānpaścimadvāraṁ nipīḍya pavanātmajaḥ
praviśatvaprameyātmā bahubhiḥ kapibhirvṛtaḥ
And let that son of the Wind-god, Hanuman, backed by innumerable monkeys, (beating the host stationed) at the Western gate, find entrance (into the city).

दैत्यदानवसंघानामृषीणां च महात्मनाम्
विप्रकारप्रियः क्षुद्रो वरदानबलान्वितः

daityadānavasaṁghānāmṛṣīṇāṁ ca mahātmanām
viprakārapriyaḥ kṣudro varadānabalānvitaḥ

I myself, determined compass the destruction of the lord of Raksasas, who, waxing powerful in consequence of the boon he has received, has brought about the destruction of high-souled saints resembling gods and Danavas, and who goes round all regions, oppressing people, will, along with Sumitra's son, smiting (the foe), occupy the Northern entiuile., where Ravana with his army is stationed.

वानरेन्द्रश्च बलवानृक्षराजश्च जाम्बवान्
राक्षसेन्द्रानुजश्चैव गुल्मे भवतु मध्यमे

vānarendraśca balavānṛkṣarājaśca jāmbavān
rākṣasendrānujaścaiva gulme bhavatu madhyame
And let the powerful king of monkeys, and the puissant sovereign of bears, and the younger brother of the Raksasa-chief, manage the soldiery posted in the centre.

न चैव मानुषं रूपं कार्यं हरिभिराहवे
एषा भवतु नः संज्ञा युद्धेऽस्मिन्वानरे बले

na caiva mānuṣaṁ rūpaṁ kāryaṁ haribhirāhave
eṣā bhavatu naḥ saṁjñā yuddhe'sminvānare bale

In this battle, the monkeys need not assume the forms of human being. And let this serve for a sign that the monkeys, in order to the recognition of our own forces, appear with their proper monkey-marks. We seven only shall battle with the foe in human shapes, viz.

अहमेव सह भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणेन महौजसा
आत्मना पञ्चमश्चायं सखा मम विभीषणः

ahameva saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena mahaujasā
ātmanā pañcamaścāyaṁ sakhā mama vibhīṣaṇaḥ
I along with my brother, the exceedingly energetic Laksmana, and my friend Vibhisana counting for the fifth in company with his own following.

स रामः कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थमेवमुक्त्वा विभीषणम्
सुवेलारोहणे बुद्धिं चकार मतिमान्मतिम्

sa rāmaḥ kāryasiddhyarthamevamuktvā vibhīṣaṇam
suvelārohaṇe buddhiṁ cakāra matimānmatim
Having said this to Vibhisana for attaining success in the enterprise, that lord, the intelligent Rama, seeing the sides of Suvela more beautiful (than other places), intended to ascend it.

ततस्तु रामो महता बलेन; प्रच्छाद्य सर्वां पृथिवीं महात्मा
प्रहृष्टरूपोऽभिजगाम लङ्कां; कृत्वा मतिं सोऽरिवधे महात्मा

tatastu rāmo mahatā balena; pracchādya sarvāṁ pṛthivīṁ mahātmā
prahṛṣṭarūpo'bhijagāma laṅkāṁ; kṛtvā matiṁ so'rivadhe mahātmā

Then, environed by a mighty host, the highsouled and magnanimous Rama, his features mirroring forth high exultation, overshadowing the entire Earth (with his forces), set out for Lanka, determined upon destroying the enemy.

स तु कृत्वा सुवेलस्य मतिमारोहणं प्रति
लक्ष्मणानुगतो रामः सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत्

sa tu kṛtvā suvelasya matimārohaṇaṁ prati
lakṣmaṇānugato rāmaḥ sugrīvamidamabravīt

Having been bent upon mounting Suvela, Rama, followed by Laksmana, addressed in sweet and excellent words, Sugriva, and that righteous night-ranger, Vibhisana, versed in। counsel and conversant with precepts, who was devoted to him, saying.

सुवेलं साधु शैलेन्द्रमिमं धातुशतैश्चितम्
अध्यारोहामहे सर्वे वत्स्यामोऽत्र निशामिमाम्

suvelaṁ sādhu śailendramimaṁ dhātuśataiścitam
adhyārohāmahe sarve vatsyāmo'tra niśāmimām
We shall all ascend this mount Suvela, be dight with metals; and pass this night even here.

एवं संमन्त्रयन्नेव सक्रोधो रावणं प्रति
रामः सुवेलं वासाय चित्रसानुमुपारुहत्

evaṁ saṁmantrayanneva sakrodho rāvaṇaṁ prati
rāmaḥ suvelaṁ vāsāya citrasānumupāruhat
Having decided thus, Rama, filled with wrath at Ravana, coming to Suvela, ascended its variegated plateau.

पृष्ठतो लक्ष्मण चैनमन्वगच्छत्समाहितः
सशरं चापमुद्यम्य सुमहद्विक्रमे रतः

pṛṣṭhato lakṣmaṇa cainamanvagacchatsamāhitaḥ
saśaraṁ cāpamudyamya sumahadvikrame rataḥ

And Laksmana, collected, went in his wake. And, upraising bow and arrow, Sugriva, (ever) engaged in valorous acts, accompanied with Vibhisana as well as his counsellors, following him, also ascended (the mountain).

ते त्वदीर्घेण कालेन गिरिमारुह्य सर्वतः
ददृशुः शिखरे तस्य विषक्तामिव खे पुरीम्

te tvadīrgheṇa kālena girimāruhya sarvataḥ
dadṛśuḥ śikhare tasya viṣaktāmiva khe purīm
And all those rangers of mountains, gifted with the vehemence of the Wind in hundreds ascended mount Suvela, where Raghava was stationed.

तां शुभां प्रवरद्वारां प्राकारवरशोभिताम्
लङ्कां राक्षससंपूर्णां ददृशुर्हरियूथपाः

tāṁ śubhāṁ pravaradvārāṁ prākāravaraśobhitām
laṅkāṁ rākṣasasaṁpūrṇāṁ dadṛśurhariyūthapāḥ

Ascending the mountain in a short time, they all beheld from its summit the city, appearing to be built on the air. And the monkey-leaders beheld Lanka, exceedingly splendid with noble gateways; gracefully enclosed with a wall; thronging with Raksasas; and defended by sable Raksasas.

प्राकारचयसंस्थैश्च तथा नीलैर्निशाचरैः
ददृशुस्ते हरिश्रेष्ठाः प्राकारमपरं कृतम्

prākāracayasaṁsthaiśca tathā nīlairniśācaraiḥ
dadṛśuste hariśreṣṭhāḥ prākāramaparaṁ kṛtam
The foremost of monkeys saw these appearing like another wall (overtopping the one beneath).

ते दृष्ट्वा वानराः सर्वे राक्षसान्युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः
मुमुचुर्विपुलान्नादांस्तत्र रामस्य पश्यतः

te dṛṣṭvā vānarāḥ sarve rākṣasānyuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
mumucurvipulānnādāṁstatra rāmasya paśyataḥ
On seeing the Raksasas, the monkeys burning for battle set up various roars in the presence of Rama.

ततोऽस्तमगमत्सूर्यः संध्यया प्रतिरञ्जितः
पूर्णचन्द्रप्रदीपा च क्षपा समभिवर्तते

tato'stamagamatsūryaḥ saṁdhyayā pratirañjitaḥ
pūrṇacandrapradīpā ca kṣapā samabhivartate
Then the Sun, crimsoned with Eve, ascended the Setting-hill; and Night came, illumined by the Moon at his full.

ततः स रामो हरिवाहिनीपति;र्विभीषणेन प्रतिनन्द्य सत्कृतः
सलक्ष्मणो यूथपयूथसंवृतः; सुवेल पृष्ठे न्यवसद्यथासुखम्

tataḥ sa rāmo harivāhinīpati;rvibhīṣaṇena pratinandya satkṛtaḥ
salakṣmaṇo yūthapayūthasaṁvṛtaḥ; suvela pṛṣṭhe nyavasadyathāsukham
Then the master of the monkey-army, Rama, saluted and honoured by Vibhisana, accompanied by Laksmana as well as the leaders of the monkeys, sojourned happily on the beast of Suvela.

तां रात्रिमुषितास्तत्र सुवेले हरिपुंगवाः
लङ्कायां ददृशुर्वीरा वनान्युपवनानि च

tāṁ rātrimuṣitāstatra suvele haripuṁgavāḥ
laṅkāyāṁ dadṛśurvīrā vanānyupavanāni ca
Having passed the night in Suvela, the heroic monkey-leaders surveyed woods and forests in Lanka.

समसौम्यानि रम्याणि विशालान्यायतानि च
दृष्टिरम्याणि ते दृष्ट्वा बभूवुर्जातविस्मयाः

samasaumyāni ramyāṇi viśālānyāyatāni ca
dṛṣṭiramyāṇi te dṛṣṭvā babhūvurjātavismayāḥ
Seeing those extensive (woods and forests), mild, and charming, and beautiful to behold, they were seized with wonderment.

विचित्रकुसुमोपेतै रक्तकोमलपल्लवैः
शाद्वलैश्च तथा नीलैश्चित्राभिर्वनराजिभिः

vicitrakusumopetai raktakomalapallavaiḥ
śādvalaiśca tathā nīlaiścitrābhirvanarājibhiḥ

And trees there, furnished with variegated flowers having tender rosy leaves, and blue lawns, and rows of woods; and bearing odorous and charming blossoms and fruits, looked like men adorned with ornaments.

तच्चैत्ररथसंकाशं मनोज्ञं नन्दनोपमम्
वनं सर्वर्तुकं रम्यं शुशुभे षट्पदायुतम्

taccaitrarathasaṁkāśaṁ manojñaṁ nandanopamam
vanaṁ sarvartukaṁ ramyaṁ śuśubhe ṣaṭpadāyutam
There a delightful and pleasant wood resembling Caitraratha, and like to Nandana itself, having all the seasons present, appeared beauteous to the view, with black bees all around.

नत्यूहकोयष्टिभकैर्नृत्यमानैश्च बर्हिभिः
रुतं परभृतानां च शुश्रुवे वननिर्झरे

natyūhakoyaṣṭibhakairnṛtyamānaiśca barhibhiḥ
rutaṁ parabhṛtānāṁ ca śuśruve vananirjhare
And it had Datyuhas, and Koyasthivas, and peacocks dancing; and the strains of the coels were heard at the woodland rills.

नित्यमत्तविहंगानि भ्रमराचरितानि च
कोकिलाकुलषण्डानि विहगाभिरुतानि च

nityamattavihaṁgāni bhramarācaritāni ca
kokilākulaṣaṇḍāni vihagābhirutāni ca

The heroic and exhilarated monkeys, capable of wearing forms at pleasure, entered those woods and groves frequented by maddened birds and ranged by Bhramaras, tracts overflowing with the lays of coels, and ringing with the voices of songsters, resonant with the notes of Bhramaras, sovereigns of their species and eloquent with the cries of ospreys.

अन्ये तु हरिवीराणां यूथान्निष्क्रम्य यूथपाः
सुग्रीवेणाभ्यनुज्ञाता लङ्कां जग्मुः पताकिनीम्

anye tu harivīrāṇāṁ yūthānniṣkramya yūthapāḥ
sugrīveṇābhyanujñātā laṅkāṁ jagmuḥ patākinīm

As the exceedingly energetic monkeys entered, there blew upon them the breeze-like to life-redolent of perfume obtained from contact with the blossoms. And others of the leaders among the heroic monkeys, coming out from the bands, ordered by Sugriva, made in the direction of Lanka crowned with ensigns.

वित्रासयन्तो विहगांस्त्रासयन्तो मृगद्विपान्
कम्पयन्तश्च तां लङ्कां नादैः स्वैर्नदतां वराः

vitrāsayanto vihagāṁstrāsayanto mṛgadvipān
kampayantaśca tāṁ laṅkāṁ nādaiḥ svairnadatāṁ varāḥ
And, terrifying the fowls and dispiriting beasts and birds and shaking Lanka with their roars, those foremost monkeys set up shouts.

कुर्वन्तस्ते महावेगा महीं चारणपीडिताम्
रजश्च सहसैवोर्ध्वं जगाम चरणोद्धतम्

kurvantaste mahāvegā mahīṁ cāraṇapīḍitām
rajaśca sahasaivordhvaṁ jagāma caraṇoddhatam
They, endowed with great impetuosity, went on, oppressing the earth with their battle-array; and clouds of dust suddenly arose from the march of the soldiery.

ऋक्षाः सिंहा वराहाश्च महिषा वारणा मृगाः
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्ता जग्मुर्भीता दिशो दश

ṛkṣāḥ siṁhā varāhāśca mahiṣā vāraṇā mṛgāḥ
tena śabdena vitrastā jagmurbhītā diśo daśa
And bears, and lions, and buffaloes, and elephants, and deer, and birds, overwhelmed with affright, made for the t en cardinal points.

यस्यां स्तम्भसहस्रेण प्रासादः समलंकृतः
कैलासशिखराकारो दृश्यते खमिवोल्लिखन्

yasyāṁ stambhasahasreṇa prāsādaḥ samalaṁkṛtaḥ
kailāsaśikharākāro dṛśyate khamivollikhan
