ऊचुः संश्रवणे ये मां द्विजाः कार्तान्तिकाः शुभाम्
तेऽद्य सर्वे हते रामेऽज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः

ūcuḥ saṁśravaṇe ye māṁ dvijāḥ kārtāntikāḥ śubhām
te'dya sarve hate rāme'jñānino'nṛtavādinaḥ
Those twice-born ones that in any hearing had said auspicious words, on Rama being slain, seem today to have spoken a falsehood although they were possessed of knowledge.

इमानि खलु पद्मानि पादयोर्यैः किल स्त्रियः
अधिराज्येऽभिषिच्यन्ते नरेन्द्रैः पतिभिः सह

imāni khalu padmāni pādayoryaiḥ kila striyaḥ
adhirājye'bhiṣicyante narendraiḥ patibhiḥ saha
These lotus-marks on the feet, betokening to gentlewomen possessing them, that they are to be installed in the kingdom in company with their husbands-who are kings-are on me.

वैधव्यं यान्ति यैर्नार्योऽलक्षणैर्भाग्यदुर्लभाः
नात्मनस्तानि पश्यामि पश्यन्ती हतलक्षणा

vaidhavyaṁ yānti yairnāryo'lakṣaṇairbhāgyadurlabhāḥ
nātmanastāni paśyāmi paśyantī hatalakṣaṇā
Those marks find I none on me by which women of rare fortune come by widowhood, but I find that in me these good tokens are nullified.

सत्यानीमानि पद्मानि स्त्रीणामुक्त्वानि लक्षणे
तान्यद्य निहते रामे वितथानि भवन्ति मे

satyānīmāni padmāni strīṇāmuktvāni lakṣaṇe
tānyadya nihate rāme vitathāni bhavanti me
Those marks that are pronounced infallible by those versed in such knowledge, on Rama being slain, are nullified in me.

केशाः सूक्ष्माः समा नीला भ्रुवौ चासंगते मम
वृत्ते चालोमशे जङ्घे दन्ताश्चाविरला मम

keśāḥ sūkṣmāḥ samā nīlā bhruvau cāsaṁgate mama
vṛtte cālomaśe jaṅghe dantāścāviralā mama
My hairs are fine, equal, and blue; my eyebrows touch each other; my hips are devoid of down and round; and my teeth are close.

शङ्खे नेत्रे करौ पादौ गुल्फावूरू च मे चितौ
अनुवृत्ता नखाः स्निग्धाः समाश्चाङ्गुलयो मम

śaṅkhe netre karau pādau gulphāvūrū ca me citau
anuvṛttā nakhāḥ snigdhāḥ samāścāṅgulayo mama
My temples, and eyes hands, feet, ankles, and thighs are equal. And my fingers are furnished with round nails, and are plump and even in the middle.

स्तनौ चाविरलौ पीनौ ममेमौ मग्नचूचुकौ
मग्ना चोत्सङ्गिनी नाभिः पार्श्वोरस्कं च मे चितम्

stanau cāviralau pīnau mamemau magnacūcukau
magnā cotsaṅginī nābhiḥ pārśvoraskaṁ ca me citam
And my breasts are close and firm and developed, and have their nipples sunk. And my navel is depressed, with high sides. And my chest is swelling.

मम वर्णो मणिनिभो मृदून्यङ्गरुहाणि च
प्रतिष्ठितां द्वदशभिर्मामूचुः शुभलक्षणाम्

mama varṇo maṇinibho mṛdūnyaṅgaruhāṇi ca
pratiṣṭhitāṁ dvadaśabhirmāmūcuḥ śubhalakṣaṇām
My complexion is like the hue of gems, and my down soft. And they said that I was furnished with twelve auspicious signs.

समग्रयवमच्छिद्रं पाणिपादं च वर्णवत्
मन्दस्मितेत्येव च मां कन्यालक्षणिका विदुः

samagrayavamacchidraṁ pāṇipādaṁ ca varṇavat
mandasmitetyeva ca māṁ kanyālakṣaṇikā viduḥ

And my hands in the middle parts of my fingers contain wheat-marks, and in the spaces between the fingers, have no uneven corners. And my feet also partake of the general complexion. And my laugh is a gentle smile. And those versed in marks of women knew that I was possessed of such marks.

अधिराज्येऽभिषेको मे ब्राह्मणैः पतिना सह
कृतान्तकुशलैरुक्तं तत्सर्वं वितथीकृतम्

adhirājye'bhiṣeko me brāhmaṇaiḥ patinā saha
kṛtāntakuśalairuktaṁ tatsarvaṁ vitathīkṛtam
Those Brahmanas skilled in telling fortune said that I should be installed in the kingdom along with my husband; but all that has been falsified.

शोधयित्वा जनस्थानं प्रवृत्तिमुपलभ्य च
तीर्त्वा सागरमक्षोभ्यं भ्रातरौ गोष्पदे हतौ

śodhayitvā janasthānaṁ pravṛttimupalabhya ca
tīrtvā sāgaramakṣobhyaṁ bhrātarau goṣpade hatau

Having purified Janasthana (of Raksasas), obtained tidings of me, and crossed the Ocean* incapable of being agitated, those brothers have been slain in the footprint of a cow! *The commentator assigns a metaphorical sense to ocean-but this is hardly necessary.

ननु वारुणमाग्नेयमैन्द्रं वायव्यमेव च
अस्त्रं ब्रह्मशिरश्चैव राघवौ प्रत्यपद्यताम्

nanu vāruṇamāgneyamaindraṁ vāyavyameva ca
astraṁ brahmaśiraścaiva rāghavau pratyapadyatām
The descendants of Raghu had obtained Varuna and Agneya and Aindra and Vayavya and Brahmasira weapons.* * And did they not remember this now? completes the sense.

अदृश्यमानेन रणे मायया वासवोपमौ
मम नाथावनाथाया निहतौ रामलक्ष्मणौ

adṛśyamānena raṇe māyayā vāsavopamau
mama nāthāvanāthāyā nihatau rāmalakṣmaṇau
Through illusion have those lords of me, who am forlorn. Rama and Laksmana, resembling Vasava himself in battle, been slain.

न हि दृष्टिपथं प्राप्य राघवस्य रणे रिपुः
जीवन्प्रतिनिवर्तेत यद्यपि स्यान्मनोजवः

na hi dṛṣṭipathaṁ prāpya rāghavasya raṇe ripuḥ
jīvanpratinivarteta yadyapi syānmanojavaḥ
Coming in battle within ken of Raghava, a foe, even if he be endowed with the fleetness of thought, does not go back living.

न कालस्यातिभारोऽस्ति कृतान्तश्च सुदुर्जयः
यत्र रामः सह भ्रात्रा शेते युधि निपाथितः

na kālasyātibhāro'sti kṛtāntaśca sudurjayaḥ
yatra rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā śete yudhi nipāthitaḥ
There is nothing which is too hard for Time; and the Destroyer is incapable of being overcome; inasmuch as Rama along with his brother Laksmana has fallen in fight.

सा हि चिन्तयते नित्यं समाप्तव्रतमागतम्
कदा द्रक्ष्यामि सीतां च रामं च सहलक्ष्मणम्

sā hi cintayate nityaṁ samāptavratamāgatam
kadā drakṣyāmi sītāṁ ca rāmaṁ ca sahalakṣmaṇam

I do not so much mourn Rama or the mighty car-warrior-Laksmana-or, for that matter, self, as I do the wretched mother-in-law of mine. She ever think of the period of the promise. "When shall I behold Sita and Laksmana with Raghava?

परिदेवयमानां तां राक्षसी त्रिजटाब्रवीत्
मा विषादं कृथा देवि भर्तायं तव जीवति

paridevayamānāṁ tāṁ rākṣasī trijaṭābravīt
mā viṣādaṁ kṛthā devi bhartāyaṁ tava jīvati
As she was thus lamenting, the Raksasai, said, O exalted lady, do not weep thus, your lord live.

कारणानि च वक्ष्यामि महान्ति सदृशानि च
यथेमौ जीवतो देवि भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ

kāraṇāni ca vakṣyāmi mahānti sadṛśāni ca
yathemau jīvato devi bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
O dignified one, I shall unfold to you potent and probable reasons why the brothers Rama and Laksmana live.

न हि कोपपरीतानि हर्षपर्युत्सुकानि च
भवन्ति युधि योधानां मुखानि निहते पतौ

na hi kopaparītāni harṣaparyutsukāni ca
bhavanti yudhi yodhānāṁ mukhāni nihate patau
When their leader fall, the countenances of the warriors in battle are not overspread with passion, or display cheerfulness and vivacity.

इदं विमानं वैदेहि पुष्पकं नाम नामतः
दिव्यं त्वां धारयेन्नेदं यद्येतौ गजजीवितौ

idaṁ vimānaṁ vaidehi puṣpakaṁ nāma nāmataḥ
divyaṁ tvāṁ dhārayennedaṁ yadyetau gajajīvitau
O Vaidehi, if those had lost their lives, this celestial chariot, named Puspaka, would not have held you.

इयं पुनरसंभ्रान्ता निरुद्विग्ना तरस्विनी
सेना रक्षति काकुत्स्थौ मायया निर्जितौ रणे

iyaṁ punarasaṁbhrāntā nirudvignā tarasvinī
senā rakṣati kākutsthau māyayā nirjitau raṇe

An army that has its heroes and chiefs slainbecoming dispirited and drooping, range the field, like a vessel on water that has losi its helmsman. But, O lorm one, these troops, be trying neither agitation nor anxiety, are guarding the Kakutsthas, This I tell you of them out of affection.

सा त्वं भव सुविस्रब्धा अनुमानैः सुखोदयैः
अहतौ पश्य काकुत्स्थौ स्नेहादेतद्ब्रवीमि ते

sā tvaṁ bhava suvisrabdhā anumānaiḥ sukhodayaiḥ
ahatau paśya kākutsthau snehādetadbravīmi te
Do you, at this conclusion bringing in joy, take comfort; and behold the Kakutsthas unslain. This I tell you from affection.

अनृतं नोक्तपूर्वं मे न च वक्ष्ये कदाचन
चारित्रसुखशीलत्वात्प्रविष्टासि मनो मम

anṛtaṁ noktapūrvaṁ me na ca vakṣye kadācana
cāritrasukhaśīlatvātpraviṣṭāsi mano mama
I never told you untruths heretofore; nor, O Mithila's daughter, will I tell them to you now. You by virtue of your character conducive to delight, have found an access into my heart.

नेमौ शक्यौ रणे जेतुं सेन्द्रैरपि सुरासुरैः
एतयोराननं दृष्ट्वा मया चावेदितं तव

nemau śakyau raṇe jetuṁ sendrairapi surāsuraiḥ
etayorānanaṁ dṛṣṭvā mayā cāveditaṁ tava
These even the celestials and Asuras with Indra (at their head) are incompetent to quell. Seeing such sight, I speak to you as to their being alive.

इदं च सुमहच्चिह्नं शनैः पश्यस्व मैथिलि
निःसंज्ञावप्युभावेतौ नैव लक्ष्मीर्वियुज्यते

idaṁ ca sumahaccihnaṁ śanaiḥ paśyasva maithili
niḥsaṁjñāvapyubhāvetau naiva lakṣmīrviyujyate
And behold O Maithili, this mighty wonder! These are lying insensible with arrows; but of these Grace has not taken leave.

प्रायेण गतसत्त्वानां पुरुषाणां गतायुषाम्
दृश्यमानेषु वक्त्रेषु परं भवति वैकृतम्

prāyeṇa gatasattvānāṁ puruṣāṇāṁ gatāyuṣām
dṛśyamāneṣu vaktreṣu paraṁ bhavati vaikṛtam

It generally happens that the faces of persons dead and gone, are unsightly to a degree. Therefore, O Janka's daughter, leave off grief and sorrow and stupor. For the sake of Rama and Laksmana you can not today put a period to your existence.

श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्याः सीता सुरसुतोपमा
कृताञ्जलिरुवाचेदमेवमस्त्विति मैथिली

śrutvā tu vacanaṁ tasyāḥ sītā surasutopamā
kṛtāñjaliruvācedamevamastviti maithilī
Hearing her words, Mithila's daughter-Sitaresembling the daughter of a celestial, with hands joined, said, "May this be so!

विमानं पुष्पकं तत्तु समिवर्त्य मनोजवम्
दीना त्रिजटया सीता लङ्कामेव प्रवेशिता

vimānaṁ puṣpakaṁ tattu samivartya manojavam
dīnā trijaṭayā sītā laṅkāmeva praveśitā
Then turning away the car Puspaka fleet as the mind, the distressed Sita entered Lanka along with Trijata.

ततस्त्रिजटया सार्धं पुष्पकादवरुह्य सा
अशोकवनिकामेव रक्षसीभिः प्रवेशिता

tatastrijaṭayā sārdhaṁ puṣpakādavaruhya sā
aśokavanikāmeva rakṣasībhiḥ praveśitā
Then in company with Trijata alighting from Puspaka, she along with the Raksasis entered the asoka wood.

प्रविश्य सीता बहुवृक्षषण्डां; तां राक्षसेन्द्रस्य विहारभूमिम्
संप्रेक्ष्य संचिन्त्य च राजपुत्रौ; परं विषादं समुपाजगाम

praviśya sītā bahuvṛkṣaṣaṇḍāṁ; tāṁ rākṣasendrasya vihārabhūmim
saṁprekṣya saṁcintya ca rājaputrau; paraṁ viṣādaṁ samupājagāma
Entering that sporting-ground of the Raksasa lord abounding in woody tracts, Sita, having beheld those princes and reflected on them, became subject to a mighty grief.

घोरेण शरबन्धेन बद्धौ दशरथात्मजौ
निश्वसन्तौ यथा नागौ शयानौ रुधिरोक्षितौ

ghoreṇa śarabandhena baddhau daśarathātmajau
niśvasantau yathā nāgau śayānau rudhirokṣitau
Bound up terribly with shafts, Dasaratha's sons, lying down bathed in blood, sighed hard like to serpents.

सर्वे ते वानरश्रेष्ठाः ससुग्रीवा महाबलाः
परिवार्य महात्मानौ तस्थुः शोकपरिप्लुताः

sarve te vānaraśreṣṭhāḥ sasugrīvā mahābalāḥ
parivārya mahātmānau tasthuḥ śokapariplutāḥ
All those foremost monkeys, along with Sugriva, possessed of exceeding strength, overwhelmed with sorrow, remained surrounding those high-souled ones.

एतस्मिन्नन्तेरे रामः प्रत्यबुध्यत वीर्यवान्
स्थिरत्वात्सत्त्वयोगाच्च शरैः संदानितोऽपि सन्

etasminnantere rāmaḥ pratyabudhyata vīryavān
sthiratvātsattvayogācca śaraiḥ saṁdānito'pi san
In the meanwhile, the powerful Rama, albeit fast bound by the shafts, awoke by virtue of the exceeding toughness of his person, as well as his might.

ततो दृष्ट्वा सरुधिरं विषण्णं गाढमर्पितम्
भ्रातरं दीनवदनं पर्यदेवयदातुरः

tato dṛṣṭvā sarudhiraṁ viṣaṇṇaṁ gāḍhamarpitam
bhrātaraṁ dīnavadanaṁ paryadevayadāturaḥ
Then, seeing his brother having a distressful countenance, covered with blood, feeble, and fast bound by the shafts, Rama, greatly aggrieved, began to mourn.

किं नु मे सीतया कार्यं किं कार्यं जीवितेन वा
शयानं योऽद्य पश्यामि भ्रातरं युधि निर्जितम्

kiṁ nu me sītayā kāryaṁ kiṁ kāryaṁ jīvitena vā
śayānaṁ yo'dya paśyāmi bhrātaraṁ yudhi nirjitam
Of what use to me is the recovery of Sita, or life either, when today I see my brother vanquished in fight and lying down in the field?

शक्या सीता समा नारी प्राप्तुं लोके विचिन्वता
न लक्ष्मणसमो भ्राता सचिवः साम्परायिकः

śakyā sītā samā nārī prāptuṁ loke vicinvatā
na lakṣmaṇasamo bhrātā sacivaḥ sāmparāyikaḥ
Seeking in the world (of men), I may light upon a woman like Sita; but never on a brother, or a helper, or a warrior like to Laksmana.

परित्यक्ष्याम्यहं प्राणान्वानराणां तु पश्यताम्
यदि पञ्चत्वमापन्नः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः

parityakṣyāmyahaṁ prāṇānvānarāṇāṁ tu paśyatām
yadi pañcatvamāpannaḥ sumitrānandavardhanaḥ
If that enhancer of Sumitra's joy have met with his end, my life I must renounce in the sight of the monkeys.

किं नु वक्ष्यामि कौसल्यां मातरं किं नु कैकयीम्
कथमम्बां सुमित्रांच पुत्रदर्शनलालसाम्

kiṁ nu vakṣyāmi kausalyāṁ mātaraṁ kiṁ nu kaikayīm
kathamambāṁ sumitrāṁca putradarśanalālasām

What shall I say to Kausalya; and what shall I say to Kaikeyi? And what shall I say to mother Sumitra eager for a sight of her son? And if I go (back) without him, how shall I soothe her, like to a cow reft of her calf; and trembling; and resembling a mourning Kurari?

कथं वक्ष्यामि शत्रुघ्नं भरतं च यशस्विनम्
मया सह वनं यातो विना तेनागतः पुनः

kathaṁ vakṣyāmi śatrughnaṁ bharataṁ ca yaśasvinam
mayā saha vanaṁ yāto vinā tenāgataḥ punaḥ
How shall I say to Satrughna and the illustrious Bharata, 'He went with me to the forest; but I come (back) here without him "?

उपालम्भं न शक्ष्यामि सोढुं बत सुमित्रया
इहैव देहं त्यक्ष्यामि न हि जीवितुमुत्सहे

upālambhaṁ na śakṣyāmi soḍhuṁ bata sumitrayā
ihaiva dehaṁ tyakṣyāmi na hi jīvitumutsahe
I shall not be able to bear the rebuke of mother Sumitra. Therefore even here shall I renounce my person; for certainly I dare not live.

धिङ्मां दुष्कृतकर्माणमनार्यं यत्कृते ह्यसौ
लक्ष्मणः पतितः शेते शरतल्पे गतासुवत्

dhiṅmāṁ duṣkṛtakarmāṇamanāryaṁ yatkṛte hyasau
lakṣmaṇaḥ patitaḥ śete śaratalpe gatāsuvat
Fie on me, who am wicked and base; for me this Laksmana, brought down, leith in the field of battle, like one that is without life.

त्वं नित्यं सुविषण्णं मामाश्वासयसि लक्ष्मण
गतासुर्नाद्य शक्नोषि मामार्तमभिभाषितुम्

tvaṁ nityaṁ suviṣaṇṇaṁ māmāśvāsayasi lakṣmaṇa
gatāsurnādya śaknoṣi māmārtamabhibhāṣitum
O Laksmana, you ever comforts me when I am dispirited. But today, having lost your life, you can not speak to me, who am afflicted.

येनाद्य बहवो युद्धे राक्षसा निहताः क्षितौ
तस्यामेव क्षितौ वीरः स शेते निहतः परैः

yenādya bahavo yuddhe rākṣasā nihatāḥ kṣitau
tasyāmeva kṣitau vīraḥ sa śete nihataḥ paraiḥ
You, O hero, who had in battle slain innumerable Raksasa lying around, have (at length) yourself been slain in the field with shafts.

शयानः शरतल्पेऽस्मिन्स्वशोणितपरिप्लुतः
शरजालैश्चितो भाति भास्करोऽस्तमिव व्रजन्

śayānaḥ śaratalpe'sminsvaśoṇitapariplutaḥ
śarajālaiścito bhāti bhāskaro'stamiva vrajan
And lying down in the battle-field, bleeding and covered with arrows, you appear like the Sun when he has gone up the Setting-hill.

बाणाभिहतमर्मत्वान्न शक्नोत्यभिवीक्षितुम्
रुजा चाब्रुवतो ह्यस्य दृष्टिरागेण सूच्यते

bāṇābhihatamarmatvānna śaknotyabhivīkṣitum
rujā cābruvato hyasya dṛṣṭirāgeṇa sūcyate
In consequence of shafts piercing your vitals, you cannot speak; but your visible expression, albeit you are dumb, betokens pain.

यथैव मां वनं यान्तमनुयातो महाद्युतिः
अहमप्यनुयास्यामि तथैवैनं यमक्षयम्

yathaiva māṁ vanaṁ yāntamanuyāto mahādyutiḥ
ahamapyanuyāsyāmi tathaivainaṁ yamakṣayam
O you endowed with exceeding splendour, even as you did follow me into the forest, will I follow you to the mansion of Yama.

इष्टबन्धुजनो नित्यं मां च नित्यमनुव्रतः
इमामद्य गतोऽवस्थां ममानार्यस्य दुर्नयैः

iṣṭabandhujano nityaṁ māṁ ca nityamanuvrataḥ
imāmadya gato'vasthāṁ mamānāryasya durnayaiḥ
You having dear friends, and ever following me, has come by this plight in consequence of my reprehensible conduct.

सुरुष्टेनापि वीरेण लक्ष्मणेना न संस्मरे
परुषं विप्रियं वापि श्रावितं न कदाचन

suruṣṭenāpi vīreṇa lakṣmaṇenā na saṁsmare
paruṣaṁ vipriyaṁ vāpi śrāvitaṁ na kadācana
I do not remember having heard any harsh speech from the heroic Laksmana, even when he had happened to be exceedingly wroth.

विससर्जैकवेगेन पञ्चबाणशतानि यः
इष्वस्त्रेष्वधिकस्तस्मात्कार्तवीर्याच्च लक्ष्मणः

visasarjaikavegena pañcabāṇaśatāni yaḥ
iṣvastreṣvadhikastasmātkārtavīryācca lakṣmaṇaḥ
He that could discharge at one shot five hundred shafts, that Laksmana is superior to karttaviryya himself in that weapon-the bow.

अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि यो हन्याच्छक्रस्यापि महात्मनः
सोऽयमुर्व्यांहतः शेते महार्हशयनोचितः

astrairastrāṇi yo hanyācchakrasyāpi mahātmanaḥ
so'yamurvyāṁhataḥ śete mahārhaśayanocitaḥ
He that with his arms could resist the arms of Sakra himself, that one worthy of a costly couchLeith down on the ground, slain.

तच्च मिथ्या प्रलप्तं मां प्रधक्ष्यति न संशयः
यन्मया न कृतो राजा राक्षसानां विभीषणः

tacca mithyā pralaptaṁ māṁ pradhakṣyati na saṁśayaḥ
yanmayā na kṛto rājā rākṣasānāṁ vibhīṣaṇaḥ
That false babble shall now, without doubt, consume me; for by me has not Bibhishna been made monarch of the Raksasas.

अस्मिन्मुहूर्ते सुग्रीव प्रतियातुमितोऽर्हसि
मत्वा हीनं मया राजन्रावणोऽभिद्रवेद्बली

asminmuhūrte sugrīva pratiyātumito'rhasi
matvā hīnaṁ mayā rājanrāvaṇo'bhidravedbalī
Do you, O Sugriva, this very moment retrace your steps. Bereft of your strength through me you will be worsted by Ravana.

अङ्गदं तु पुरस्कृत्य ससैन्यः ससुहृज्जनः
सागरं तर सुग्रीव पुनस्तेनैव सेतुना

aṅgadaṁ tu puraskṛtya sasainyaḥ sasuhṛjjanaḥ
sāgaraṁ tara sugrīva punastenaiva setunā
O Sugriva, placing Angada to the fore, do you, taking your host as well as the equipage, in company with Nila and Nala, cross over the Ocean.

अङ्गदेन कृतं कर्म मैन्देन द्विविदेन च
युद्धं केसरिणा संख्ये घोरं संपातिना कृतम्

aṅgadena kṛtaṁ karma maindena dvividena ca
yuddhaṁ kesariṇā saṁkhye ghoraṁ saṁpātinā kṛtam

By you has been achieved a mighty feat incapable of being done by another in battle. And pleased am I with the king of bears, and the lord of Golangulas; and Angada has quit himself nobly, as also Mainda and Dvivida. And Kesarin and Sampati have both faught terribly.

गवयेन गवाक्षेण शरभेण गजेन च
अन्यैश्च हरिभिर्युद्धं मदार्थे त्यक्तजीवितैः

gavayena gavākṣeṇa śarabheṇa gajena ca
anyaiśca haribhiryuddhaṁ madārthe tyaktajīvitaiḥ
Gavaya, and Gavaksa, and Sarabha, and Gaja, and other monkeys have faught as others are incapable of fighting, determined to lay down their lives (for me).

न चातिक्रमितुं शक्यं दैवं सुग्रीव मानुषैः
यत्तु शक्यं वयस्येन सुहृदा वा परंतप
कृतं सुग्रीव तत्सर्वं भवताधर्मभीरुणा

na cātikramituṁ śakyaṁ daivaṁ sugrīva mānuṣaiḥ
yattu śakyaṁ vayasyena suhṛdā vā paraṁtapa
kṛtaṁ sugrīva tatsarvaṁ bhavatādharmabhīruṇā

But, O Sugriva, man cannot overrule Destiny. You, my friend, fearing righteousness, has done what lay in your power. And, You foremost of monkeys, you also have acted as become friends. Now, with my permission, go you whitersoever you are minded.

शुश्रुवुस्तस्य ते सर्वे वानराः परिदेवितम्
वर्तयां चक्रुरश्रूणि नेत्रैः कृष्णेतरेक्षणाः

śuśruvustasya te sarve vānarāḥ paridevitam
vartayāṁ cakruraśrūṇi netraiḥ kṛṣṇetarekṣaṇāḥ
Hearing Rama's lament, the monkeys-those dark-eyed and others-began to shed tears from their eyes.

ततः सर्वाण्यनीकानि स्थापयित्वा विभीषणः
आजगाम गदापाणिस्त्वरितो यत्र राघवः

tataḥ sarvāṇyanīkāni sthāpayitvā vibhīṣaṇaḥ
ājagāma gadāpāṇistvarito yatra rāghavaḥ
Then Vibhisana, quieting the army, taking a mace in his hand, swiftly went to where Raghava was.

तं दृष्ट्वा त्वरितं यान्तं नीलाञ्जनचयोपमम्
वानरा दुद्रुवुः सर्वे मन्यमानास्तु रावणिम्

taṁ dṛṣṭvā tvaritaṁ yāntaṁ nīlāñjanacayopamam
vānarā dudruvuḥ sarve manyamānāstu rāvaṇim
Seeing him fast making his way, resembling a mass of dark collyrium, the monkeys taking him to be Ravana's son, began to run away.

अथोवाच महातेजा हरिराजो महाबलः
किमियं व्यथिता सेना मूढवातेव नौर्जले

athovāca mahātejā harirājo mahābalaḥ
kimiyaṁ vyathitā senā mūḍhavāteva naurjale
Then out spoke the highly energetic and exceedingly mighty king of monkeys, “Why is this host agitated like a bark driven hither and thither by the wind?"

सुग्रीवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा वालिपुत्रोऽङ्गदोऽब्रवीत्
न त्वं पश्यसि रामं च लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्

sugrīvasya vacaḥ śrutvā vāliputro'ṅgado'bravīt
na tvaṁ paśyasi rāmaṁ ca lakṣmaṇaṁ ca mahābalam
Hearing Sugriva's speech, Vali's son said, Did you not see both those heroes-sons of Dasaratha, Rama and that mighty car-warriorLaksmana-covered with arrows?

शरजालाचितौ वीरावुभौ दशरथात्मजौ
शरतल्पे महात्मानौ शयानौ रुधिरोक्षितौ

śarajālācitau vīrāvubhau daśarathātmajau
śaratalpe mahātmānau śayānau rudhirokṣitau
And (did you not see) those high-should ones lying in the field of battle, covered with blood?

अथाब्रवीद्वानरेन्द्रः सुग्रीवः पुत्रमङ्गदम्
नानिमित्तमिदं मन्ये भवितव्यं भयेन तु

athābravīdvānarendraḥ sugrīvaḥ putramaṅgadam
nānimittamidaṁ manye bhavitavyaṁ bhayena tu
Thereat, the lord of monkeys, Sugriva, spoke to his son, Angada "I do not deem it without cause. This may have come to pass through sheer fear.

विषण्णवदना ह्येते त्यक्तप्रहरणा दिशः
प्रपलायन्ति हरयस्त्रासादुत्फुल्ललोचनाः

viṣaṇṇavadanā hyete tyaktapraharaṇā diśaḥ
prapalāyanti harayastrāsādutphullalocanāḥ
These monkeys with sad faces, leaving their arms behind them are flying in all directions, their eyes distended in affright.

अन्योन्यस्य न लज्जन्ते न निरीक्षन्ति पृष्ठतः
विप्रकर्षन्ति चान्योन्यं पतितं लङ्घयन्ति च

anyonyasya na lajjante na nirīkṣanti pṛṣṭhataḥ
viprakarṣanti cānyonyaṁ patitaṁ laṅghayanti ca
They are not ashamed of each other, and they do not cast their looks back. And they hug each other, and go leaping over the fallen.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरो गदापाणिर्विभीषणः
सुग्रीवं वर्धयामास राघवं च निरैक्षत

etasminnantare vīro gadāpāṇirvibhīṣaṇaḥ
sugrīvaṁ vardhayāmāsa rāghavaṁ ca niraikṣata
In the meanwhile that hero, Vibhisana, bearing a mace in his hand, (approaching) greeted Sugriva as well as Raghava with blessings of victory.

विभीषणं तं सुग्रीवो दृष्ट्वा वानरभीषणम्
ऋक्षराजं समीपस्थं जाम्बवन्तमुवाच ह

vibhīṣaṇaṁ taṁ sugrīvo dṛṣṭvā vānarabhīṣaṇam
ṛkṣarājaṁ samīpasthaṁ jāmbavantamuvāca ha
And Sugriva, seeing Vibhisana, capable of inspiring fear in the monkeys, spoke to the highsouled sovereign of bears, who stood by.

विभीषणोऽयं संप्राप्तो यं दृष्ट्वा वानरर्षभाः
विद्रवन्ति परित्रस्ता रावणात्मजशङ्कया

vibhīṣaṇo'yaṁ saṁprāpto yaṁ dṛṣṭvā vānararṣabhāḥ
vidravanti paritrastā rāvaṇātmajaśaṅkayā
This is Vibhisana that has come hither, seeing whom the foremost among the monkeys, from fear of Ravana's son who, they apprehend, he is, are fleeing away, seized with a panic.

शीघ्रमेतान्सुवित्रस्तान्बहुधा विप्रधावितान्
पर्यवस्थापयाख्याहि विभीषणमुपस्थितम्

śīghrametānsuvitrastānbahudhā vipradhāvitān
paryavasthāpayākhyāhi vibhīṣaṇamupasthitam
Do you at once stay these agitated with fear and scampering all around; and proclaim, 'This is Vibhisana, who has come here.'

सुग्रीवेणैवमुक्तस्तु जाम्बवानृक्षपार्थिवः
वानरान्सान्त्वयामास संनिवर्त्य प्रहावतः

sugrīveṇaivamuktastu jāmbavānṛkṣapārthivaḥ
vānarānsāntvayāmāsa saṁnivartya prahāvataḥ
Thus directed, Jombavan-king of bearsrestraining those that were flying, composed the monkeys.

ते निवृत्ताः पुनः सर्वे वानरास्त्यक्तसंभ्रमाः
ऋक्षराजवचः श्रुत्वा तं च दृष्ट्वा विभीषणम्

te nivṛttāḥ punaḥ sarve vānarāstyaktasaṁbhramāḥ
ṛkṣarājavacaḥ śrutvā taṁ ca dṛṣṭvā vibhīṣaṇam
Hearing the bear-king's words, and seeing Vibhisana, the monkeys, renouncing fear, desisted (from their flight).

विभीषणस्तु रामस्य दृष्ट्वा गात्रं शरैश्चितम्
लक्ष्मणस्य च धर्मात्मा बभूव व्यथितेन्द्रियः

vibhīṣaṇastu rāmasya dṛṣṭvā gātraṁ śaraiścitam
lakṣmaṇasya ca dharmātmā babhūva vyathitendriyaḥ
Then the righteous Vibhisana, viewing Rama's as well as Laksmana's body pierced with arrows, was exceedingly aggrieved.

जलक्लिन्नेन हस्तेन तयोर्नेत्रे प्रमृज्य च
शोकसंपीडितमना रुरोद विललाप च

jalaklinnena hastena tayornetre pramṛjya ca
śokasaṁpīḍitamanā ruroda vilalāpa ca
Washing their eyes with water, he, with his mind overpowered with grief, began to weep and broke out into lamentation.

इमौ तौ सत्त्वसंपन्नौ विक्रान्तौ प्रियसंयुगौ
इमामवस्थां गमितौ राकसैः कूटयोधिभिः

imau tau sattvasaṁpannau vikrāntau priyasaṁyugau
imāmavasthāṁ gamitau rākasaiḥ kūṭayodhibhiḥ
The Raksasas, fighting in wily ways, have brought to this pass these ones endowed with prowess and possessed of every perfection and gifted with might (of arm).

भ्रातुः पुत्रेण मे तेन दुष्पुत्रेण दुरात्मना
राक्षस्या जिह्मया बुद्ध्या छलितावृजुविक्रमौ

bhrātuḥ putreṇa me tena duṣputreṇa durātmanā
rākṣasyā jihmayā buddhyā chalitāvṛjuvikramau
And with his guileful mind, that brother's son of mine, wicked-souled and an evil son (to me), has deceived these ones of straight prowess.

शरैरिमावलं विद्धौ रुधिरेण समुक्षितौ
वसुधायामिम सुप्तौ दृश्येते शल्यकाविव

śarairimāvalaṁ viddhau rudhireṇa samukṣitau
vasudhāyāmima suptau dṛśyete śalyakāviva
Pierced with innumerable shafts, and covered with blood, these are lying on the ground like Salyakas.

ययोर्वीर्यमुपाश्रित्य प्रतिष्ठा काङ्क्षिता मया
तावुभौ देहनाशाय प्रसुप्तौ पुरुषर्षभौ

yayorvīryamupāśritya pratiṣṭhā kāṅkṣitā mayā
tāvubhau dehanāśāya prasuptau puruṣarṣabhau
Those depending on whose prowess, I had sought eminence, those foremost of men, sleep here soundly for renouncing their bodies.

जीवन्नद्य विपन्नोऽस्मि नष्टराज्यमनोरथः
प्राप्तप्रतिज्ञश्च रिपुः सकामो रावणः कृतः

jīvannadya vipanno'smi naṣṭarājyamanorathaḥ
prāptapratijñaśca ripuḥ sakāmo rāvaṇaḥ kṛtaḥ
Living, today I am in distress: and my desire of dominion is annihilated; and my foe, Ravana, has his promise fulfilled and his aim crowned with success.

एवं विलपमानं तं परिष्वज्य विभीषणम्
सुग्रीवः सत्त्वसंपन्नो हरिराजोऽब्रवीदिदम्

evaṁ vilapamānaṁ taṁ pariṣvajya vibhīṣaṇam
sugrīvaḥ sattvasaṁpanno harirājo'bravīdidam
As Vibhisana was thus lamenting, the lord of monkeys-Sugriva-endowed with strength, embracing him spoke to him.

राज्यं प्राप्स्यसि धर्मज्ञ लङ्कायां नात्र संशयः
रावणः सह पुत्रेण स राज्यं नेह लप्स्यते

rājyaṁ prāpsyasi dharmajña laṅkāyāṁ nātra saṁśayaḥ
rāvaṇaḥ saha putreṇa sa rājyaṁ neha lapsyate
O you cognisant of righteousness, you will here in Lanka obtain empire: no doubt of this; and Ravana along with his sons will be disappointed in their expectations.

शरसंपीडितावेतावुभौ राघवलक्ष्मणौ
त्यक्त्वा मोहं वधिष्येते सगणं रावणं रणे

śarasaṁpīḍitāvetāvubhau rāghavalakṣmaṇau
tyaktvā mohaṁ vadhiṣyete sagaṇaṁ rāvaṇaṁ raṇe
Both these-Rama and Laksmana-are under the aegis of Garuda; and, casting off their stupor: they will in battle slay Ravana along with his adherents.

तमेवं सान्त्वयित्वा तु समाश्वास्य च राक्षसं
सुषेणं श्वशुरं पार्श्वे सुग्रीवस्तमुवाच ह

tamevaṁ sāntvayitvā tu samāśvāsya ca rākṣasaṁ
suṣeṇaṁ śvaśuraṁ pārśve sugrīvastamuvāca ha
Having thus soothed and comforted the Raksasa, Sugriva addressed his father-in-law, who was at his side, saying.

सह शूरैर्हरिगणैर्लब्धसंज्ञावरिंदमौ
गच्छ त्वं भ्रातरौ गृह्य किष्किन्धां रामलक्ष्मणौ

saha śūrairharigaṇairlabdhasaṁjñāvariṁdamau
gaccha tvaṁ bhrātarau gṛhya kiṣkindhāṁ rāmalakṣmaṇau
Do you along with numbers of heroic monkeys, taking those repressors of foes, the brothers-Rama and Laksmana-when they shall have regained their consciousness, repair to Kiskindha.

अहं तु रावणं हत्वा सपुत्रं सहबान्धवम्
मैथिलीमानयिष्यामि शक्रो नष्टामिव श्रियम्

ahaṁ tu rāvaṇaṁ hatvā saputraṁ sahabāndhavam
maithilīmānayiṣyāmi śakro naṣṭāmiva śriyam
And I, slaying Ravana along with his sons and friends, shall bring back Mithila's daughter, even as Sakra recovered the lost Sri.

श्रुत्वैतद्वानरेन्द्रस्य सुषेणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
देवासुरं महायुद्धमनुभूतं सुदारुणम्

śrutvaitadvānarendrasya suṣeṇo vākyamabravīt
devāsuraṁ mahāyuddhamanubhūtaṁ sudāruṇam
Hearing the words of the monkey-king, Susena said, I had witnessed the war of yore between the gods and the Asuras.

तदा स्म दानवा देवाञ्शरसंस्पर्शकोविदाः
निजघ्नुः शस्त्रविदुषश्छादयन्तो मुहुर्मुहुः

tadā sma dānavā devāñśarasaṁsparśakovidāḥ
nijaghnuḥ śastraviduṣaśchādayanto muhurmuhuḥ
Then the Danavas, enveloping themselves, momentarily destroyed the deities, albeit versed in arms and accomplished in weapons.

तानार्तान्नष्टसंज्ञांश्च परासूंश्च बृहस्पतिः
विध्याभिर्मन्त्रयुक्ताभिरोषधीभिश्चिकित्सति

tānārtānnaṣṭasaṁjñāṁśca parāsūṁśca bṛhaspatiḥ
vidhyābhirmantrayuktābhiroṣadhībhiścikitsati
They, their senses lost, and their lives departed, Bihaspati treated by means of his knowledge of mantras, as well with medicines.

तान्यौषधान्यानयितुं क्षीरोदं यान्तु सागरम्
जवेन वानराः शीघ्रं संपाति पनसादयः

tānyauṣadhānyānayituṁ kṣīrodaṁ yāntu sāgaram
javena vānarāḥ śīghraṁ saṁpāti panasādayaḥ
Let Sampati, Panasa, and other monkeys speedily hie to the Milky Ocean for the purpose of bringing those medicines.

हरयस्तु विजानन्ति पार्वती ते महौषधी
संजीवकरणीं दिव्यां विशल्यां देवनिर्मिताम्

harayastu vijānanti pārvatī te mahauṣadhī
saṁjīvakaraṇīṁ divyāṁ viśalyāṁ devanirmitām
The monkeys well know that mighty mountainous medicine-divine and capable of reviving the dead, and made by the deities themselves-visalya.

चन्द्रश्च नाम द्रोणश्च पर्वतौ सागरोत्तमे
अमृतं यत्र मथितं तत्र ते परमौषधी

candraśca nāma droṇaśca parvatau sāgarottame
amṛtaṁ yatra mathitaṁ tatra te paramauṣadhī

There are (the mountains) named Candra and Drona: where the ambrosia was churned, there is that supreme drug. And those mountains have been placed by the deities in the mighty deep. And, o king, let the son of the Wing-god go thither.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वायुर्मेघांश्चापि सविद्युतः
पर्यस्यन्सागरे तोयं कम्पयन्निव पर्वतान्

etasminnantare vāyurmeghāṁścāpi savidyutaḥ
paryasyansāgare toyaṁ kampayanniva parvatān
In the meanwhile, the wing arose, and masses of clouds appeared along with lightning, and the wind blew, agitating the waters of the deep, and shaking the mountains.

महता पक्षवातेन सर्वे द्वीपमहाद्रुमाः
निपेतुर्भग्नविटपाः समूला लवणाम्भसि

mahatā pakṣavātena sarve dvīpamahādrumāḥ
nipeturbhagnaviṭapāḥ samūlā lavaṇāmbhasi
And mighty trees of the ocean-islands, broken down by-the terrible wing-raised wind, began to topple headlong into the salt waters.

अभवन्पन्नगास्त्रस्ता भोगिनस्तत्रवासिनः
शीघ्रं सर्वाणि यादांसि जग्मुश्च लवणार्णवम्

abhavanpannagāstrastā bhoginastatravāsinaḥ
śīghraṁ sarvāṇi yādāṁsi jagmuśca lavaṇārṇavam
The serpents dwelling there were seized with affright; and speedily all the aquatic animals dived into the Salt sea,

ततो मुहूर्तद्गरुडं वैनतेयं महाबलम्
वानरा ददृशुः सर्वे ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्

tato muhūrtadgaruḍaṁ vainateyaṁ mahābalam
vānarā dadṛśuḥ sarve jvalantamiva pāvakam
Then in a moment the monkeys saw Vinata's son possessed of terrific strength, like to a flaming fire.

तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य नागास्ते विप्रदुद्रुवुः
यैस्तौ सत्पुरुषौ बद्धौ शरभूतैर्महाबलौ

tamāgatamabhiprekṣya nāgāste vipradudruvuḥ
yaistau satpuruṣau baddhau śarabhūtairmahābalau
Seeing him come, the serpents began to dart away, those exceedingly powerful ones that, turning into shafts, had bound those persons.* *Rama and Laksmana.

ततः सुपर्णः काकुत्स्थौ दृष्ट्वा प्रत्यभिनन्द्य च
विममर्श च पाणिभ्यां मुखे चन्द्रसमप्रभे

tataḥ suparṇaḥ kākutsthau dṛṣṭvā pratyabhinandya ca
vimamarśa ca pāṇibhyāṁ mukhe candrasamaprabhe
Then, touching the Kakutsthas and saluting them, Suparna rubbed with his hands their countenances furnished with the splendour of the Moon.

वैनतेयेन संस्पृष्टास्तयोः संरुरुहुर्व्रणाः
सुवर्णे च तनू स्निग्धे तयोराशु बभूवतुः

vainateyena saṁspṛṣṭāstayoḥ saṁruruhurvraṇāḥ
suvarṇe ca tanū snigdhe tayorāśu babhūvatuḥ
Their wounds, on being touched by Vinata's son, were (immediately) healed: and the bodies of both speedily became cool and shone with an excellent complexion.

तेजो वीर्यं बलं चौज उत्साहश्च महागुणाः
प्रदर्शनं च बुद्धिश्च स्मृतिश्च द्विगुणं तयोः

tejo vīryaṁ balaṁ cauja utsāhaśca mahāguṇāḥ
pradarśanaṁ ca buddhiśca smṛtiśca dviguṇaṁ tayoḥ
They attained immense energy and prowess; and a double share of strength, and of rational and perceptive powers, and of memory.

तावुत्थाप्य महावीर्यौ गरुडो वासवोपमौ
उभौ तौ सस्वजे हृष्टौ रामश्चैनमुवाच ह

tāvutthāpya mahāvīryau garuḍo vāsavopamau
ubhau tau sasvaje hṛṣṭau rāmaścainamuvāca ha
Then raising them up, the exceedingly energetic Garuda, resembling Vasava himself, embraced both joyfully. And then Rama addressed (Garuda), saying.

भवत्प्रसादाद्व्यसनं रावणिप्रभवं महत्
आवामिह व्यतिक्रान्तौ शीघ्रं च बलिनौ कृतौ

bhavatprasādādvyasanaṁ rāvaṇiprabhavaṁ mahat
āvāmiha vyatikrāntau śīghraṁ ca balinau kṛtau
By your grace we have through means survived the mighty calamity that had sprung from Ravana's son; and we have also speedily been rendered strong.

यथा तातं दशरथं यथाजं च पितामहम्
तथा भवन्तमासाद्य हृषयं मे प्रसीदति

yathā tātaṁ daśarathaṁ yathājaṁ ca pitāmaham
tathā bhavantamāsādya hṛṣayaṁ me prasīdati
My heart is delighted on having these, like to my father, Dasaratha, or my grand sire, Aja.

को भवान्रूपसंपन्नो दिव्यस्रगनुलेपनः
वसानो विरजे वस्त्रे दिव्याभरणभूषितः

ko bhavānrūpasaṁpanno divyasraganulepanaḥ
vasāno viraje vastre divyābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ
Who are your, furnished with beauty, and bearing wreaths and unguents (on your person); clad in stainless attire: and adorned in noble ornaments?

तमुवाच महातेजा वैनतेयो महाबलः
पतत्रिराजः प्रीतात्मा हर्षपर्याकुलेक्षणः

tamuvāca mahātejā vainateyo mahābalaḥ
patatrirājaḥ prītātmā harṣaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ
To him spoke the exceedingly energetic son of Vinata endowed with great strength, the lord of birds, with a pleased heart, and his eyes wild with glee.

अहं सखा ते काकुत्स्थ प्रियः प्राणो बहिश्चरः
गरुत्मानिह संप्राप्तो युवयोः साह्यकारणात्

ahaṁ sakhā te kākutstha priyaḥ prāṇo bahiścaraḥ
garutmāniha saṁprāpto yuvayoḥ sāhyakāraṇāt
O Kakutstha, I am your friend-your life ranging externally-Garutman. I am come hither for aiding you.

सभाग्यश्चासि धर्मज्ञ राम सत्यपराक्रम
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा समरे रिपुघातिना

sabhāgyaścāsi dharmajña rāma satyaparākrama
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā samare ripughātinā
O Rama having truth for prowess, you are fortunate-along with that destroyer of foe in fight, Laksmana.

इमं श्रुत्वा तु वृत्तान्तं त्वरमाणोऽहमागतः
सहसा युवयोः स्नेहात्सखित्वमनुपालयन्

imaṁ śrutvā tu vṛttāntaṁ tvaramāṇo'hamāgataḥ
sahasā yuvayoḥ snehātsakhitvamanupālayan
Hearing this, I, summoning energy: have come hither swiftly, and I, doing by you as a friend, have from affection at once set you free from these dreadful arrowy bonds.

प्रकृत्या राक्षसाः सर्वे संग्रामे कूटयोधिनः
शूराणां शुद्धभावानां भवतामार्जवं बलम्

prakṛtyā rākṣasāḥ sarve saṁgrāme kūṭayodhinaḥ
śūrāṇāṁ śuddhabhāvānāṁ bhavatāmārjavaṁ balam
you should always be on your guard. By nature the Raksasas have cunning shifts in fight and you, who are heroic and of a pure spirit, can but rely on your simplicity alone for strength.

तन्न विश्वसितव्यं वो राक्षसानां रणाजिरे
एतेनैवोपमानेन नित्यजिह्मा हि राक्षसाः

tanna viśvasitavyaṁ vo rākṣasānāṁ raṇājire
etenaivopamānena nityajihmā hi rākṣasāḥ
Therefore you must not trust the Raksasas in the field of battle. By this one instance you must know that Raksasas are ever deceitful in fight.

एवमुक्त्वा ततो रामं सुपर्णः सुमहाबलः
परिष्वज्य सुहृत्स्निग्धमाप्रष्टुमुपचक्रमे

evamuktvā tato rāmaṁ suparṇaḥ sumahābalaḥ
pariṣvajya suhṛtsnigdhamāpraṣṭumupacakrame
Having said this the wondrous mighty Suparna, embracing Rama tenderly again) said.

सखे राघव धर्मज्ञ रिपूणामपि वत्सल
अभ्यनुज्ञातुमिच्छामि गमिष्यामि यथागतम्

sakhe rāghava dharmajña ripūṇāmapi vatsala
abhyanujñātumicchāmi gamiṣyāmi yathāgatam

My friend Raghava, O you who even cherish affection for your foes, permit me, I shall go at pleasure. And O Raghva, entertain no curiosity as to our friendship. when, O hero, you shall have achieved success in battle, you shall know all about this friendship of ours.

बालवृद्धावशेषां तु लङ्कां कृत्वा शरोर्मिभिः
रावणं च रिपुं हत्वा सीतां समुपलप्स्यसे

bālavṛddhāvaśeṣāṁ tu laṅkāṁ kṛtvā śarormibhiḥ
rāvaṇaṁ ca ripuṁ hatvā sītāṁ samupalapsyase
And with the surges of your shafts, making Larka contain only children and aged, and slaying your foe, Ravana, you shall recover Sita.

प्रदक्षिणं ततः कृत्वा परिष्वज्य च वीर्यवान्
जगामाकाशमाविश्य सुपर्णः पवनो यथा

pradakṣiṇaṁ tataḥ kṛtvā pariṣvajya ca vīryavān
jagāmākāśamāviśya suparṇaḥ pavano yathā

Having spoken thus, Suparna, endowed with vigour, having rendered Rama hale in the midst of the monkeys, having gone round them and embrace them also, that one possessed of prowess, set out, covering up the sky, like to the wind.

विरुजौ राघवौ दृष्ट्वा ततो वानरयूथपाः
सिंहनादांस्तदा नेदुर्लाङ्गूलं दुधुवुश्च ते

virujau rāghavau dṛṣṭvā tato vānarayūthapāḥ
siṁhanādāṁstadā nedurlāṅgūlaṁ dudhuvuśca te
Seeing Raghu's sons rendered hale, the monkey-leaders set up leonine roars, and began to flourish their tails.

ततो भेरीः समाजघ्नुर्मृदङ्गांश्च व्यनादयन्
दध्मुः शङ्खान्संप्रहृष्टाः क्ष्वेलन्त्यपि यथापुरम्

tato bherīḥ samājaghnurmṛdaṅgāṁśca vyanādayan
dadhmuḥ śaṅkhānsaṁprahṛṣṭāḥ kṣvelantyapi yathāpuram
Then beat the kettle-drums and the drums struck up. And conchs were cheerfully blown; and shouts were sent.

विसृजन्तो महानादांस्त्रासयन्तो निशाचरान्
लङ्काद्वाराण्युपाजग्मुर्योद्धुकामाः प्लवंगमाः

visṛjanto mahānādāṁstrāsayanto niśācarān
laṅkādvārāṇyupājagmuryoddhukāmāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ

And others struck at their arms with their hands. The monkeys, accustomed to battle with trees, uprooting them, stood by hundreds and thousands. And emitting tremendous roars and thereby frightening the night-rangers, the monkeys eager for encounter, approached the gate of Lanka.

ततस्तु भीमस्तुमुलो निनादो; बभूव शाखामृगयूथपानाम्
क्षये निदाघस्य यथा घनानां; नादः सुभीमो नदतां निशीथे

tatastu bhīmastumulo ninādo; babhūva śākhāmṛgayūthapānām
kṣaye nidāghasya yathā ghanānāṁ; nādaḥ subhīmo nadatāṁ niśīthe
That mighty and dreadful din raised by the monkeys, resembled the terrible rumbling of the clouds at midnight about the end of Summer.

तेषां सुतुमुलं शब्दं वानराणां तरस्विनाम्
नर्दतां राक्षसैः सार्धं तदा शुश्राव रावणः

teṣāṁ sutumulaṁ śabdaṁ vānarāṇāṁ tarasvinām
nardatāṁ rākṣasaiḥ sārdhaṁ tadā śuśrāva rāvaṇaḥ
Then Ravana heard the tumult raised by the highly energetic monkeys roaring in company with the Raksasas.

स्निग्धगम्भीरनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा स निनदं भृशम्
सचिवानां ततस्तेषां मध्ये वचनमब्रवीत्

snigdhagambhīranirghoṣaṁ śrutvā sa ninadaṁ bhṛśam
sacivānāṁ tatasteṣāṁ madhye vacanamabravīt
Hearing that low and solemn noise-that prodigious uproar-Ravana said in the midst of his counsellors.

यथासौ संप्रहृष्टानां वानराणां समुत्थितः
बहूनां सुमहान्नादो मेघानामिव गर्जताम्

yathāsau saṁprahṛṣṭānāṁ vānarāṇāṁ samutthitaḥ
bahūnāṁ sumahānnādo meghānāmiva garjatām

From mighty roars that are heard of in innumerous delighted monkeys, resembling the roar of couds, it is evident, beyond a doubt, that there is great rejoicing there. And the salt Ocean is vexed with these thundering noises.

तौ तु बद्धौ शरैस्तीष्क्णैर्भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
अयं च सुमहान्नादः शङ्कां जनयतीव मे

tau tu baddhau śaraistīṣkṇairbhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
ayaṁ ca sumahānnādaḥ śaṅkāṁ janayatīva me
The brother-Rama and Laksmana-have been fast bound with sharp shafts, and here this uproar is exciting my alarm.

एतत्तु वचनं चोक्त्वा मन्त्रिणो राक्षसेश्वरः
उवाच नैरृतांस्तत्र समीपपरिवर्तिनः

etattu vacanaṁ coktvā mantriṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
uvāca nairṛtāṁstatra samīpaparivartinaḥ
Having spoken thus to his ministers, the lord of the Raksasas addressed the Naistas present there, saying.

ज्ञायतां तूर्णमेतषां सर्वेषां वनचारिणाम्
शोककाले समुत्पन्ने हर्षकारणमुत्थितम्

jñāyatāṁ tūrṇametaṣāṁ sarveṣāṁ vanacāriṇām
śokakāle samutpanne harṣakāraṇamutthitam
Do you speedily acquaint yourselves with the cause of rejoicing that has arisen of these monkeys on this mournful occasion.

तथोक्तास्तेन संभ्रान्ताः प्राकारमधिरुह्य ते
ददृशुः पालितां सेनां सुग्रीवेण महात्मना

tathoktāstena saṁbhrāntāḥ prākāramadhiruhya te
dadṛśuḥ pālitāṁ senāṁ sugrīveṇa mahātmanā

Thus accosted, they hurriedly mounting up on the wall, surveyed the forces maintained by the high-souled Sugriva as well as those exalted ones-Raghu's sons-emancipated from their terrific arrowy fetters and arisen (now).

संत्रस्तहृदया सर्वे प्राकारादवरुह्य ते
विषण्णवदनाः सर्वे राक्षसेन्द्रमुपस्थिताः

saṁtrastahṛdayā sarve prākārādavaruhya te
viṣaṇṇavadanāḥ sarve rākṣasendramupasthitāḥ
Thereat, with their hearts wrought up, grimvisaged Raksasas descending from the wall appeared before the Raksasa-lord with pale faces.

तदप्रियं दीनमुखा रावणस्य निशाचराः
कृत्स्नं निवेदयामासुर्यथावद्वाक्यकोविदाः

tadapriyaṁ dīnamukhā rāvaṇasya niśācarāḥ
kṛtsnaṁ nivedayāmāsuryathāvadvākyakovidāḥ
Then with woe-begone faces, those Raksasas, skilled in speech, faithfully informed Ravana in full of that unfortunate circumstance.

यौ ताविन्द्रजिता युद्धे भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
निबद्धौ शरबन्धेन निष्प्रकम्पभुजौ कृतौ

yau tāvindrajitā yuddhe bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
nibaddhau śarabandhena niṣprakampabhujau kṛtau

Those brothers-Rama and Laksmana-who had in battle been bound up in arrowy fetters by Indrajit, and whose arms lay moveless, having been emancipated from the arrowy bonds, are seen in the field of battle; and those ones like to the foremost of elephants in strength, seem like elephants that have snapped their fetters.

तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तेषां राक्षसेन्द्रो महाबलः
चिन्ताशोकसमाक्रान्तो विषण्णवदनोऽब्रवीत्

tacchrutvā vacanaṁ teṣāṁ rākṣasendro mahābalaḥ
cintāśokasamākrānto viṣaṇṇavadano'bravīt
Hearing those words of theirs, the exceedingly powerful lord of the Raksasas was wrought up with anxiety and anger, and his countenance lost its complexion.

घोरैर्दत्तवरैर्बद्धौ शरैराशीविषोमपैः
अमोघैः सूर्यसंकाशैः प्रमथ्येन्द्रजिता युधि

ghorairdattavarairbaddhau śarairāśīviṣomapaiḥ
amoghaiḥ sūryasaṁkāśaiḥ pramathyendrajitā yudhi

Indrajit, having routed them in conflict, had bound them by means of irresistible and terrible arrows, resembling venomous serpents, and like to the Sun himself, which had been conferred on (Indrajit) as boons. But if my enemy having actually been bound by the weapons, can have been liberated, all this strength of mine I see placed in peril.

निष्फलाः खलु संवृत्ताः शरा वासुकितेजसः
आदत्तं यैस्तु संग्रामे रिपूणां मम जीवितम्

niṣphalāḥ khalu saṁvṛttāḥ śarā vāsukitejasaḥ
ādattaṁ yaistu saṁgrāme ripūṇāṁ mama jīvitam
And those shafts resembling Fire in fierceness, which had in battle deprived my foes of their lives, have forsooth been rendered fruitless.

एवमुक्त्वा तु संक्रुद्धो निश्वसन्नुरगो यथा
अब्रवीद्रक्षसां मध्ये धूम्राक्षं नाम राकसं

evamuktvā tu saṁkruddho niśvasannurago yathā
abravīdrakṣasāṁ madhye dhūmrākṣaṁ nāma rākasaṁ
Having said this in high rage Ravana, sighing like a serpent, addressed a Raksasa, named Dhumraksa, seated in the midst of the Raksasa.

बलेन महता युक्तो रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्
त्वं वधायाभिनिर्याहि रामस्य सह वानरैः

balena mahatā yukto rakṣasāṁ bhīmakarmaṇām
tvaṁ vadhāyābhiniryāhi rāmasya saha vānaraiḥ
O you of dreadful prowess, surrounded by a mighty force, do you march forth to compass the destruction of Rama along with the monkeys.

एवमुक्तस्तु धूम्राक्षो राक्षसेन्द्रेण धीमता
कृत्वा प्रणामं संहृष्टो निर्जगाम नृपालयात्

evamuktastu dhūmrākṣo rākṣasendreṇa dhīmatā
kṛtvā praṇāmaṁ saṁhṛṣṭo nirjagāma nṛpālayāt
Thus accosted by the intelligent lord of the Raksasas, Dhumraksa, turning about, issued out of the abode of the king.

अभिनिष्क्रम्य तद्द्वारं बलाध्यक्षमुवाच ह
त्वरयस्व बलं तूर्णं किं चिरेण युयुत्सतः

abhiniṣkramya taddvāraṁ balādhyakṣamuvāca ha
tvarayasva balaṁ tūrṇaṁ kiṁ cireṇa yuyutsataḥ
And speedily sallying forth from the gate of (Ravana's residence, he said to the general of the forces, “Do you speedily move off your forces. why should a warrior linger?”

धूम्राक्षस्य वचः श्रुत्वा बलाध्यक्षो बलानुगः
बलमुद्योजयामास रावणस्याज्ञया द्रुतम्

dhūmrākṣasya vacaḥ śrutvā balādhyakṣo balānugaḥ
balamudyojayāmāsa rāvaṇasyājñayā drutam
Hearing Dhumraksa's words, the general of the forces, following them, at the command of Ravana forthwith made the army ready.

ते बद्धघण्टा बलिनो घोररूपा निशाचराः
विनर्दमानाः संहृष्टा धूम्राक्षं पर्यवारयन्

te baddhaghaṇṭā balino ghorarūpā niśācarāḥ
vinardamānāḥ saṁhṛṣṭā dhūmrākṣaṁ paryavārayan
And those powerful and dreadful nightrangers, bursting with high spirits, with bells tied to their arms, set up shouts, and surrounded Dhumraksa.

विविधायुधहस्ताश्च शूलमुद्गरपाणयः
गदाभिः पट्टसैर्दण्डैरायसैर्मुसलैर्भृशम्

vividhāyudhahastāśca śūlamudgarapāṇayaḥ
gadābhiḥ paṭṭasairdaṇḍairāyasairmusalairbhṛśam

And bearing various weapons in their hands, and wielding darts and clubs, and equipped with maces and bearded darts and rods and iron bludgeons and parighas and bhindipalas and lances and nooses and axes, those terrific Raks asas sallied out roaring like to clouds.

रथैः कवचिनस्त्वन्ये ध्वजैश्च समलंकृतैः
सुवर्णजालविहितैः खरैश्च विविधाननैः

rathaiḥ kavacinastvanye dhvajaiśca samalaṁkṛtaiḥ
suvarṇajālavihitaiḥ kharaiśca vividhānanaiḥ

And others, accoutred in armour, with cars; adorned with banners; furnished with golden networks, and mules having various faces, and extremely swift steeds, and lusty elephants in rut, tiger-like Naistas incapable of being subdued even as tigers-sallied out (thereafter).

वृकसिंहमुखैर्युक्तं खरैः कनकभूषणैः
आरुरोह रथं दिव्यं धूम्राक्षः खरनिस्वनः

vṛkasiṁhamukhairyuktaṁ kharaiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ
āruroha rathaṁ divyaṁ dhūmrākṣaḥ kharanisvanaḥ
Then Dhumraksa himself ascended a superb car, bearing faces of deer and lions decked with gold, and sending forth a loud clatter.

स निर्यातो महावीर्यो धूम्राक्षो राक्षसैर्वृतः
प्रहसन्पश्चिमद्वारं हनूमान्यत्र यूथपः

sa niryāto mahāvīryo dhūmrākṣo rākṣasairvṛtaḥ
prahasanpaścimadvāraṁ hanūmānyatra yūthapaḥ
The highly powerful Dhumraksa, surrounded by Raksasas, cheerfully issued out of the Western Entrance, where Hanuman was posted.

प्रयान्तं तु महाघोरं राक्षसं भीमदर्शनम्
अन्तरिक्षगताः क्रूराः शकुनाः प्रत्यवारयन्

prayāntaṁ tu mahāghoraṁ rākṣasaṁ bhīmadarśanam
antarikṣagatāḥ krūrāḥ śakunāḥ pratyavārayan
Thereat, fell fowls of the air forbade that exceedingly dreadful Raksasa of a fearful form, as he went out ascending an excellent car joked with mules, and sending sharp sounds.

रथशीर्षे महाभीमो गृध्रश्च निपपात ह
ध्वजाग्रे ग्रथिताश्चैव निपेतुः कुणपाशनाः

rathaśīrṣe mahābhīmo gṛdhraśca nipapāta ha
dhvajāgre grathitāścaiva nipetuḥ kuṇapāśanāḥ

And an exceedingly terrific vulture alighted at the crest of the car and forming themselves into lines, vultures began to drop down about the top of the banner. And emitting a frightful cry, (a headless trunk) dropped down before Dhumraksa.

ववर्ष रुधिरं देवः संचचाल च मेदिनी
प्रतिलोमं ववौ वायुर्निर्घातसमनिस्वनः
तिमिरौघावृतास्तत्र दिशश्च न चकाशिरे

vavarṣa rudhiraṁ devaḥ saṁcacāla ca medinī
pratilomaṁ vavau vāyurnirghātasamanisvanaḥ
timiraughāvṛtāstatra diśaśca na cakāśire
That god* showered down blood; and the earth shook. And the wind blew awry with a sound resembling thunder. And every side, covered with darkness, appeared dim. *Indra-cloud compeller.

स तूत्पातांस्ततो दृष्ट्वा राक्षसानां भयावहान्
प्रादुर्भूतान्सुघोरांश्च धूम्राक्षो व्यथितोऽभवत्

sa tūtpātāṁstato dṛṣṭvā rākṣasānāṁ bhayāvahān
prādurbhūtānsughorāṁśca dhūmrākṣo vyathito'bhavat
And witnessing those dreadful inauspicious omens at the outset, fraught with fear to the Raksasas, Dhumraksa was greatly aggrieved; and the Raksasas marching before him, were stupefied.

ततः सुभीमो बहुभिर्निशाचरै;र्वृतोऽभिनिष्क्रम्य रणोत्सुको बली
ददर्श तां राघवबाहुपालितां; समुद्रकल्पां बहुवानरीं चमूम्

tataḥ subhīmo bahubhirniśācarai;rvṛto'bhiniṣkramya raṇotsuko balī
dadarśa tāṁ rāghavabāhupālitāṁ; samudrakalpāṁ bahuvānarīṁ camūm

Then as that strong and fearful one, eager for encounter, surrounded by in numerable nigh rangers, issued out (of the city), he beheld that monkey-host, protected by the arm of Raghava, resembling the deep at the time of universal dissolution.

धूम्राक्षं प्रेक्ष्य निर्यान्तं राक्षसं भीमनिस्वनम्
विनेदुर्वानराः सर्वे प्रहृष्टा युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः

dhūmrākṣaṁ prekṣya niryāntaṁ rākṣasaṁ bhīmanisvanam
vinedurvānarāḥ sarve prahṛṣṭā yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
Seeing the Raksasa-Dhumraksa of dreadful prowess-issue out, the monkeys, rejoicing greatly, eager for encounter, set up roars.

तेषां तु तुमुलं युद्धं संजज्ञे हरिरक्षसाम्
अन्योन्यं पादपैर्घोरैर्निघ्नतं शूलमुद्गरैः

teṣāṁ tu tumulaṁ yuddhaṁ saṁjajñe harirakṣasām
anyonyaṁ pādapairghorairnighnataṁ śūlamudgaraiḥ
Then there took place a terrific conflict between the monkeys and the Raksasas, charging each other with fearful trees, and darts, and maces.

राक्षसैर्वानरा घोरा विनिकृत्ताः समन्ततः
वानरै राक्षसाश्चापि द्रुमैर्भूमौ समीकृताः

rākṣasairvānarā ghorā vinikṛttāḥ samantataḥ
vānarai rākṣasāścāpi drumairbhūmau samīkṛtāḥ
The Raksasas began to scatter the dreadful monkeys on all sides; and the monkeys (on their parts) felled the Raksasas with trees.

राक्षसाश्चापि संक्रुद्धा वानरान्निशितैः शरैः
विव्यधुर्घोरसंकाशैः कङ्कपत्रैरजिह्मगैः

rākṣasāścāpi saṁkruddhā vānarānniśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
vivyadhurghorasaṁkāśaiḥ kaṅkapatrairajihmagaiḥ
The Raksasas, growing enraged, began to pierce that monkeys with straight speeding sharp shafts winged with Kanka plumes.

विदार्यमाणा रक्षोभिर्वानरास्ते महाबलाः
अमर्षाज्जनितोद्धर्षाश्चक्रुः कर्माण्यभीतवत्

vidāryamāṇā rakṣobhirvānarāste mahābalāḥ
amarṣājjanitoddharṣāścakruḥ karmāṇyabhītavat

And riven by the Raksasa with drcadful clubs and bearded darts, daggers and maces and terrible and curious bludgeons and grasped javelins, the exceedingly powerful (monkeys), their anger aroused, began with alacrity to perform deeds of intrepid valour.

शरनिर्भिन्नगात्रास्ते शूलनिर्भिन्नदेहिनः
जगृहुस्ते द्रुमांस्तत्र शिलाश्च हरियूथपाः

śaranirbhinnagātrāste śūlanirbhinnadehinaḥ
jagṛhuste drumāṁstatra śilāśca hariyūthapāḥ
Those monkey-leaders, their bodies pierced with shafts and their persons riven with darts, took up trees and crags.

ते भीमवेगा हरयो नर्दमानास्ततस्ततः
ममन्थू राक्षसान्भीमान्नामानि च बभाषिरे

te bhīmavegā harayo nardamānāstatastataḥ
mamanthū rākṣasānbhīmānnāmāni ca babhāṣire
Those monkeys, endowed with terrific vehemence, sending up shouts, and proclaiming their respective names, set about tossing the brave Raksasa rank,

तद्बभूवाद्भुतं घोरं युद्धं वानररक्षसाम्
शिलाभिर्विविधाभिश्च बहुशाखैश्च पादपैः

tadbabhūvādbhutaṁ ghoraṁ yuddhaṁ vānararakṣasām
śilābhirvividhābhiśca bahuśākhaiśca pādapaiḥ
The monkeys, waged with diverse rocks and innumerable trees, waxed exceedingly furious.

राक्षसा मथिताः केचिद्वानरैर्जितकाशिभिः
ववर्षू रुधिरं केचिन्मुखै रुधिरभोजनाः

rākṣasā mathitāḥ kecidvānarairjitakāśibhiḥ
vavarṣū rudhiraṁ kecinmukhai rudhirabhojanāḥ
Sparkling in the glory of victory, the monkeys crushed the Raksasas and some among them feeding on gore began to vomit blood.

पार्श्वेषु दारिताः केचित्केचिद्राशीकृता द्रुमैः
शिलाभिश्चूर्णिताः केचित्केचिद्दन्तैर्विदारिताः

pārśveṣu dāritāḥ kecitkecidrāśīkṛtā drumaiḥ
śilābhiścūrṇitāḥ kecitkeciddantairvidāritāḥ
And some were severed along their flanks; and, some, slain with trees, were heaped up; and some were crushed with crags; and some were torn with teeth.

ध्वजैर्विमथितैर्भग्नैः खरैश्च विनिपातितैः
रथैर्विध्वंसितैश्चापि पतितै रजनीचरैः

dhvajairvimathitairbhagnaiḥ kharaiśca vinipātitaiḥ
rathairvidhvaṁsitaiścāpi patitai rajanīcaraiḥ
Some being broken down by means of broken standards, and some by means of fallen swords, and some crushed down by cars, the rangers of the night suffered sorely.

वानरैर्भीमविक्रान्तैराप्लुत्याप्लुत्य वेगितैः
राक्षसाः करजैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मुखेषु विनिकर्तिताः

vānarairbhīmavikrāntairāplutyāplutya vegitaiḥ
rākṣasāḥ karajaistīkṣṇairmukheṣu vinikartitāḥ
Bounding again and again, the vehement monkeys endowed with terrific prowess, with their finger-nails tore up the Raksasas by the mouths.

विवर्णवदना भूयो विप्रकीर्णशिरोरुहाः
मूढाः शोणितगन्धेन निपेतुर्धरणीतले

vivarṇavadanā bhūyo viprakīrṇaśiroruhāḥ
mūḍhāḥ śoṇitagandhena nipeturdharaṇītale
With woebegone faces, and with hair dishevelled, (the Raksasas), stupified with the smell of blood, saught the earth.

नये तु परमक्रुद्धा राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः
तलैरेवाभिधावन्ति वज्रस्पर्शसमैर्हरीन्

naye tu paramakruddhā rākṣasā bhīmavikramāḥ
talairevābhidhāvanti vajrasparśasamairharīn
Other Raksasas endowed with dreadful vigour, waxing wondrous wroth, dealt the monkeys slaps with hands having the touch of the thunder-bolt.

वनरैरापतन्तस्ते वेगिता वेगवत्तरैः
मुष्टिभिश्चरणैर्दन्तैः पादपैश्चापपोथिताः

vanarairāpatantaste vegitā vegavattaraiḥ
muṣṭibhiścaraṇairdantaiḥ pādapaiścāpapothitāḥ
Gift with greater impetuosity, the monkeys felled the impetuous (Raksasas) with blows, and feet and teeth; and some were slain with trees.

सन्यं तु विद्रुतं दृष्ट्वा धूम्राक्षो राक्षसर्षभः
क्रोधेन कदनं चक्रे वानराणां युयुत्सताम्

sanyaṁ tu vidrutaṁ dṛṣṭvā dhūmrākṣo rākṣasarṣabhaḥ
krodhena kadanaṁ cakre vānarāṇāṁ yuyutsatām
Seeing the forces fleeing away, that foremost of Raksasas-Dhumraksa-flying into fury, began a terrific conflict with the monkeys desirous of encounter.

प्रासैः प्रमथिताः केचिद्वानराः शोणितस्रवाः
मुद्गरैराहताः केचित्पतिता धरणीतले

prāsaiḥ pramathitāḥ kecidvānarāḥ śoṇitasravāḥ
mudgarairāhatāḥ kecitpatitā dharaṇītale
Some of the monkeys, sore assailed with prasas, began to bleed; and some, wounded with maces, dropped down to the ground.

परिघैर्मथितः केचिद्भिण्डिपालैर्विदारिताः
पट्टसैराहताः केचिद्विह्वलन्तो गतासवः

parighairmathitaḥ kecidbhiṇḍipālairvidāritāḥ
paṭṭasairāhatāḥ kecidvihvalanto gatāsavaḥ
Some were beaten hard with bludgeons; and some were cleft with bhindipalas. And some, on being assailed with bearded darts, became insensible and lost their lives.

केचिद्विनिहता भूमौ रुधिरार्द्रा वनौकसः
केचिद्विद्राविता नष्टाः संक्रुद्धै राक्षसैर्युधि

kecidvinihatā bhūmau rudhirārdrā vanaukasaḥ
kecidvidrāvitā naṣṭāḥ saṁkruddhai rākṣasairyudhi
Some among the monkeys lay slain on the ground, drenched in blood. and some, fleeing away from the field, were slaughtered by the infuriated Raksasas.

विभिन्नहृदयाः केचिदेकपार्श्वेन शायिताः
विदारितास्त्रशूलै च केचिदान्त्रैर्विनिस्रुताः

vibhinnahṛdayāḥ kecidekapārśvena śāyitāḥ
vidāritāstraśūlai ca kecidāntrairvinisrutāḥ
Some, having their breasts pierced, lay on their sides. and some were riven with tridents; and the entrails of some had come out.

तत्सुभीमं महद्युद्धं हरिराकस संकुलम्
प्रबभौ शस्त्रबहुलं शिलापादपसंकुलम्

tatsubhīmaṁ mahadyuddhaṁ harirākasa saṁkulam
prababhau śastrabahulaṁ śilāpādapasaṁkulam
That mighty and dreadful encounter of the Raksasas and the monkeys, was waged with countless weapons and rocks and trees.

धनुर्ज्यातन्त्रिमधुरं हिक्कातालसमन्वितम्
मन्द्रस्तनितसंगीतं युद्धगान्धर्वमाबभौ

dhanurjyātantrimadhuraṁ hikkātālasamanvitam
mandrastanitasaṁgītaṁ yuddhagāndharvamābabhau

That battle he come a musical entertainment' mellifluous with bow-string for Vina, having the neighing of chargers for its measure, and with the cries of Maindas' for its strains. 1. The reader has already perceived that the carrying out of a simile to a number of details is a characteristic as much of Valmiki as of his rival in the epic sphere-Vyasa, but the comparisons are never on all fours, as in the case before us. 2. A classical Hindu musical instrument, having metallic strings, with a pair of gourds at one end for the sounding-board. Vide Yantra-Kosa by Sir Saurindra Mohan Tagore, Mus-Doc. 3. A species of elephants.

धूम्राक्षस्तु धनुष्पाणिर्वानरान्रणमूर्धनि
हसन्विद्रावयामास दिशस्ताञ्शरवृष्टिभिः

dhūmrākṣastu dhanuṣpāṇirvānarānraṇamūrdhani
hasanvidrāvayāmāsa diśastāñśaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
Then in the field, Dhumraksa bow in hand, laughing, pursued the monkeys in all directions with showers of shafts.

धूम्राक्षेणार्दितं सैन्यं व्यथितं दृश्य मारुतिः
अभ्यवर्तत संक्रुद्धः प्रगृह्य विपुलां शिलाम्

dhūmrākṣeṇārditaṁ sainyaṁ vyathitaṁ dṛśya mārutiḥ
abhyavartata saṁkruddhaḥ pragṛhya vipulāṁ śilām
Seeing the forces hard beset by Dhumraksa and distressed thereat, the Windgod's offspring, waxing enraged, seizing a huge crag, approached (the Raksasa).

क्रोधाद्द्विगुणताम्राक्षः पितृतुल्यपराक्रमः
शिलां तां पातयामास धूम्राक्षस्य रथं प्रति

krodhāddviguṇatāmrākṣaḥ pitṛtulyaparākramaḥ
śilāṁ tāṁ pātayāmāsa dhūmrākṣasya rathaṁ prati
And with his eyes double reddened in wrath, the one, like to his sire himself in prowess, brought down the crag upon Dhumraksa's car.

आपतन्तीं शिलां दृष्ट्वा गदामुद्यम्य संभ्रमात्
रथादाप्लुत्य वेगेन वसुधायां व्यतिष्ठत

āpatantīṁ śilāṁ dṛṣṭvā gadāmudyamya saṁbhramāt
rathādāplutya vegena vasudhāyāṁ vyatiṣṭhata
Seeing the crag, (Dhumraksa) upraising his mace hurriedly, leapt down in vehemence, and stood on the ground. And having shattered his car, that crag fell down to the earth.

स भङ्क्त्वा तु रथं तस्य हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
रक्षसां कदनं चक्रे सस्कन्धविटपैर्द्रुमैः

sa bhaṅktvā tu rathaṁ tasya hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
rakṣasāṁ kadanaṁ cakre saskandhaviṭapairdrumaiḥ

Thereat letting go the car furnished with wheels, Kuvaras and a face, as well as a banner; in which Dhumraksa had left his bow, Hanuman-son to the Wind-god-laid about him right lustily for destroying the Raksasas, with trees having branches long and short.

विभिन्नशिरसो भूत्वा राक्षसाः शोणितोक्षिताः
द्रुमैः प्रमथिताश्चान्ये निपेतुर्धरणीतले

vibhinnaśiraso bhūtvā rākṣasāḥ śoṇitokṣitāḥ
drumaiḥ pramathitāścānye nipeturdharaṇītale
Thereat some Raksasas with their heads shattered, lay drenched in blood; and others, struck with trees, dropped down to the earth.

विद्राव्य राक्षसं सैन्यं हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
गिरेः शिखरमादाय धूम्राक्षमभिदुद्रुवे

vidrāvya rākṣasaṁ sainyaṁ hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
gireḥ śikharamādāya dhūmrākṣamabhidudruve
Then Hanuman-son to the Wind-god-charged in full career against the Raksasa army; and, taking a mountain-peak, he rushed against Dhumraksa.

तमापतन्तं धूम्राक्षो गदामुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्
विनर्दमानः सहसा हनूमन्तमभिद्रवत्

tamāpatantaṁ dhūmrākṣo gadāmudyamya vīryavān
vinardamānaḥ sahasā hanūmantamabhidravat
As Hanuman was descending, the powerful Dhumraksa, upraising a mace and giving out a shout, made towards him speedily.

ततः क्रुद्धस्तु वेगेन गदां तां बहुकण्टकाम्
पातयामास धूम्राक्षो मस्तके तु हनूमतः

tataḥ kruddhastu vegena gadāṁ tāṁ bahukaṇṭakām
pātayāmāsa dhūmrākṣo mastake tu hanūmataḥ
Then Dhumraksa enraged, brought down that mace studded with innumerable pricks, on the head of Hanuman fired with wrath.

ताडितः स तया तत्र गदया भीमरूपया
स कपिर्मारुतबलस्तं प्रहारमचिन्तयन्
धूम्राक्षस्य शिरो मध्ये गिरिशृङ्गमपातयत्

tāḍitaḥ sa tayā tatra gadayā bhīmarūpayā
sa kapirmārutabalastaṁ prahāramacintayan
dhūmrākṣasya śiro madhye giriśṛṅgamapātayat

Thus assailed with the mace of fearful impetuosity, the monkey endowed with he mace of fearful impetuosity, the monkey endowed with the strength of the wind without at all heeding that blow, let fall a mountain-top right against Dhumraksa's head.

स विह्वलितसर्वाङ्गो गिरिशृङ्गेण ताडितः
पपात सहसा भूमौ विकीर्ण इव पर्वतः

sa vihvalitasarvāṅgo giriśṛṅgeṇa tāḍitaḥ
papāta sahasā bhūmau vikīrṇa iva parvataḥ
On being assailed with the mountain-peak, Dhumraksa, having his entire body mangled, suddenly fell to the earth, like to a toppling hill.

धूम्राक्षं निहतं दृष्ट्वा हतशेषा निशाचराः
त्रस्ताः प्रविविशुर्लङ्कां वध्यमानाः प्लवंगमैः

dhūmrākṣaṁ nihataṁ dṛṣṭvā hataśeṣā niśācarāḥ
trastāḥ praviviśurlaṅkāṁ vadhyamānāḥ plavaṁgamaiḥ
Seeing Dhumraksa slain, those night-rangers that survived the carnage, in extreme agitation began to pour into Lanka, attacked by the monkeys.

स तु पवनसुतो निहत्य शत्रुं; क्षतजवहाः सरितश्च संविकीर्य
रिपुवधजनितश्रमो महात्मा; मुदमगमत्कपिभिश्च पूज्यमानः

sa tu pavanasuto nihatya śatruṁ; kṣatajavahāḥ saritaśca saṁvikīrya
ripuvadhajanitaśramo mahātmā; mudamagamatkapibhiśca pūjyamānaḥ

That high-souled offspring of the Wind-god, having slain his foes, and come under the influence of fatigue incident to his slaughtering his enemies, having caused rivers of gore to flow (in the field), experienced the excess of joy on being honoured of the monkeys.

धूम्राक्षं निहतं श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
बलाध्यक्षमुवाचेदं कृताञ्जलिमुपस्थितम्

dhūmrākṣaṁ nihataṁ śrutvā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
balādhyakṣamuvācedaṁ kṛtāñjalimupasthitam
Hearing Vajradanstra slain by the son of Vali, Ravana said to the general of his forces, standing before him with joined hands,

शीघ्रं निर्यान्तु दुर्धर्षा राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः
अकम्पनं पुरस्कृत्य सर्वशस्त्रप्रकोविदम्

śīghraṁ niryāntu durdharṣā rākṣasā bhīmavikramāḥ
akampanaṁ puraskṛtya sarvaśastraprakovidam
Let invincible Raksasas of dreadful prowess, march forth, placing before them Akampana, skilled in all weapons and arms.

ततो नानाप्रहरणा भीमाक्षा भीमदर्शनाः
निष्पेतू राक्षसा मुख्या बलाध्यक्षप्रचोदिताः

tato nānāpraharaṇā bhīmākṣā bhīmadarśanāḥ
niṣpetū rākṣasā mukhyā balādhyakṣapracoditāḥ
Then equipped with various arms, the foremost of Raksasas, having dreadful eyes (in their heads, and of dreadful forms, marched forth, urged on by their general.

रथमास्थाय विपुलं तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः
राकसैः संवृतो घोरैस्तदा निर्यात्यकम्पनः

rathamāsthāya vipulaṁ taptakāñcanakuṇḍalaḥ
rākasaiḥ saṁvṛto ghoraistadā niryātyakampanaḥ

Ascending a large car, adorned with burnished gold, Akampana, possessed of the splendour of clouds,* and cloud-hued, and furnished with a voice resembling the roar of clouds, went out, environed by Rakasasas of terrific forms. *There is a pun here on the word Akampana-lit.one incapable of being shaken.

न हि कम्पयितुं शक्यः सुरैरपि महामृधे
अकम्पनस्ततस्तेषामादित्य इव तेजसा

na hi kampayituṁ śakyaḥ surairapi mahāmṛdhe
akampanastatasteṣāmāditya iva tejasā

Akampana, resembling the sun in power, was incapable of being shaken in fight by the very gods, and of being beheld by them. 1. Possessed of a person measuring, according to the commentator, a mass of clouds. I give the apparent sense, which answers. 2. Monkeys.

तस्य निधावमानस्य संरब्धस्य युयुत्सया
अकस्माद्दैन्यमागच्छद्धयानां रथवाहिनाम्

tasya nidhāvamānasya saṁrabdhasya yuyutsayā
akasmāddainyamāgacchaddhayānāṁ rathavāhinām
And as, burning for battle, he rushed out in wrath, the steeds drawing his car suddenly lost their energy.

व्यस्फुरन्नयनं चास्य सव्यं युद्धाभिनन्दिनः
विवर्णो मुखवर्णश्च गद्गदश्चाभवत्स्वरः

vyasphurannayanaṁ cāsya savyaṁ yuddhābhinandinaḥ
vivarṇo mukhavarṇaśca gadgadaścābhavatsvaraḥ
The left eye of that one delighting in encounter, began to throb. And his continence grew pale, and his voice faltered.

अभवत्सुदिने चापि दुर्दिने रूक्षमारुतम्
ऊचुः खगा मृगाः सर्वे वाचः क्रूरा भयावहाः

abhavatsudine cāpi durdine rūkṣamārutam
ūcuḥ khagā mṛgāḥ sarve vācaḥ krūrā bhayāvahāḥ
In a fair day, it looked foul with the wind breathing roughly. And fierce and frightful beasts and birds began to emit cries.

स सिंहोपचितस्कन्धः शार्दूलसमविक्रमः
तानुत्पातानचिन्त्यैव निर्जगाम रणाजिरम्

sa siṁhopacitaskandhaḥ śārdūlasamavikramaḥ
tānutpātānacintyaiva nirjagāma raṇājiram
That lion-shouldered one like a tiger in prowess, without heeding these ominous occurrences, marched forth into the field.

तदा निर्गच्छतस्तस्य रक्षसः सह राक्षसैः
बभूव सुमहान्नादः क्षोभयन्निव सागरम्

tadā nirgacchatastasya rakṣasaḥ saha rākṣasaiḥ
babhūva sumahānnādaḥ kṣobhayanniva sāgaram
As that Raksasa was setting out along with the Raksasas, he set up mighty roars as if agitating the deep.

तेषां युद्धं महारौद्रं संजज्ञे कपिरक्षसाम्
रामरावणयोरर्थे समभित्यक्तजीविनाम्

teṣāṁ yuddhaṁ mahāraudraṁ saṁjajñe kapirakṣasām
rāmarāvaṇayorarthe samabhityaktajīvinām

The mighty army of monkeys was seized with trepidation at that sound. And then there took place a mighty encounter of the Raksasas and the monkeys equipped staying in fight with trees and rocks, who had given up all concern for their selves in behalf of Rama and Ravana.

तेषां विनर्दातां शब्दः संयुगेऽतितरस्विनाम्
शुश्रुवे सुमहान्क्रोधादन्योन्यमभिगर्जताम्

teṣāṁ vinardātāṁ śabdaḥ saṁyuge'titarasvinām
śuśruve sumahānkrodhādanyonyamabhigarjatām

And each side desirous of slaying the other, the monkeys and the Raksasas were exceedingly strong and heroic and like to mountains. And each party storming at the other, in that conflict were heard loud cries emitted by those swiftspeeding ones in anger.

रजश्चारुणवर्णाभं सुभीममभवद्भृशम्
उद्धूतं हरिरक्षोभिः संरुरोध दिशो दश

rajaścāruṇavarṇābhaṁ subhīmamabhavadbhṛśam
uddhūtaṁ harirakṣobhiḥ saṁrurodha diśo daśa
And fearful was the dust red-hued that was raised incessantly by the monkeys and the Raksasa; and it enveloped the ten cardinal points.

अन्योन्यं रजसा तेन कौशेयोद्धूतपाण्डुना
संवृतानि च भूतानि ददृशुर्न रणाजिरे

anyonyaṁ rajasā tena kauśeyoddhūtapāṇḍunā
saṁvṛtāni ca bhūtāni dadṛśurna raṇājire
In the field of battle, each enveloped with that dust raised, pale as silk, could not be discovered by the other.

न ध्वजो न पताकावा वर्म वा तुरगोऽपि वा
आयुधं स्यन्दनं वापि ददृशे तेन रेणुना

na dhvajo na patākāvā varma vā turago'pi vā
āyudhaṁ syandanaṁ vāpi dadṛśe tena reṇunā
In consequence of that dust arising, neither standard, nor ensign, nor shield, nor steed, nor weapon, nor car could be seen.

शब्दश्च सुमहांस्तेषां नर्दतामभिधावताम्
श्रूयते तुमुले युद्धे न रूपाणि चकाशिरे

śabdaśca sumahāṁsteṣāṁ nardatāmabhidhāvatām
śrūyate tumule yuddhe na rūpāṇi cakāśire
The fierce cries alone of those roaring and rushing were heard in that dreadful battle; but their forms were not visible to the sight.

हरीनेव सुसंक्रुद्धा हरयो जघ्नुराहवे
राक्षसाश्चापि रक्षांसि निजघ्नुस्तिमिरे तदा

harīneva susaṁkruddhā harayo jaghnurāhave
rākṣasāścāpi rakṣāṁsi nijaghnustimire tadā
In that conflict in the dark then monkeys extremely enraged slew monkeys, and Raksasas also killed the Raksasas.

परांश्चैव विनिघ्नन्तः स्वांश्च वानरराक्षसाः
रुधिरार्द्रं तदा चक्रुर्महीं पङ्कानुलेपनाम्

parāṁścaiva vinighnantaḥ svāṁśca vānararākṣasāḥ
rudhirārdraṁ tadā cakrurmahīṁ paṅkānulepanām
And monkeys and Raksasas slaying (indiscriminately) friends and foes, made the earth wet with blood, and miry.

ततस्तु रुधिरौघेण सिक्तं व्यपगतं रजः
शरीरशवसंकीर्णा बभूव च वसुंधरा

tatastu rudhiraugheṇa siktaṁ vyapagataṁ rajaḥ
śarīraśavasaṁkīrṇā babhūva ca vasuṁdharā
Then with showers of blood the dust was layed; and the earth was covered with corpses.

बाहुभिः परिघाकारैर्युध्यन्तः पर्वतोपमाः
हरयो भीमकर्माणो राक्षसाञ्जघ्नुराहवे

bāhubhiḥ parighākārairyudhyantaḥ parvatopamāḥ
harayo bhīmakarmāṇo rākṣasāñjaghnurāhave

Raksasas and monkeys fast slew each other vigorously with trees and darts, maces and prasas, rocks, bludgeons and Tomaras, and by means of their arms resembling bludgeons, coped with their adversaries appearing like hills.

राक्षसाश्चापि संक्रुद्धाः प्रासतोमरपाणयः
कपीन्निजघ्निरे तत्र शस्त्रैः परमदारुणैः

rākṣasāścāpi saṁkruddhāḥ prāsatomarapāṇayaḥ
kapīnnijaghnire tatra śastraiḥ paramadāruṇaiḥ
And in the encounter monkeys slew Raksasas of dreadful deeds. And in their turn Raksasas, wrought up with passion, bearing in their hands prasas and tomaras destroyed monkeys wielding dire arms.

हरयस्त्वपि रक्षांसि महाद्रुममहाश्मभिः
विदारयन्त्यभिक्रम्य शस्त्राण्याच्छिद्य वीर्यतः

harayastvapi rakṣāṁsi mahādrumamahāśmabhiḥ
vidārayantyabhikramya śastrāṇyācchidya vīryataḥ
And the monkeys forcibly snatching away the weapons (of the Raksasas), began to rive the Raksasas with mighty trees and giant crags.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरा हरयः कुमुदो नलः
मैन्दश्च परमक्रुद्धश्चक्रुर्वेगमनुत्तमम्

etasminnantare vīrā harayaḥ kumudo nalaḥ
maindaśca paramakruddhaścakrurvegamanuttamam
In the meanwhile those heroes among the monkeys-Kumuda, Nila and the exceedingly exasperated Mainda, summoned the utmost impetuosity they were masters of.

ते तु वृक्षैर्महावेगा राक्षसानां चमूमुखे
कदनं सुमह चक्रुर्लीलया हरियूथपाः

te tu vṛkṣairmahāvegā rākṣasānāṁ camūmukhe
kadanaṁ sumaha cakrurlīlayā hariyūthapāḥ
And those foremost of monkeys and redoubtable able warriors without much ado began to spread quite a carnage in the van of the Raksasa army, and by means of various arms terribly beat the Raksasas.

तद्दृष्ट्वा सुमहत्कर्म कृतं वानरसत्तमैः
क्रोधमाहारयामास युधि तीव्रमकम्पनः

taddṛṣṭvā sumahatkarma kṛtaṁ vānarasattamaiḥ
krodhamāhārayāmāsa yudhi tīvramakampanaḥ
And witnessing that mighty exploit of the foremost of the monkeys, Akampana waxed furious with wrath.

क्रोधमूर्छितरूपस्तु ध्नुवन्परमकार्मुकम्
दृष्ट्वा तु कर्म शत्रूणां सारथिं वाक्यमब्रवीत्

krodhamūrchitarūpastu dhnuvanparamakārmukam
dṛṣṭvā tu karma śatrūṇāṁ sārathiṁ vākyamabravīt
And transported with passion, he, twanging his mighty bow seeing that feat of his foe, addressed his charioteer saying.

तत्रैव तावत्त्वरितं रथं प्रापय सारथे
एतेऽत्र बहवो घ्नन्ति सुबहून्राक्षसान्रणे

tatraiva tāvattvaritaṁ rathaṁ prāpaya sārathe
ete'tra bahavo ghnanti subahūnrākṣasānraṇe
O charioteer, swiftly conduct you the car to that same place. These powerful ones are slaying innumerable Raksasas in fight.

एतेऽत्र बलवन्तो हि भीमकायाश्च वानराः
द्रुमशैलप्रहरणास्तिष्ठन्ति प्रमुखे मम

ete'tra balavanto hi bhīmakāyāśca vānarāḥ
drumaśailapraharaṇāstiṣṭhanti pramukhe mama
And all those vigorous monkeys of dreadful deeds stay before me, armed with trees and rocks.

एतान्निहन्तुमिच्छामि समरश्लाघिनो ह्यहम्
एतैः प्रमथितं सर्वं दृश्यते राक्षसं बलम्

etānnihantumicchāmi samaraślāghino hyaham
etaiḥ pramathitaṁ sarvaṁ dṛśyate rākṣasaṁ balam
Those, pluming themselves overmuch on their martial worth, I intended to slay in battle. And all this Raksasa force appeared to be harassed by these.

ततः प्रजविताश्वेन रथेन रथिनां वरः
हरीनभ्यहनत्क्रोधाच्छरजालैरकम्पनः

tataḥ prajavitāśvena rathena rathināṁ varaḥ
harīnabhyahanatkrodhāccharajālairakampanaḥ
Then on a car drawn by moving steeds, Akampana from a distance attacked the monkeys with showers of arrows.

न स्थातुं वानराः शेकुः किं पुनर्योद्धुमाहवे
अकम्पनशरैर्भग्नाः सर्व एव प्रदुद्रुवुः

na sthātuṁ vānarāḥ śekuḥ kiṁ punaryoddhumāhave
akampanaśarairbhagnāḥ sarva eva pradudruvuḥ
Thereat the monkeys could not so much as maintain their ground in the field, and how could they fight?

तान्मृत्युवशमापन्नानकम्पनवशं गतान्
समीक्ष्य हनुमाञ्ज्ञातीनुपतस्थे महाबलः

tānmṛtyuvaśamāpannānakampanavaśaṁ gatān
samīkṣya hanumāñjñātīnupatasthe mahābalaḥ

Broken by the arrows of Akampana, they began to fly. and the exceedingly strong Hanuman, seeing his kindred come under the masterdom of Death and follow the course pursued by the shafts of Akampana, advanced (to the conflict). And seeing that mighty monkey, all those heroic prime monkeys together surrounded (Hanuman) in the field.

व्यवस्थितं हनूमन्तं ते दृष्ट्वा हरियूथपाः
बभूवुर्बलवन्तो हि बलवन्तमुपाश्रिताः

vyavasthitaṁ hanūmantaṁ te dṛṣṭvā hariyūthapāḥ
babhūvurbalavanto hi balavantamupāśritāḥ
Those best of monkeys, seeing Hanuman stay, grew strong by relying on that strong one.

अकम्पनस्तु शैलाभं हनूमन्तमवस्थितम्
महेन्द्र इव धाराभिः शरैरभिववर्ष ह

akampanastu śailābhaṁ hanūmantamavasthitam
mahendra iva dhārābhiḥ śarairabhivavarṣa ha
And even as the great Indra shower down rain, Akampana showered shafts on Hanuman resembling a mountain-summit in grandeur.

अचिन्तयित्वा बाणौघाञ्शरीरे पतिताञ्शितान्
अकम्पनवधार्थाय मनो दध्रे महाबलः

acintayitvā bāṇaughāñśarīre patitāñśitān
akampanavadhārthāya mano dadhre mahābalaḥ
And without casting a thought on the showers of arrows poured on his person, that monkey gifted with exceeding strength, set his heart on compassing the death of Akampana.

स प्रहस्य महातेजा हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
अभिदुद्राव तद्रक्षः कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्

sa prahasya mahātejā hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
abhidudrāva tadrakṣaḥ kampayanniva medinīm
And laughing, that exceedingly energetic offspring of the Wind-god rushed after that Raksasa, as if making the Earth herself tremble.

तस्याभिनर्दमानस्य दीप्यमानस्य तेजसा
बभूव रूपं दुर्धर्षं दीप्तस्येव विभावसोः

tasyābhinardamānasya dīpyamānasya tejasā
babhūva rūpaṁ durdharṣaṁ dīptasyeva vibhāvasoḥ
The form of that one roaring and flaming up in energy, was irresistible, like to the appearance of a flaming fire.

आत्मानं त्वप्रहरणं ज्ञात्वा क्रोधसमन्वितः
शैलमुत्पाटयामास वेगेन हरिपुंगवः

ātmānaṁ tvapraharaṇaṁ jñātvā krodhasamanvitaḥ
śailamutpāṭayāmāsa vegena haripuṁgavaḥ
And thinking that he was unfurnished with any arms, that foremost of monkeys, waxing wroth, vehemently rooted up a hill.

तं गृहीत्वा महाशैलं पाणिनैकेन मारुतिः
विनद्य सुमहानादं भ्रामयामास वीर्यवान्

taṁ gṛhītvā mahāśailaṁ pāṇinaikena mārutiḥ
vinadya sumahānādaṁ bhrāmayāmāsa vīryavān
And taking that huge hill, the Wind-god's son endowed with prowess, sending up a tremendous roar, began to whirl it with a single arm.

ततस्तमभिदुद्राव राक्षसेन्द्रमकम्पनम्
यथा हि नमुचिं संख्ये वज्रेणेव पुरंदरः

tatastamabhidudrāva rākṣasendramakampanam
yathā hi namuciṁ saṁkhye vajreṇeva puraṁdaraḥ
As of yore Purandara had in encounter pursued Namuchi with the thunder-bolt, (Hanuman) pursued that best of RaksasasAkampana.

अकम्पनस्तु तद्दृष्ट्वा गिरिशृङ्गं समुद्यतम्
दूरादेव महाबाणैरर्धचन्द्रैर्व्यदारयत्

akampanastu taddṛṣṭvā giriśṛṅgaṁ samudyatam
dūrādeva mahābāṇairardhacandrairvyadārayat
Akampana, seeing that uplifted crag, from a distance cut it off with mighty crescent-shaped shafts.

तत्पर्वताग्रमाकाशे रक्षोबाणविदारितम्
विकीर्णं पतितं दृष्ट्वा हनूमान्क्रोधमूर्छितः

tatparvatāgramākāśe rakṣobāṇavidāritam
vikīrṇaṁ patitaṁ dṛṣṭvā hanūmānkrodhamūrchitaḥ
And finding that mountain top severed by the shafts of the Raksasa and scattered in pieces, Hanuman was seized with a mighty wrath.

सोऽश्वकर्णं समासाद्य रोषदर्पान्वितो हरिः
तूर्णमुत्पाटयामास महागिरिमिवोच्छ्रितम्

so'śvakarṇaṁ samāsādya roṣadarpānvito hariḥ
tūrṇamutpāṭayāmāsa mahāgirimivocchritam
That monkey, wrought up with rage and pride, grasping an Asvakarna elevated like to a hill, at once uprooted it.

तं गृहीत्वा महास्कन्धं सोऽश्वकर्णं महाद्युतिः
प्रहस्य परया प्रीत्या भ्रामयामास संयुगे

taṁ gṛhītvā mahāskandhaṁ so'śvakarṇaṁ mahādyutiḥ
prahasya parayā prītyā bhrāmayāmāsa saṁyuge
And taking that broad-shouldered Asvakarma, that one furnished with high splendour, with great glee whirled it above the ground.

प्रधावन्नुरुवेगेन प्रभञ्जंस्तरसा द्रुमान्
हनूमान्परमक्रुद्धश्चरणैर्दारयत्क्षितिम्

pradhāvannuruvegena prabhañjaṁstarasā drumān
hanūmānparamakruddhaścaraṇairdārayatkṣitim
Thereat rushing a main vehemently (Akampana) speedily broke the trees. And (seeing this) Hanuman, transported with passion, rived the earth with his kicks.

गजांश्च सगजारोहान्सरथान्रथिनस्तथा
जघान हनुमान्धीमान्राक्षसांश्च पदातिकान्

gajāṁśca sagajārohānsarathānrathinastathā
jaghāna hanumāndhīmānrākṣasāṁśca padātikān
And Hanuman slaughtered elephants, and the riders thereof, and cars with their riders, and dreadful Raksasas and footmen.

तमन्तकमिव क्रुद्धं समरे प्राणहारिणम्
हनूमन्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य राक्षसा विप्रदुद्रुवुः

tamantakamiva kruddhaṁ samare prāṇahāriṇam
hanūmantamabhiprekṣya rākṣasā vipradudruvuḥ
Seeing the enraged Hanuman resembling the Finisher armed with trees and destructive, the Raksasas began to fly fast.

तमापतन्तं संक्रुद्धं राक्षसानां भयावहम्
ददर्शाकम्पनो वीरश्चुक्रोध च ननाद च

tamāpatantaṁ saṁkruddhaṁ rākṣasānāṁ bhayāvaham
dadarśākampano vīraścukrodha ca nanāda ca
Seeing that one enraged, terrific to the Raks asas, the heroic Akampana was agitated greatly and sent up shouts.

स चतुर्दशभिर्बाणैः शितैर्देहविदारणैः
निर्बिभेद हनूमन्तं महावीर्यमकम्पनः

sa caturdaśabhirbāṇaiḥ śitairdehavidāraṇaiḥ
nirbibheda hanūmantaṁ mahāvīryamakampanaḥ
Akampana pierced Hanuman endowed with exceeding prowess with four and ten shafts, sharpened and capable of cleaving the bodies of people.

स तथा प्रतिविद्धस्तु बह्वीभिः शरवृष्टिभिः
हनूमान्ददृशे वीरः प्ररूढ इव सानुमान्

sa tathā pratividdhastu bahvībhiḥ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
hanūmāndadṛśe vīraḥ prarūḍha iva sānumān
And thus covered with iron arrows and whetted darts, that hero Hanuman-looked like a hill covered with trees.

ततोऽन्यं वृक्षमुत्पाट्य कृत्वा वेगमनुत्तमम्
शिरस्यभिजघानाशु राक्षसेन्द्रमकम्पनम्

tato'nyaṁ vṛkṣamutpāṭya kṛtvā vegamanuttamam
śirasyabhijaghānāśu rākṣasendramakampanam
Then uprooting another tree, (Hanuman) summoning up hi best impetuosity, swiftly hit Akampana foremost of Raksasas-on the head.

स वृक्षेण हतस्तेन सक्रोधेन महात्मना
राक्षसो वानरेन्द्रेण पपात स ममार च

sa vṛkṣeṇa hatastena sakrodhena mahātmanā
rākṣaso vānarendreṇa papāta sa mamāra ca
And slain with that tree by that high souled monkeys chief wrought up with passion that Raksasas fell down and died.

तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं भूमौ राक्षसेन्द्रमकम्पनम्
व्यथिता राक्षसाः सर्वे क्षितिकम्प इव द्रुमाः

taṁ dṛṣṭvā nihataṁ bhūmau rākṣasendramakampanam
vyathitā rākṣasāḥ sarve kṣitikampa iva drumāḥ
Seeing that foremost of Raksasas-Akampanaslain (and lying) on the ground, the Raksasa were extremely aggrieved, and (appeared)like trees in an earthquake.

त्यक्तप्रहरणाः सर्वे राक्षसास्ते पराजिताः
लङ्कामभिययुस्त्रस्ता वानरैस्तैरभिद्रुताः

tyaktapraharaṇāḥ sarve rākṣasāste parājitāḥ
laṅkāmabhiyayustrastā vānaraistairabhidrutāḥ
And those Raksasas defeated, leaving their arms behind, made for Lanka in fear, pursued by the monkeys.

ते मुक्तकेशाः संभ्रान्ता भग्नमानाः पराजिताः
स्रवच्छ्रमजलैरङ्गैः श्वसन्तो विप्रदुद्रुवुः

te muktakeśāḥ saṁbhrāntā bhagnamānāḥ parājitāḥ
sravacchramajalairaṅgaiḥ śvasanto vipradudruvuḥ
And with their hair flowing loosely, (the Raks asas), afflicted with affright, and dispirited and beaten, fled fast, with the water of fatigue running down their persons.

अन्योन्यं प्रममन्तुस्ते विविशुर्नगरं भयात्
पृष्ठतस्ते सुसंमूढाः प्रेक्षमाणा मुहुर्मुहुः

anyonyaṁ pramamantuste viviśurnagaraṁ bhayāt
pṛṣṭhataste susaṁmūḍhāḥ prekṣamāṇā muhurmuhuḥ
And crushing down each other, they entered the city in a panic, momentarily casting their looks behind them.

तेषु लङ्कां प्रविष्टेषु राक्षसेषु महाबलाः
समेत्य हरयः सर्वे हनूमन्तमपूजयन्

teṣu laṅkāṁ praviṣṭeṣu rākṣaseṣu mahābalāḥ
sametya harayaḥ sarve hanūmantamapūjayan
When the Raksasas had entered Lanka, the exceedingly mighty monkeys, assembled together, paid homage to Hanuman.

सोऽपि प्रहृष्टस्तान्सर्वान्हरीन्संप्रत्यपूजयत्
हनूमान्सत्त्वसंपन्नो यथार्हमनुकूलतः

so'pi prahṛṣṭastānsarvānharīnsaṁpratyapūjayat
hanūmānsattvasaṁpanno yathārhamanukūlataḥ
And Hanuman, gifted with strength, honoured the seniors each as he deserved in consideration of his lineage.

विनेदुश्च यथा प्राणं हरयो जितकाशिनः
चकर्षुश्च पुनस्तत्र सप्राणानेव राक्षसान्

vineduśca yathā prāṇaṁ harayo jitakāśinaḥ
cakarṣuśca punastatra saprāṇāneva rākṣasān
The monkeys eager for victory shouted with might and main, and began to drag the Raksasas with the view of taking their lives.

अपूजयन्देवगणास्तदा कपिं; स्वयं च रामोऽतिबलश्च लक्ष्मणः
तथैव सुग्रीवमुखाः प्लवंगमा; विभीषणश्चैव महाबलस्तदा

apūjayandevagaṇāstadā kapiṁ; svayaṁ ca rāmo'tibalaśca lakṣmaṇaḥ
tathaiva sugrīvamukhāḥ plavaṁgamā; vibhīṣaṇaścaiva mahābalastadā

That mighty monkey-son to the Wind godhaving destroyed the Raksasas and arrived (in the midst of the host), attained heroic glory, even as did Visnu, having slain that destroyer of enemies-the mighty and dreadful Asura possessed of exceeding strength, stationed in the ban of the forces. And then the deities and Rama himself and the highly powerful Laksmana, also the monkeys headed by Sugriva, and Vibhisana endowed with great strength, honoured that monkey.

अकम्पनवधं श्रुत्वा क्रुद्धो वै राक्षसेश्वरः
किंचिद्दीनमुखश्चापि सचिवांस्तानुदैक्षत

akampanavadhaṁ śrutvā kruddho vai rākṣaseśvaraḥ
kiṁciddīnamukhaścāpi sacivāṁstānudaikṣata
Hearing that Akampana had been killed, the lord of Raksasas, overwhelmed with anger, with his face somewhat fallen, cast his eyes on his counsellors.

स तु ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तं तु मन्त्रिभिः संविचार्य च
पुरीं परिययौ लङ्कां सर्वान्गुल्मानवेक्षितुम्

sa tu dhyātvā muhūrtaṁ tu mantribhiḥ saṁvicārya ca
purīṁ pariyayau laṅkāṁ sarvāngulmānavekṣitum
Then pondering and reflecting for a while, in the forenoon he went round the city of Lanka for inspecting the barracks.

तां राक्षसगणैर्गुप्तां गुल्मैर्बहुभिरावृताम्
ददर्श नगरीं लङ्कां पताकाध्वजमालिनीम्

tāṁ rākṣasagaṇairguptāṁ gulmairbahubhirāvṛtām
dadarśa nagarīṁ laṅkāṁ patākādhvajamālinīm
The king surveyed the city guarded by the Rakssasas, covered with innumerable barracks, and crowned with ensigns and standards,

रुद्धां तु नगरीं दृष्ट्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
उवाचामर्षितः काले प्रहस्तं युद्धकोविदम्

ruddhāṁ tu nagarīṁ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
uvācāmarṣitaḥ kāle prahastaṁ yuddhakovidam
Seeing the city besieged, Ravana-lord of the Raksasas-seasonably spoke words of welfare to Prahasta skilled in fight.

पुरस्योपनिविष्टस्य सहसा पीडितस्य च
नान्यं युद्धात्प्रपश्यामि मोक्षं युद्धविशारद

purasyopaniviṣṭasya sahasā pīḍitasya ca
nānyaṁ yuddhātprapaśyāmi mokṣaṁ yuddhaviśārada
"Save battle, deliverance find I none for the city suddenly beleaguered and put to straits.

अहं वा कुम्भकर्णो वा त्वं वा सेनापतिर्मम
इन्द्रजिद्वा निकुम्भो वा वहेयुर्भारमीदृशम्

ahaṁ vā kumbhakarṇo vā tvaṁ vā senāpatirmama
indrajidvā nikumbho vā vaheyurbhāramīdṛśam
And this strain must be borne by these versed in warfare-me or Kumbhakarna or you-my general or Indrajit or Nikumbha.

स त्वं बलमितः शीघ्रमादाय परिगृह्य च
विजयायाभिनिर्याहि यत्र सर्वे वनौकसः

sa tvaṁ balamitaḥ śīghramādāya parigṛhya ca
vijayāyābhiniryāhi yatra sarve vanaukasaḥ
Therefore do you from this place, speedily taking this force, march to where the monkeys are, for securing victory (in the encounter).

निर्याणादेव ते नूनं चपला हरिवाहिनी
नर्दतां राक्षसेन्द्राणां श्रुत्वा नादं द्रविष्यति

niryāṇādeva te nūnaṁ capalā harivāhinī
nardatāṁ rākṣasendrāṇāṁ śrutvā nādaṁ draviṣyati
