Charged at all points by nur bers of monkeys armed with fire-brands, those firece-eyed (Raks asas) that guarded the gates.* suddenly fled away. *Araksastha-according to some means gates. According to others, a gulma or division of an army.

गोपुराट्ट प्रतोलीषु चर्यासु विविधासु च
प्रासादेषु च संहृष्टाः ससृजुस्ते हुताशनम्

gopurāṭṭa pratolīṣu caryāsu vividhāsu ca
prāsādeṣu ca saṁhṛṣṭāḥ sasṛjuste hutāśanam
Thereat (the monkeys) delighted set fire to gates and upper apartments and spacious highways and various by-ways and edifices.

तेषां गृहसहस्राणि ददाह हुतभुक्तदा
आवासान्राक्षसानां च सर्वेषां गृहमेधिनाम्

teṣāṁ gṛhasahasrāṇi dadāha hutabhuktadā
āvāsānrākṣasānāṁ ca sarveṣāṁ gṛhamedhinām

The fire' burnt their mansions by thousands; and mountain-like superstructures toppled headiong to the earth. 1. Hutabhuk-lit. eater of sacrificial offspring's, a designation of fire. 2. According to the commentator this refers to the fire lighted by the monkeys. I differ.

विमानेषु प्रसुप्ताश्च दह्यमाना वराङ्गनाः
त्यक्ताभरणसंयोगा हाहेत्युच्चैर्विचुक्रुशः

vimāneṣu prasuptāśca dahyamānā varāṅganāḥ
tyaktābharaṇasaṁyogā hāhetyuccairvicukruśaḥ
And superb damsels asleep in lofty edifices, being burnt, cast away their ornaments and shrieked bitterly saying "Alas! Woe is me". * Vimana, according to Ramanuja, is a sevenstoried edifice.

तत्र चाग्निपरीतानि निपेतुर्भवनान्यपि
वज्रिवज्रहतानीव शिखराणि महागिरेः

tatra cāgniparītāni nipeturbhavanānyapi
vajrivajrahatānīva śikharāṇi mahāgireḥ
Consumed by the fire, buildings began to drop down like the summits of a mighty mountain smite with the thunder-bolt of the thunderer.

तानि निर्दह्यमानानि दूरतः प्रचकाशिरे
हिमवच्छिखराणीव दीप्तौषधिवनानि च

tāni nirdahyamānāni dūrataḥ pracakāśire
himavacchikharāṇīva dīptauṣadhivanāni ca
And those burning, appeared from a distance like the peaks of Himalaya aglow.

हर्म्याग्रैर्दह्यमानैश्च ज्वालाप्रज्वलितैरपि
रात्रौ सा दृश्यते लङ्का पुष्पितैरिव किंशुकैः

harmyāgrairdahyamānaiśca jvālāprajvalitairapi
rātrau sā dṛśyate laṅkā puṣpitairiva kiṁśukaiḥ
In consequence of those tops of the edifices burning and of the living flames, that night Lanka looked as if swarming with flowering Kinsukas.

हस्त्यध्यक्षैर्गजैर्मुक्तैर्मुक्तैश्च तुरगैरपि
बभूव लङ्का लोकान्ते भ्रान्तग्राह इवार्णवः

hastyadhyakṣairgajairmuktairmuktaiśca turagairapi
babhūva laṅkā lokānte bhrāntagrāha ivārṇavaḥ
With elephant-riders, and elephants, and steeds let loose, Lanka appeared like the Ocean at the hour of Universal tumbling, with its ferocious aquatic animals whirling in wild chaos.

अश्वं मुक्तं गजो दृष्ट्वा कच्चिद्भीतोऽपसर्पति
भीतो भीतं गजं दृष्ट्वा क्वचिदश्वो निवर्तते

aśvaṁ muktaṁ gajo dṛṣṭvā kaccidbhīto'pasarpati
bhīto bhītaṁ gajaṁ dṛṣṭvā kvacidaśvo nivartate
Sometimes, an elephant seeing a steed let loose, was flying away in fear, and sometimes a horse seeing a frightened elephant, was stopping, himself seized with fear.

सा बभूव मुहूर्तेन हरिभिर्दीपिता पुरी
लोकस्यास्य क्षये घोरे प्रदीप्तेव वसुंधरा

sā babhūva muhūrtena haribhirdīpitā purī
lokasyāsya kṣaye ghore pradīpteva vasuṁdharā
In a short time that city set on fire by the monkeys, looked like the earth glowing at the time of the Universal dissolution.

नारी जनस्य धूमेन व्याप्तस्योच्चैर्विनेदुषः
स्वनो ज्वलनतप्तस्य शुश्रुवे दशयोजनम्

nārī janasya dhūmena vyāptasyoccairvineduṣaḥ
svano jvalanataptasya śuśruve daśayojanam
The cries of the females amidst the drift of smoke, heated by the flames, could be heard from an hundred Yojanas.

प्रदग्धकायानपरान्राक्षसान्निर्गतान्बहिः
सहसाभ्युत्पतन्ति स्म हरयोऽथ युयुत्सवः

pradagdhakāyānaparānrākṣasānnirgatānbahiḥ
sahasābhyutpatanti sma harayo'tha yuyutsavaḥ
As Raksasas having their bodies burnt came out of houses, monkeys eager for encounter on a sudden sprung upon them.

उद्घुष्टं वानराणां च राक्षसानां च निस्वनः
दिशो दश समुद्रं च पृथिवीं चान्वनादयत्

udghuṣṭaṁ vānarāṇāṁ ca rākṣasānāṁ ca nisvanaḥ
diśo daśa samudraṁ ca pṛthivīṁ cānvanādayat
The shouts of the monkeys and the cries of the Raksasas made the ten cardinal quarters and the ocean and the Earth resound.

विशल्यौ तु महात्मानौ तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
असंभ्रान्तौ जगृहतुस्तावुभौ धनुषी वरे

viśalyau tu mahātmānau tāvubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau
asaṁbhrāntau jagṛhatustāvubhau dhanuṣī vare
On those high-souled ones both Rama and Laksmana-having been cured of their wounds, possessing themselves in calmness, took up their excellent bows.

ततो विस्फारयाणस्य रामस्य धनुरुत्तमम्
बभूव तुमुलः शब्दो राक्षसानां भयावहः

tato visphārayāṇasya rāmasya dhanuruttamam
babhūva tumulaḥ śabdo rākṣasānāṁ bhayāvahaḥ
Rama drew that best of bows. And thereat there was heard a tremendous twang striking terror into the Raksasas,

अशोभत तदा रामो धनुर्विस्फारयन्महत्
भगवानिव संक्रुद्धो भवो वेदमयं धनुः

aśobhata tadā rāmo dhanurvisphārayanmahat
bhagavāniva saṁkruddho bhavo vedamayaṁ dhanuḥ
And drawing his redoubtable bow, Rama appeared like the reverend enraged Bhava, drawing his bow having sounds, and instinct with Brahma energy.

वानरोद्घुष्टघोषश्च राक्षसानां च निस्वनः
ज्याशब्दश्चापि रामस्य त्रयं व्याप दिशो दश

vānarodghuṣṭaghoṣaśca rākṣasānāṁ ca nisvanaḥ
jyāśabdaścāpi rāmasya trayaṁ vyāpa diśo daśa
The ululations of the monkeys and the cries of the Raksasas and the rattle of Rama's bowthese three filled the ten cardinal quarters.

तस्य कार्मुकमुक्तैश्च शरैस्तत्पुरगोपुरम्
कैलासशृङ्गप्रतिमं विकीर्णमपतद्भुवि

tasya kārmukamuktaiśca śaraistatpuragopuram
kailāsaśṛṅgapratimaṁ vikīrṇamapatadbhuvi
With the shafts discharged from his bow, the gieway of the city resembling the summit of 1. islas. was crushed in pieces, scattered around cr the ground.

ततो रामशरान्दृष्ट्वा विमानेषु गृहेषु च
संनाहो राक्षसेन्द्राणां तुमुलः समपद्यत

tato rāmaśarāndṛṣṭvā vimāneṣu gṛheṣu ca
saṁnāho rākṣasendrāṇāṁ tumulaḥ samapadyata
See cs Rama's shafts in cars and dwellings, the preparations for conflict were pushed on with great viour.

तेषां संनह्यमानानां सिंहनादं च कुर्वताम्
शर्वरी राक्षसेन्द्राणां रौद्रीव समपद्यत

teṣāṁ saṁnahyamānānāṁ siṁhanādaṁ ca kurvatām
śarvarī rākṣasendrāṇāṁ raudrīva samapadyata
An' in consequence of the foremost Raksasas preparing for fight, and emitting roars, that night appeared like the Fatal Night itself.

आदिष्टा वानरेन्द्रास्ते सुग्रीवेण महात्मना
आसन्ना द्वारमासाद्य युध्यध्वं प्लवगर्षभाः

ādiṣṭā vānarendrāste sugrīveṇa mahātmanā
āsannā dvāramāsādya yudhyadhvaṁ plavagarṣabhāḥ
The foremost monkeys were directed by the high-souled Sugriva, saying, “You monkeys, do you fight, approaching the gate lying at hand.

यश्च वो वितथं कुर्यात्तत्र तत्र व्यवस्थितः
स हन्तव्योऽभिसंप्लुत्य राजशासनदूषकः

yaśca vo vitathaṁ kuryāttatra tatra vyavasthitaḥ
sa hantavyo'bhisaṁplutya rājaśāsanadūṣakaḥ
But he that fly from his ranks, should be slain by main force.

तेषु वानरमुख्येषु दीप्तोल्कोज्ज्वलपाणिषु
स्थितेषु द्वारमासाद्य रावणं मन्युराविशत्

teṣu vānaramukhyeṣu dīptolkojjvalapāṇiṣu
sthiteṣu dvāramāsādya rāvaṇaṁ manyurāviśat
As the principal monkeys stationed themselves at the gate, equipped with fire-brands, wrath took possession of Ravana.

तस्य जृम्भितविक्षेपाद्व्यामिश्रा वै दिशो दश
रूपवानिव रुद्रस्य मन्युर्गात्रेष्वदृश्यत

tasya jṛmbhitavikṣepādvyāmiśrā vai diśo daśa
rūpavāniva rudrasya manyurgātreṣvadṛśyata
And as he yawned, the wind (blowing) from his mouth), filled the ten cardinal regions; and his wrath resembled that appearing in the person of Rudra.

स निकुम्भं च कुम्भं च कुम्भकर्णात्मजावुभौ
प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धो राक्षसैर्बहुभिः सह

sa nikumbhaṁ ca kumbhaṁ ca kumbhakarṇātmajāvubhau
preṣayāmāsa saṁkruddho rākṣasairbahubhiḥ saha
And wrought up with a mighty rage, he sent forth Kumbha and Nikumbha-both sons of Kumbhakarna-in company with innumerable Raksasas.

शशास चैव तान्सर्वान्राक्षसान्राक्षसेश्वरः
राक्षसा गच्छतात्रैव सिंहनादं च नादयन्

śaśāsa caiva tānsarvānrākṣasānrākṣaseśvaraḥ
rākṣasā gacchatātraiva siṁhanādaṁ ca nādayan
Setting up leonine roars, he commanded all those highly powerful Raksasas, saying, "Do you go this very day for battle."

ततस्तु चोदितास्तेन राक्षसा ज्वलितायुधाः
लङ्काया निर्ययुर्वीराः प्रणदन्तः पुनः पुनः

tatastu coditāstena rākṣasā jvalitāyudhāḥ
laṅkāyā niryayurvīrāḥ praṇadantaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
Thus directed, those heroic heroic Raksasas, equipped with flaming weapons, went out, roaring again and again.

गन्धमाल्यमधूत्सेकसंमोदित महानिलम्
घोरं शूरजनाकीर्णं महाम्बुधरनिस्वनम्

gandhamālyamadhūtsekasaṁmodita mahānilam
ghoraṁ śūrajanākīrṇaṁ mahāmbudharanisvanam
Seeing the army of the Raksasas incapable of being coped with advance, the monkey-forces began to move and send up loud cheers.

तं दृष्ट्वा बलमायान्तं राक्षसानां सुदारुणम्
संचचाल प्लवंगानां बलमुच्चैर्ननाद च

taṁ dṛṣṭvā balamāyāntaṁ rākṣasānāṁ sudāruṇam
saṁcacāla plavaṁgānāṁ balamuccairnanāda ca
Thereat that array of Raksasas vehemently sprang forward before the force of the foe, like to insects plunging into a flame.

तेषां भुजपरामर्शव्यामृष्टपरिघाशनि
राक्षसानां बलं श्रेष्ठं भूयस्तरमशोभत

teṣāṁ bhujaparāmarśavyāmṛṣṭaparighāśani
rākṣasānāṁ balaṁ śreṣṭhaṁ bhūyastaramaśobhata
And whirling with their arms bludgeons and asanis, that army of Raksasas appeared exceedingly grand.

तथैवाप्यपरे तेषां कपीनामसिभिः शितैः
प्रवीरानभितो जघ्नुर्घोररूपा निशाचराः

tathaivāpyapare teṣāṁ kapīnāmasibhiḥ śitaiḥ
pravīrānabhito jaghnurghorarūpā niśācarāḥ
In the same way other grim-visaged nightrangers slew with sharpened swords the foremost of monkeys on all sides.

घ्नन्तमन्यं जघानान्यः पातयन्तमपातयत्
गर्हमाणं जगर्हान्ये दशन्तमपरेऽदशत्

ghnantamanyaṁ jaghānānyaḥ pātayantamapātayat
garhamāṇaṁ jagarhānye daśantamapare'daśat

And one about to slay another was himself slain by the latter; and one, about to bring another down, was himself brought down (by his adversary, and one that was railing at another, was in turn rebuked by his enemy; and one who was going to bite his foe, was himself bitten by him.

देहीत्यन्ये ददात्यन्यो ददामीत्यपरः पुनः
किं क्लेशयसि तिष्ठेति तत्रान्योन्यं बभाषिरे

dehītyanye dadātyanyo dadāmītyaparaḥ punaḥ
kiṁ kleśayasi tiṣṭheti tatrānyonyaṁ babhāṣire
One was crying 'Give.'* and his adversary anon give; and another, again said, I will give. Why put yourself to trouble? Stay. *Battle.

समुद्यतमहाप्रासं मुष्टिशूलासिसंकुलम्
प्रावर्तत महारौद्रं युद्धं वानररक्षसाम्

samudyatamahāprāsaṁ muṣṭiśūlāsisaṁkulam
prāvartata mahāraudraṁ yuddhaṁ vānararakṣasām

Thus there did they accost each other. And there was waged a terrific encounter between the monkeys and the Raksasas, in which arms lay scattered about; and armour and weapons strewn around; and mighty prasas' were upraised; and which was fought with blows and darts and swords and Kuntalas? And in that conflict the Raksasas slaughtered monkeys by tens and sevens. 1. A bearded dart. 2. What could this be like? The commentator is mute. Wilson has Kuntalik-butter-knife or scoop. Kuntala may, however, mean a plough.

विस्रस्तकेशरसनं विमुक्तकवचध्वजम्
बलं राक्षसमालम्ब्य वानराः पर्यवारयन्

visrastakeśarasanaṁ vimuktakavacadhvajam
balaṁ rākṣasamālambya vānarāḥ paryavārayan

Then the monkeys hemmed in the Raksasaforces, with their apparels falling off and with their mail and standards strewn around. swords and Kuntalas? And in that conflict the Raksasas slaughtered monkeys by tens and sevens. 1. A bearded dart. 2. What could this be like? The commentator is mute. Wilson has Kuntalik-butter-knife or scoop. Kuntala may, however, mean a plough.

प्रवृत्ते संकुले तस्मिन्घोरे वीरजनक्षये
अङ्गदः कम्पनं वीरमाससाद रणोत्सुकः

pravṛtte saṁkule tasminghore vīrajanakṣaye
aṅgadaḥ kampanaṁ vīramāsasāda raṇotsukaḥ
On that furious and destructive carnage proceeding, Angada eager for encounter, approached the heroic Kampana.

आहूय सोऽङ्गदं कोपात्ताडयामास वेगितः
गदया कम्पनः पूर्वं स चचाल भृशाहतः

āhūya so'ṅgadaṁ kopāttāḍayāmāsa vegitaḥ
gadayā kampanaḥ pūrvaṁ sa cacāla bhṛśāhataḥ
Thereat, challenging Angada in wrath, he assailed him with impetuosity. And Kampana dealt a blow to Angada with his mace; and thereat, wounded with it, he reeled.

स संज्ञां प्राप्य तेजस्वी चिक्षेप शिखरं गिरेः
अर्दितश्च प्रहारेण कम्पनः पतितो भुवि

sa saṁjñāṁ prāpya tejasvī cikṣepa śikharaṁ gireḥ
arditaśca prahāreṇa kampanaḥ patito bhuvi
Then regaining his senses, that energetic one hurled a mountain-top. Borne down by the blow, Kampana dropped down to the earth.

हतप्रवीरा व्यथिता राक्षसेन्द्रचमूस्तदा
जगामाभिमुखी सा तु कुम्भकर्णसुतो यतः
आपतन्तीं च वेगेन कुम्भस्तां सान्त्वयच्चमूम्

hatapravīrā vyathitā rākṣasendracamūstadā
jagāmābhimukhī sā tu kumbhakarṇasuto yataḥ
āpatantīṁ ca vegena kumbhastāṁ sāntvayaccamūm
Thereupon the force of the lord of the Raks asas, having its foremost heroes slain, and aggrieved thereat, went to where Kumbhakarma's son was.

स धनुर्धन्विनां श्रेष्ठः प्रगृह्य सुसमाहितः
मुमोचाशीविषप्रख्याञ्शरान्देहविदारणान्

sa dhanurdhanvināṁ śreṣṭhaḥ pragṛhya susamāhitaḥ
mumocāśīviṣaprakhyāñśarāndehavidāraṇān
And heedfully taking his bow, that first of bowmen discharged shafts resembling venomous serpents capable of piercing the body.

तस्य तच्छुशुभे भूयः सशरं धनुरुत्तमम्
विद्युदैरावतार्चिष्मद्द्वितीयेन्द्रधनुर्यथा

tasya tacchuśubhe bhūyaḥ saśaraṁ dhanuruttamam
vidyudairāvatārciṣmaddvitīyendradhanuryathā
And his excellent bow with shafts shone resplendent like the very bow of Indra himself affluent with the splendour of Airavata and lightning.

आकर्णकृष्टमुक्तेन जघान द्विविदं तदा
तेन हाटकपुङ्खेन पत्रिणा पत्रवाससा

ākarṇakṛṣṭamuktena jaghāna dvividaṁ tadā
tena hāṭakapuṅkhena patriṇā patravāsasā
Then drawing his bow to its utmost bent, he hit Dvivida with a feathered shaft knobbed with gold.

सहसाभिहतस्तेन विप्रमुक्तपदः स्फुरन्
निपपाताद्रिकूटाभो विह्वलः प्लवगोत्तमः

sahasābhihatastena vipramuktapadaḥ sphuran
nipapātādrikūṭābho vihvalaḥ plavagottamaḥ
Suddenly wounded with it, that best of monkeys having the splendour of Trikuta, fell down senseless to the earth, stretching his legs wide.

तां शिलां तु प्रचिक्षेप राक्षसाय महाबलः
बिभेद तां शिलां कुम्भः प्रसन्नैः पञ्चभिः शरैः

tāṁ śilāṁ tu pracikṣepa rākṣasāya mahābalaḥ
bibheda tāṁ śilāṁ kumbhaḥ prasannaiḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ

Mainda, seeing his brother, broken in mighty encounter, furiously rushed forward, taking a gigantic crag; and that one possessed of great strength, hurled it at the Raksasa. And thereat Kumbha "severed that crag with five shafts discharged (from his bow).

संधाय चान्यं सुमुखं शरमाशीविषोपमम्
आजघान महातेजा वक्षसि द्विविदाग्रजम्

saṁdhāya cānyaṁ sumukhaṁ śaramāśīviṣopamam
ājaghāna mahātejā vakṣasi dvividāgrajam
Then aiming other fair-headed arrows resembling venomous snakes, that exceedingly energetic one smote Dvivida's elder brother in the chest.

स तु तेन प्रहारेण मैन्दो वानरयूथपः
मर्मण्यभिहतस्तेन पपात भुवि मूर्छितः

sa tu tena prahāreṇa maindo vānarayūthapaḥ
marmaṇyabhihatastena papāta bhuvi mūrchitaḥ
And struck (with those arrows), that leader of monkey-bands, Mainda, with his marrow pierced therewith, fell down to the earth, deprived of his senses.

अङ्गदो मातुलौ दृष्ट्वा पतितौ तौ महाबलौ
अभिदुद्राव वेगेन कुम्भमुद्यतकार्मुकम्

aṅgado mātulau dṛṣṭvā patitau tau mahābalau
abhidudrāva vegena kumbhamudyatakārmukam
Angada seeing his uncles* endowed with exceeding prowess, overpowered, darted vehemently at Kumbha staying with bow upraised. *Maternal uncles.

सोऽङ्गदं विविधैर्बाणैः कुम्भो विव्याध वीर्यवान्
अकुण्ठधारैर्निशितैस्तीक्ष्णैः कनकभूषणैः

so'ṅgadaṁ vividhairbāṇaiḥ kumbho vivyādha vīryavān
akuṇṭhadhārairniśitaistīkṣṇaiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ

As he descended, Kumbha pierced him with five shafts; and as one pierce an elephant with tomaras, he also pierced (Angada) with three other arrows. And the powerful Kumbha pierced Angada with a great many arrows, sharppointed, whetted, keen and ornamented with gold.

स प्रचिच्छेद तान्सर्वान्बिभेद च पुनः शिलाः
कुम्भकर्णात्मजः श्रीमान्वालिपुत्रसमीरितान्

sa praciccheda tānsarvānbibheda ca punaḥ śilāḥ
kumbhakarṇātmajaḥ śrīmānvāliputrasamīritān

Vali's son Angada albeit pierced all over in his person, did not shake; and he kept showering on his* head stones and trees. And the graceful son of Kumbhakarna cut off and cleft all those (stone and trees) discharged by Valr's son. *Kumbha's.

आपतन्तं च संप्रेक्ष्य कुम्भो वानरयूथपम्
भ्रुवोर्विव्याध बाणाभ्यामुल्काभ्यामिव कुञ्जरम्

āpatantaṁ ca saṁprekṣya kumbho vānarayūthapam
bhruvorvivyādha bāṇābhyāmulkābhyāmiva kuñjaram
Seeing him spring up, Kumbha pierced that monkey-leader on the ground with shafts, even as one assail an elephant with fire-brands.

स चिच्छेद शितैर्बाणैः सप्तभिः कायभेदनैः
अङ्गदो विव्यथेऽभीक्ष्णं ससाद च मुमोह च

sa ciccheda śitairbāṇaiḥ saptabhiḥ kāyabhedanaiḥ
aṅgado vivyathe'bhīkṣṇaṁ sasāda ca mumoha ca
Thereat he* severed it with seven sharp shafts capable of piercing the body. And Angada experienced a sharp pang and fell down deprived of his senses. *Kumbha.

अङ्गदं व्यथितं दृष्ट्वा सीदन्तमिव सागरे
दुरासदं हरिश्रेष्ठा राघवाय न्यवेदयन्

aṅgadaṁ vyathitaṁ dṛṣṭvā sīdantamiva sāgare
durāsadaṁ hariśreṣṭhā rāghavāya nyavedayan
Seeing the invincible Angada down like ebbing sea, the foremost monkeys informed Raghava of it.

रामस्तु व्यथितं श्रुत्वा वालिपुत्रं महाहवे
व्यादिदेश हरिश्रेष्ठाञ्जाम्बवत्प्रमुखांस्ततः

rāmastu vyathitaṁ śrutvā vāliputraṁ mahāhave
vyādideśa hariśreṣṭhāñjāmbavatpramukhāṁstataḥ
Rama, hearing that Vali's son had come to grief in terrific fight, directed the principal monkeys, headed by Jambavan.

ते तु वानरशार्दूलाः श्रुत्वा रामस्य शासनम्
अभिपेतुः सुसंक्रुद्धाः कुम्भमुद्यतकार्मुकम्

te tu vānaraśārdūlāḥ śrutvā rāmasya śāsanam
abhipetuḥ susaṁkruddhāḥ kumbhamudyatakārmukam
And hearing Rama's command, the monkeys, fired with wrath, charged Kumbha, staying with his bow upraised.

ततो द्रुमशिलाहस्ताः कोपसंरक्तलोचनाः
रिरक्षिषन्तोऽभ्यपतन्नङ्गदं वानरर्षभाः

tato drumaśilāhastāḥ kopasaṁraktalocanāḥ
rirakṣiṣanto'bhyapatannaṅgadaṁ vānararṣabhāḥ
Those powerful monkeys, with their eyes crimsoned with choler and bearing rocks and trees in their hands, were engaged in defending Angada.

जाम्बवांश्च सुषेणश्च वेगदर्शी च वानरः
कुम्भकर्णात्मजं वीरं क्रुद्धाः समभिदुद्रुवुः

jāmbavāṁśca suṣeṇaśca vegadarśī ca vānaraḥ
kumbhakarṇātmajaṁ vīraṁ kruddhāḥ samabhidudruvuḥ
Jambavan and Susena and the monkey, Vegadarsi, wrought with wrath, darted against that hero-son to Kumbhakarma.

समीक्ष्यातततस्तांस्तु वानरेन्द्रान्महाबलान्
आववार शरौघेण नगेनेव जलाशयम्

samīkṣyātatatastāṁstu vānarendrānmahābalān
āvavāra śaraugheṇa nageneva jalāśayam
Seeing them spring forward; he covered up those exceedingly mighty lords of monkey, with showers of shafts, even as a crag obstruct the course of a current.

तस्य बाणचयं प्राप्य न शोकेरतिवर्तितुम्
वानरेन्द्रा महात्मानो वेलामिव महोदधिः

tasya bāṇacayaṁ prāpya na śokerativartitum
vānarendrā mahātmāno velāmiva mahodadhiḥ
Even the great deep cannot see his own shores, those high-souled lord of monkeys, coming within the range of his arrows, could not even see.

तांस्तु दृष्ट्वा हरिगणाञ्शरवृष्टिभिरर्दितान्
अङ्गदं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा भ्रातृजं प्लवगेश्वरः

tāṁstu dṛṣṭvā harigaṇāñśaravṛṣṭibhirarditān
aṅgadaṁ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā bhrātṛjaṁ plavageśvaraḥ

Seeing those monkeys sore distressed by the shafts, the king of the monkeys, Sugriva, in that conflict taking his brother's son on his back, rushed against the son of Kumbhakarna, even as a powerful lion rush at an elephant ranging on the slopes of a mountain.

उत्पाट्य च महाशैलानश्वकर्णान्धवान्बहून्
अन्यांश्च विविधान्वृक्षांश्चिक्षेप च महाबलः

utpāṭya ca mahāśailānaśvakarṇāndhavānbahūn
anyāṁśca vividhānvṛkṣāṁścikṣepa ca mahābalaḥ
That mighty monkey, uprooting many an asvakarna and other mighty trees of various kinds, discharged them (at the foe).

तां छादयन्तीमाकाशं वृक्षवृष्टिं दुरासदाम्
कुम्भकर्णात्मजः श्रीमांश्चिच्छेद निशितैः शरैः

tāṁ chādayantīmākāśaṁ vṛkṣavṛṣṭiṁ durāsadām
kumbhakarṇātmajaḥ śrīmāṁściccheda niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
By means of his sharp arrows the graceful son of Kumbhakarna cut off that down-pour of trees covering the welkin; and incapable of being resisted. And being beffled those trees looked like sataghnis.

द्रुमवर्षं तु तच्छिन्नं दृष्ट्वा कुम्भेन वीर्यवान्
वानराधिपतिः श्रीमान्महासत्त्वो न विव्यथे

drumavarṣaṁ tu tacchinnaṁ dṛṣṭvā kumbhena vīryavān
vānarādhipatiḥ śrīmānmahāsattvo na vivyathe
Seeing that shower of trees riven by Kumbha, the graceful lord of the monkeys endowed with exceeding strength and prowess, did not feel any mortification.

अवप्लुत्य ततः शीघ्रं कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्
अब्रवीत्कुपितः कुम्भं भग्नशृङ्गमिव द्विपम्

avaplutya tataḥ śīghraṁ kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram
abravītkupitaḥ kumbhaṁ bhagnaśṛṅgamiva dvipam

Suddenly attacked, he bearing those arrows, seized Kumbha's bow resembling in resplendence the very bow of Indra. And swiftly bounding up and performing that feat difficult of being achieved, he, exceedingly enraged, addressed Kumbha resembling an elephant shorn of his tusks, saying.

वरदानात्पितृव्यस्ते सहते देवदानवान्
कुम्भकर्णस्तु वीर्येण सहते च सुरासुरान्

varadānātpitṛvyaste sahate devadānavān
kumbhakarṇastu vīryeṇa sahate ca surāsurān

It is only by virtue of the boon he has received, that your uncle can bear the deities and the Danavas. But Kumbhakarna cop with the immortals and Asuras by means of his native might. And in the bow equal to Indrajit himself and in power equal to Ravana, you now in might and energy are the foremost of Raksasas.

महाविमर्दं समरे मया सह तवाद्भुतम्
अद्य भूतानि पश्यन्तु शक्रशम्बरयोरिव

mahāvimardaṁ samare mayā saha tavādbhutam
adya bhūtāni paśyantu śakraśambarayoriva
Today let all creatures witness the mighty and wonderful encounter in conflict between you and me, like to the meeting of Sakra and Sambara.

कृतमप्रतिमं कर्म दर्शितं चास्त्रकौशलम्
पातिता हरिवीराश्च त्वयैते भीमविक्रमाः

kṛtamapratimaṁ karma darśitaṁ cāstrakauśalam
pātitā harivīrāśca tvayaite bhīmavikramāḥ
Unparalleled is the feat you have performed; and you have displayed your skill in weapons. And heroic monkeys endowed with dreadful vigour, have been brought down by you.

उपालम्भभयाच्चापि नासि वीर मया हतः
कृतकर्मा परिश्रान्तो विश्रान्तः पश्य मे बलम्

upālambhabhayāccāpi nāsi vīra mayā hataḥ
kṛtakarmā pariśrānto viśrāntaḥ paśya me balam

O hero it is only because of the apprehension* of censure of the people that I do not slay you who are fatigued in consequence of the acts that you have performed. And reposing from fight, do you see my strength! *i.e. Lest people should censure me, saying, Sugriva slew Kumbha when he was fatigued in fight.

तेन सुग्रीववाक्येन सावमानेन मानितः
अग्नेराज्यहुतस्येव तेजस्तस्याभ्यवर्धत

tena sugrīvavākyena sāvamānena mānitaḥ
agnerājyahutasyeva tejastasyābhyavardhata
Being thus honoured (by Sugriva) with fair speech, (Kumbha) flamed up like a flame into which oblations have been poured.

ततः कुम्भः समुत्पत्य सुग्रीवमभिपद्य च
आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो वज्रवेगेन मुष्टिना

tataḥ kumbhaḥ samutpatya sugrīvamabhipadya ca
ājaghānorasi kruddho vajravegena muṣṭinā
Then springing up, and bringing Sugriva down, Kumbha, transported with wrath dealt a blow on his chest, like to the levin.

तस्य चर्म च पुस्फोट संजज्ञे चास्य शोणितम्
स च मुष्टिर्महावेगः प्रतिजघ्नेऽस्थिमण्डले

tasya carma ca pusphoṭa saṁjajñe cāsya śoṇitam
sa ca muṣṭirmahāvegaḥ pratijaghne'sthimaṇḍale
Thereat his skin was rent, and blood began to gush out, and the impetus of that blow broke Sugriva's bones.

तदा वेगेन तत्रासीत्तेजः प्रज्वालितं मुहुः
वज्रनिष्पेषसंजातज्वाला मेरौ यथा गिरौ

tadā vegena tatrāsīttejaḥ prajvālitaṁ muhuḥ
vajraniṣpeṣasaṁjātajvālā merau yathā girau
The vehemence (of the blow) caused a great fire to blaze up at that spot, even as the thunderbolt smiting the mountain Meru, make place blazed.

स तत्राभिहतस्तेन सुग्रीवो वानरर्षभः
मुष्टिं संवर्तयामास वज्रकल्पं महाबलः

sa tatrābhihatastena sugrīvo vānararṣabhaḥ
muṣṭiṁ saṁvartayāmāsa vajrakalpaṁ mahābalaḥ

The mighty Sugriva foremost of monkeys-sorely handled by him, fastened his fingers into a box resembling the thunder-bolt, and furnished with all the effulgence of the solar disc having a thousand rays.

अर्चिःसहस्रविकचं रविमण्डलसप्रभम्
स मुष्टिं पातयामास कुम्भस्योरसि वीर्यवान्

arciḥsahasravikacaṁ ravimaṇḍalasaprabham
sa muṣṭiṁ pātayāmāsa kumbhasyorasi vīryavān
Then that powerful one made that blow descend right on on Kumbha's breast. And agonised with that stroke, Kumbha reft of his senses, dropped like to a fire that has lost its brightness.

मुष्टिनाभिहतस्तेन निपपाताशु राक्षसः
लोहिताङ्ग इवाकाशाद्दीप्तरश्मिर्यदृच्छया

muṣṭinābhihatastena nipapātāśu rākṣasaḥ
lohitāṅga ivākāśāddīptaraśmiryadṛcchayā
And overpowered by that blow, the Raksasa anon dropped down, like to the bright Lohitanga dropping from the firmament urged on by Destiny.

कुम्भस्य पततो रूपं भग्नस्योरसि मुष्टिना
बभौ रुद्राभिपन्नस्य यथारूपं गवां पतेः

kumbhasya patato rūpaṁ bhagnasyorasi muṣṭinā
babhau rudrābhipannasya yathārūpaṁ gavāṁ pateḥ
The aspect of the falling Kumbha with his breast broken by the blow, appeared like that of the Sun routed by Rudra.

तस्मिन्हते भीमपराक्रमेण; प्लवंगमानामृषभेण युद्धे
मही सशैला सवना चचाल; भयं च रक्षांस्यधिकं विवेश

tasminhate bhīmaparākrameṇa; plavaṁgamānāmṛṣabheṇa yuddhe
mahī saśailā savanā cacāla; bhayaṁ ca rakṣāṁsyadhikaṁ viveśa
On his being slain, in encounter, by the foremost of monkeys endowed with terrific strength, the earth with her hills and woods, shook; and a mighty fear took possession of the Raksasas.

निकुम्भो भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवेण निपातितम्
प्रदहन्निव कोपेन वानरेन्द्रमवैक्षत

nikumbho bhrātaraṁ dṛṣṭvā sugrīveṇa nipātitam
pradahanniva kopena vānarendramavaikṣata
Seeing his brother slain by Sugriva, Nikumbha, gazed at the lord of the monkeys, as if consuming him with his passion.

हेमपट्टपरिक्षिप्तं वज्रविद्रुमभूषितम्
यमदण्डोपमं भीमं रक्षसां भयनाशनम्

hemapaṭṭaparikṣiptaṁ vajravidrumabhūṣitam
yamadaṇḍopamaṁ bhīmaṁ rakṣasāṁ bhayanāśanam

Then that one endowed with calmness, grasped a bludgeon entwined with wreaths, and furnished with an iron ring measuring five fingers, and resembling the top of the Mahendra;* plated with gold and embellished with diamonds and lapises, and looking like the rod of Yama himself; dreadful and capable of removing the fear of the Raksas. *The mountain, so named.

तमाविध्य महातेजाः शक्रध्वजसमं रणे
विननाद विवृत्तास्यो निकुम्भो भीमविक्रमः

tamāvidhya mahātejāḥ śakradhvajasamaṁ raṇe
vinanāda vivṛttāsyo nikumbho bhīmavikramaḥ
And whirling this, that highly powerful one, resembling the banner itself of Sakra in energy, Nikumbha possessed of terrific strength, with his mouth wide open, set up shouts.

निकुम्भो भूषणैर्भाति तेन स्म परिघेण च
यथेन्द्रधनुषा मेघः सविद्युत्स्तनयित्नुमान्

nikumbho bhūṣaṇairbhāti tena sma parigheṇa ca
yathendradhanuṣā meghaḥ savidyutstanayitnumān

With gold adorning his breast, and Angadas placed on his arms and a pair of curious and variegated ear-rings, Nikumbha, with his ornaments and that same bludgeon, appeared beautiful like a mass of roaring clouds laughing with lightning and furnished with the iris.

परिघाग्रेण पुस्फोट वातग्रन्थिर्महात्मनः
प्रजज्वाल सघोषश्च विधूम इव पावकः

parighāgreṇa pusphoṭa vātagranthirmahātmanaḥ
prajajvāla saghoṣaśca vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ

The head of that huge-bodied hero's parigha undid the conjunction of the seven' Winds and appeared? like a noiseless and smokeless flame. 1. This indicates the length of the Parigha. 2. This might refer to Kumbha as well.

सतारागणनक्षत्रं सचन्द्रं समहाग्रहम्
निकुम्भपरिघाघूर्णं भ्रमतीव नभस्तलम्

satārāgaṇanakṣatraṁ sacandraṁ samahāgraham
nikumbhaparighāghūrṇaṁ bhramatīva nabhastalam

Along with the gyration of Nikumbha's parigha the whole welkin, together with the excellent city* of the gandharvas, and the planets, stars and the moon, began to whirl. *Some say Vitapabati and some say Alaka.

दुरासदश्च संजज्ञे परिघाभरणप्रभः
क्रोधेन्धनो निकुम्भाग्निर्युगान्ताग्निरिवोत्थितः

durāsadaśca saṁjajñe parighābharaṇaprabhaḥ
krodhendhano nikumbhāgniryugāntāgnirivotthitaḥ
Nikumbha was hard to approach like to the fire of dissolution, being resplendent with the brilliance of parigha and other ornaments and having his anger for its fuels.

राक्षसा वानराश्चापि न शेकुः स्पन्दितुं भयात्
हनूमंस्तु विवृत्योरस्तस्थौ प्रमुखतो बली

rākṣasā vānarāścāpi na śekuḥ spandituṁ bhayāt
hanūmaṁstu vivṛtyorastasthau pramukhato balī
The Raksasas and monkeys did not dare stir even out of fear. And the heroic Hanuman, spreading his breast, stood before him.

परिघोपमबाहुस्तु परिघं भास्करप्रभम्
बली बलवतस्तस्य पातयामास वक्षसि

parighopamabāhustu parighaṁ bhāskaraprabham
balī balavatastasya pātayāmāsa vakṣasi
Thereat the powerful (Nikumbha) having long-arm* threw his parigha resembling the Sun at the breast of that powerful one. *Lit. arms resembling parighas.

स्थिरे तस्योरसि व्यूढे परिघः शतधा कृतः
विशीर्यमाणः सहसा उल्का शतमिवाम्बरे

sthire tasyorasi vyūḍhe parighaḥ śatadhā kṛtaḥ
viśīryamāṇaḥ sahasā ulkā śatamivāmbare
Falling on the firm and spacious breast of Hanuman it was broken into hundred pieces. The broken portions, being scattered, appeared like hundreds of fire-brands in the sky.

स तु तेन प्रहारेण चचाल च महाकपिः
परिघेण समाधूतो यथा भूमिचलेऽचलः

sa tu tena prahāreṇa cacāla ca mahākapiḥ
parigheṇa samādhūto yathā bhūmicale'calaḥ
Like to a mountain standing still even at the time of an earthquake that mighty monkey was not moved albeit struck with the parigha.

स तथाभिहतस्तेन हनूमान्प्लवगोत्तमः
मुष्टिं संवर्तयामास बलेनातिमहाबलः

sa tathābhihatastena hanūmānplavagottamaḥ
muṣṭiṁ saṁvartayāmāsa balenātimahābalaḥ
Being thus hurt that highly powerful Hanuman, the foremost of the monkeys, with great velocity clenched his fist.

तमुद्यम्य महातेजा निकुम्भोरसि वीर्यवान्
अभिचिक्षेप वेगेन वेगवान्वायुविक्रमः

tamudyamya mahātejā nikumbhorasi vīryavān
abhicikṣepa vegena vegavānvāyuvikramaḥ
With this, the powerful (monkey) gifted with great impetuosity, and resembling the wind in prowess, struck Nikumbha on his breast.

ततः पुस्फोट चर्मास्य प्रसुस्राव च शोणितम्
मुष्टिना तेन संजज्ञे ज्वाला विद्युदिवोत्थिता

tataḥ pusphoṭa carmāsya prasusrāva ca śoṇitam
muṣṭinā tena saṁjajñe jvālā vidyudivotthitā

With that fist, his (Nikumbha's) armour* was riven and blood gushed out. And a light rising out of his breast suddenly disappeared like to lightning disappearing in a mass of clouds. *Some texts read carma (skin) in the place of Varma-(armour) i.e., his skin was rent-This equally indicates Hanuman's strength.

स तु तेन प्रहारेण निकुम्भो विचचाल ह
स्वस्थश्चापि निजग्राह हनूमन्तं महाबलम्

sa tu tena prahāreṇa nikumbho vicacāla ha
svasthaścāpi nijagrāha hanūmantaṁ mahābalam
Being struck with his (Hanuman's) fist Nikumbha was greatly moved and restoring himself attacked the mighty Hanuman and pulled him up.

विचुक्रुशुस्तदा संख्ये भीमं लङ्कानिवासिनः
निकुम्भेनोद्धृतं दृष्ट्वा हनूमन्तं महाबलम्

vicukruśustadā saṁkhye bhīmaṁ laṅkānivāsinaḥ
nikumbhenoddhṛtaṁ dṛṣṭvā hanūmantaṁ mahābalam
Beholding in conflict the terrible and powerful Hanuman pulled up by Nikumbha, the residents of Lanka began to shout with joy.

स तथा ह्रियमाणोऽपि कुम्भकर्णात्मजेन हि
आजघानानिलसुतो वज्रवेगेन मुष्टिना

sa tathā hriyamāṇo'pi kumbhakarṇātmajena hi
ājaghānānilasuto vajravegena muṣṭinā
Being thus put to shame by that Raksasa, Hanuman the son of the Wind, struck him with his iron fist.

आत्मानं मोचयित्वाथ क्षितावभ्यवपद्यत
हनूमानुन्ममथाशु निकुम्भं मारुतात्मजः

ātmānaṁ mocayitvātha kṣitāvabhyavapadyata
hanūmānunmamathāśu nikumbhaṁ mārutātmajaḥ
And releasing himself from the grasp of Nikumbha, Hanuman the Wind-god's son instantly planted his foot on the earth.

परिगृह्य च बाहुभ्यां परिवृत्य शिरोधराम्
उत्पाटयामास शिरो भैरवं नदतो महत्

parigṛhya ca bāhubhyāṁ parivṛtya śirodharām
utpāṭayāmāsa śiro bhairavaṁ nadato mahat

Inflamed with ire, he, throwing down Nikumbha, began to crush him; and gifted with vehemence, he, with great impetuosity, leaped up and sat on the breast (of the Raksa). And halding his head with two hands, he, emitting loud roars, displaced his head.

अथ विनदति सादिते निकुम्भे; पवनसुतेन रणे बभूव युद्धम्
दशरथसुतराक्षसेन्द्रचम्वो;र्भृशतरमागतरोषयोः सुभीमम्

atha vinadati sādite nikumbhe; pavanasutena raṇe babhūva yuddham
daśarathasutarākṣasendracamvo;rbhṛśataramāgataroṣayoḥ subhīmam
Nikumbha being thus slain in conflict by the Wind-god's son, there ensued a terrible conflict between the highly enraged armies of the son of Dasaratha and the lord of Raksasas.

निकुम्भं च हतं श्रुत्वा कुम्भं च विनिपातितम्
रावणः परमामर्षी प्रजज्वालानलो यथा

nikumbhaṁ ca hataṁ śrutvā kumbhaṁ ca vinipātitam
rāvaṇaḥ paramāmarṣī prajajvālānalo yathā
Beholding Kumbha and Nikumbha slain, Ravana was excited with ire like to flaming fire.

नैरृतः क्रोधशोकाभ्यां द्वाभ्यां तु परिमूर्छितः
खरपुत्रं विशालाक्षं मकराक्षमचोदयत्

nairṛtaḥ krodhaśokābhyāṁ dvābhyāṁ tu parimūrchitaḥ
kharaputraṁ viśālākṣaṁ makarākṣamacodayat

Being beside himself, simultaneously with wrath and grief Ravana* spoke to Makaraksa, Kahara's son, having spacious eyes, saying, O child, do you proceed at my command with the army and destroy Raghava and Laksmana with all the monkeys. *Nairta is another name of Ravana.

सोऽभिवाद्य दशग्रीवं कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्
निर्जगाम गृहाच्छुभ्राद्रावणस्याज्ञया बली

so'bhivādya daśagrīvaṁ kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam
nirjagāma gṛhācchubhrādrāvaṇasyājñayā balī

Hearing the words of Ravana, Khara's son, Makaraksa, proud of his own own prowess, delightedly spoke to the night-ranger, saying, “Be it so." And saluting and circumambulating the ten-necked one, that hero, at Ravana's behest, issued out of the house.

समीपस्थं बलाध्यक्षं खरपुत्रोऽब्रवीदिदम्
रथमानीयतां शीघ्रं सैन्यं चानीयतां त्वरात्

samīpasthaṁ balādhyakṣaṁ kharaputro'bravīdidam
rathamānīyatāṁ śīghraṁ sainyaṁ cānīyatāṁ tvarāt
Khara's son spoke to the commander who was near him, saying, “Do you speedily bring the chariot here and all the soldiers."

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा बलाध्यक्षो निशाचरः
स्यन्दनं च बलं चैव समीपं प्रत्यपादयत्

tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā balādhyakṣo niśācaraḥ
syandanaṁ ca balaṁ caiva samīpaṁ pratyapādayat
Hearing his words, that commanding nightranger, soon let before him the army and the chariot.

प्रदक्षिणं रथं कृत्वा आरुरोह निशाचरः
सूतं संचोदयामास शीघ्रं मे रथमावह

pradakṣiṇaṁ rathaṁ kṛtvā āruroha niśācaraḥ
sūtaṁ saṁcodayāmāsa śīghraṁ me rathamāvaha
And going round the chariot and addressing the charioteer that night-ranger (Makaraksa) said, O charioteer, do you soon drive the chariot.

अथ तान्राक्षसान्सर्वान्मकराक्षोऽब्रवीदिदम्
यूयं सर्वे प्रयुध्यध्वं पुरस्तान्मम राक्षसाः

atha tānrākṣasānsarvānmakarākṣo'bravīdidam
yūyaṁ sarve prayudhyadhvaṁ purastānmama rākṣasāḥ
Thereat Makaraksa addressed those Raksasas, saying, O Raksasas! do you all fight before me.

अहं राक्षसराजेन रावणेन महात्मना
आज्ञप्तः समरे हन्तुं तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ

ahaṁ rākṣasarājena rāvaṇena mahātmanā
ājñaptaḥ samare hantuṁ tāvubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau
I have been commanded by the high-souled Ravana, the lord of Raksasas, to slay both Rama and Laksmana in conflict.

अद्य रामं वधिष्यामि लक्ष्मणं च निशाचराः
शाखामृगं च सुग्रीवं वानरांश्च शरोत्तमैः

adya rāmaṁ vadhiṣyāmi lakṣmaṇaṁ ca niśācarāḥ
śākhāmṛgaṁ ca sugrīvaṁ vānarāṁśca śarottamaiḥ
I shall slay to-day, O night-ranger, with my excellent arrows, Rama, Laksmana, Sugriva and all other monkeys.

अद्य शूलनिपातैश्च वानराणां महाचमूम्
प्रदहिष्यामि संप्राप्तां शुष्केन्धनमिवानलः

adya śūlanipātaiśca vānarāṇāṁ mahācamūm
pradahiṣyāmi saṁprāptāṁ śuṣkendhanamivānalaḥ
Like to fire consuming dry fuel, shall I today slay the host of monkeys with my darts.

मकराक्षस्य तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं ते निशाचराः
सर्वे नानायुधोपेता बलवन्तः समाहिताः

makarākṣasya tacchrutvā vacanaṁ te niśācarāḥ
sarve nānāyudhopetā balavantaḥ samāhitāḥ
Hearing those words of Makaraksa, the mighty night-rangers, (addressed themselves for fight).

ते कामरूपिणः शूरा दंष्ट्रिणः पिङ्गलेक्षणाः
मातंगा इव नर्दन्तो ध्वस्तकेशा भयानकाः

te kāmarūpiṇaḥ śūrā daṁṣṭriṇaḥ piṅgalekṣaṇāḥ
mātaṁgā iva nardanto dhvastakeśā bhayānakāḥ

They were armed with various weapons, cautious; assuming shapes at will, crooked, having fearful teeth, coppery eyes; roaring like elephants, having dishevelled hair and terrible. And encircling the huge-bodied son of Khara, those gigantic (Raksasas) began to proceed, delighted and moving the earth (with the weight of their persons).

शङ्खभेरीसहस्राणामाहतानां समन्ततः
क्ष्वेडितास्फोटितानां च ततः शब्दो महानभूत्

śaṅkhabherīsahasrāṇāmāhatānāṁ samantataḥ
kṣveḍitāsphoṭitānāṁ ca tataḥ śabdo mahānabhūt
There arose a terrible noise on all sides from the sound of conches, and thousands of bugles, and from the moving of the arms of the heroes.

प्रभ्रष्टोऽथ करात्तस्य प्रतोदः सारथेस्तदा
पपात सहसा चैव ध्वजस्तस्य च रक्षसः

prabhraṣṭo'tha karāttasya pratodaḥ sārathestadā
papāta sahasā caiva dhvajastasya ca rakṣasaḥ
And all on a sudden the reins slipped off (the hands of) the charioteer and the flag of the Raksasas dropped down.

तस्य ते रथसंयुक्ता हया विक्रमवर्जिताः
चरणैराकुलैर्गत्वा दीनाः सास्रमुखा ययुः

tasya te rathasaṁyuktā hayā vikramavarjitāḥ
caraṇairākulairgatvā dīnāḥ sāsramukhā yayuḥ
The course of the steeds was thus slackened and they began to move slowly and poorly with their heads drooping down.

प्रवाति पवनस्तस्य सपांसुः खरदारुणः
निर्याणे तस्य रौद्रस्य मकराक्षस्य दुर्मतेः

pravāti pavanastasya sapāṁsuḥ kharadāruṇaḥ
niryāṇe tasya raudrasya makarākṣasya durmateḥ
There blew a terribly rough wind mixed with dust when the fearfully wicked-minded Makaraksa's issued out for battle.

तानि दृष्ट्वा निमित्तानि राक्षसा वीर्यवत्तमाः
अचिन्त्यनिर्गताः सर्वे यत्र तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ

tāni dṛṣṭvā nimittāni rākṣasā vīryavattamāḥ
acintyanirgatāḥ sarve yatra tau rāmalakṣmaṇau
Those powerful Raksasas neglecting those bad omens proceeded towards where Rama and Laksmana were.

घनगजमहिषाङ्गतुल्यवर्णाः; समरमुखेष्वसकृद्गदासिभिन्नाः
अहमहमिति युद्धकौशलास्ते; रजनिचराः परिबभ्रमुर्नदन्तः

ghanagajamahiṣāṅgatulyavarṇāḥ; samaramukheṣvasakṛdgadāsibhinnāḥ
ahamahamiti yuddhakauśalāste; rajanicarāḥ paribabhramurnadantaḥ

They were all black like to clouds, elephants and buffaloes, and had marks of swords and maces on their persons. And all those nightrangers were skilled in the art of warfare and began to range to and fro (in the battle field) saying, “I shall to first.”

निर्गतं मकराक्षं ते दृष्ट्वा वानरपुंगवाः
आप्लुत्य सहसा सर्वे योद्धुकामा व्यवस्थिताः

nirgataṁ makarākṣaṁ te dṛṣṭvā vānarapuṁgavāḥ
āplutya sahasā sarve yoddhukāmā vyavasthitāḥ
Beholding Makaraksa out for battle, those foremost monkeys leaping on a sudden, addressed themselves for fight.

ततः प्रवृत्तं सुमहत्तद्युद्धं लोमहर्षणम्
निशाचरैः प्लवंगानां देवानां दानवैरिव

tataḥ pravṛttaṁ sumahattadyuddhaṁ lomaharṣaṇam
niśācaraiḥ plavaṁgānāṁ devānāṁ dānavairiva
Thereupon ensued a terrible conflict, capable of making one's down stand on end, between the right-rangers and the monkeys like to one between the celestials and Danavas.

वृक्षशूलनिपातैश्च शिलापरिघपातनैः
अन्योन्यं मर्दयन्ति स्म तदा कपिनिशाचराः

vṛkṣaśūlanipātaiśca śilāparighapātanaiḥ
anyonyaṁ mardayanti sma tadā kapiniśācarāḥ
Those monkeys and night-rangers crushed each other down with trees, darts, maces and parighas.

पाशमुद्गरदण्डैश्च निर्घातैश्चापरैस्तथा
कदनं कपिसिंहानां चक्रुस्ते रजनीचराः

pāśamudgaradaṇḍaiśca nirghātaiścāparaistathā
kadanaṁ kapisiṁhānāṁ cakruste rajanīcarāḥ

Those night-rangers began to assail those foremost of monkeys with sakti.' swords, maces, kuntas, tomaras, pattisas, Bhindipalas, arrows, nooses and clubs. 1. A short arrow thrown from the hand or shot through a tube. 2. An Iron spear or dart.

बाणौघैरर्दिताश्चापि खरपुत्रेण वानराः
संभ्रान्तमनसः सर्वे दुद्रुवुर्भयपीडिताः

bāṇaughairarditāścāpi kharaputreṇa vānarāḥ
saṁbhrāntamanasaḥ sarve dudruvurbhayapīḍitāḥ
Being thus assailed with fearful arrows by Khara's son, those monkeys, stricken with fear, fled away.

तान्दृष्ट्वा राक्षसाः सर्वे द्रवमाणान्वनौकसः
नेदुस्ते सिंहवद्धृष्टा राक्षसा जितकाशिनः

tāndṛṣṭvā rākṣasāḥ sarve dravamāṇānvanaukasaḥ
neduste siṁhavaddhṛṣṭā rākṣasā jitakāśinaḥ
Beholding those monkeys fly away, all the victorious Raksasas began to roar like excited lions.

विद्रवत्सु तदा तेषु वानरेषु समन्ततः
रामस्तान्वारयामास शरवर्षेण राक्षसान्

vidravatsu tadā teṣu vānareṣu samantataḥ
rāmastānvārayāmāsa śaravarṣeṇa rākṣasān
The monkeys thus flying away to all quarters, Rama with a downpour of shafts assailed the Raksasas.

वारितान्राक्षसान्दृष्ट्वा मकराक्षो निशाचरः
क्रोधानलसमाविष्टो वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्

vāritānrākṣasāndṛṣṭvā makarākṣo niśācaraḥ
krodhānalasamāviṣṭo vacanaṁ cedamabravīt
Beholding the Raksasas thus overpowered, the night-ranger Makaraksa, excited with the flame of ire, said.

तिष्ठ राम मया सार्धं द्वन्द्वयुद्धं ददामि ते
त्याजयिष्यामि ते प्राणान्धनुर्मुक्तैः शितैः शरैः

tiṣṭha rāma mayā sārdhaṁ dvandvayuddhaṁ dadāmi te
tyājayiṣyāmi te prāṇāndhanurmuktaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
Stay, O Rama, let us both fight with each other; I shall take your life with sharp arrows discharged off my bow.

यत्तदा दण्डकारण्ये पितरं हतवान्मम
मदग्रतः स्वकर्मस्थं स्मृत्वा रोषोऽभिवर्धते

yattadā daṇḍakāraṇye pitaraṁ hatavānmama
madagrataḥ svakarmasthaṁ smṛtvā roṣo'bhivardhate
You did slay my father in the forest of Dandaka. Remembering your action and finding you before, my ire is excited.

दह्यन्ते भृशमङ्गानि दुरात्मन्मम राघव
यन्मयासि न दृष्टस्त्वं तस्मिन्काले महावने

dahyante bhṛśamaṅgāni durātmanmama rāghava
yanmayāsi na dṛṣṭastvaṁ tasminkāle mahāvane
O Raghava! O Vicious souled one! My limbs are being burnt (with wrath) for I did not see you then in that mighty forest.

दिष्ट्यासि दर्शनं राम मम त्वं प्राप्तवानिह
काङ्क्षितोऽसि क्षुधार्तस्य सिंहस्येवेतरो मृगः

diṣṭyāsi darśanaṁ rāma mama tvaṁ prāptavāniha
kāṅkṣito'si kṣudhārtasya siṁhasyevetaro mṛgaḥ
O Rama, by my good luck, I have got you today, like to a hungry lion desiring to have other animals.

अद्य मद्बाणवेगेन प्रेतराड्विषयं गतः
ये त्वया निहताः शूराः सह तैस्त्वं समेष्यसि

adya madbāṇavegena pretarāḍviṣayaṁ gataḥ
ye tvayā nihatāḥ śūrāḥ saha taistvaṁ sameṣyasi
Being despatched by my arrows to the world of devils, you shall live with those heroes, who had been killed by you before.

बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन शृणु राम वचो मम
पश्यन्तु सकला लोकास्त्वां मां चैव रणाजिरे

bahunātra kimuktena śṛṇu rāma vaco mama
paśyantu sakalā lokāstvāṁ māṁ caiva raṇājire
What is the use of speaking more, O Rama, do you hear my words. Let all the people behold your as well as my prowess in the battle-field.

अस्त्रैर्वा गदया वापि बाहुभ्यां वा महाहवे
अभ्यस्तं येन वा राम तेन वा वर्ततां युधि

astrairvā gadayā vāpi bāhubhyāṁ vā mahāhave
abhyastaṁ yena vā rāma tena vā vartatāṁ yudhi
Either with weapon or with clubs, in whatever you are expert, do you fight.with me in the battle-field, O Rama.

मकराक्षवचः श्रुत्वा रामो दशरथात्मजः
अब्रवीत्प्रहसन्वाक्यमुत्तरोत्तरवादिनम्

makarākṣavacaḥ śrutvā rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
abravītprahasanvākyamuttarottaravādinam
Hearing the words of Makaraksa, Rama, Dasaratha's son, smiling, replied to the words of the babbler.

स्वाशितास्तव मांसेन गृध्रगोमायुवायसाः
भविष्यन्त्यद्य वै पाप तीक्ष्णतुण्डनखाङ्कुशाः

svāśitāstava māṁsena gṛdhragomāyuvāyasāḥ
bhaviṣyantyadya vai pāpa tīkṣṇatuṇḍanakhāṅkuśāḥ

I slew in the forest of Dandaka your father with fourteen thousand Raksasas, Trisira and Dusana. O vile one, you being slain to day, with your flesh, vultures and crows, having sharp beaks and nails, and jackals shall be satisfied.* [*Here is another sloka, which is to be found in all N.W.P. texts and in one or two texts published in Bengal-but it has been omitted by many for it conveys the same meaning as the previous sloka; the meaning is-And the birds drinking your blood shall fly away to various quarters.]

एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण खरपुत्रो निशाचरः
बाणौघानसृजत्तस्मै राघवाय रणाजिरे

evamuktastu rāmeṇa kharaputro niśācaraḥ
bāṇaughānasṛjattasmai rāghavāya raṇājire
Being thus addressed by Raghava, the mighty Makaraksa, began to dart sharp arrows towards him in the battle-field.

ताञ्शराञ्शरवर्षेण रामश्चिच्छेद नैकधा
निपेतुर्भुवि ते छिन्ना रुक्मपुङ्खाः सहस्रशः

tāñśarāñśaravarṣeṇa rāmaściccheda naikadhā
nipeturbhuvi te chinnā rukmapuṅkhāḥ sahasraśaḥ
And Rama, with his shafts, sundered into several pieces, those arrows. And being thus rendered useless those arrows, feathered in gold, fell down on the earth.

तद्युद्धमभवत्तत्र समेत्यान्योन्यमोजसा
खर राक्षसपुत्रस्य सूनोर्दशरथस्य च

tadyuddhamabhavattatra sametyānyonyamojasā
khara rākṣasaputrasya sūnordaśarathasya ca
Then there arose a terrible conflict between the Raksasa Khara's son and Dasaratha's son.

जीमूतयोरिवाकाशे शब्दो ज्यातलयोस्तदा
धनुर्मुक्तः स्वनोत्कृष्टः श्रूयते च रणाजिरे

jīmūtayorivākāśe śabdo jyātalayostadā
dhanurmuktaḥ svanotkṛṣṭaḥ śrūyate ca raṇājire
There were audible in that battle-field, the outcry of the heroes and the twang of the bows stretched by their hands, like to the muttering of the clouds in the sky.

देवदानवगन्धर्वाः किंनराश्च महोरगाः
अन्तरिक्षगताः सर्वे द्रष्टुकामास्तदद्भुतम्

devadānavagandharvāḥ kiṁnarāśca mahoragāḥ
antarikṣagatāḥ sarve draṣṭukāmāstadadbhutam
To see that wondrous conflict, the celestials, Danavas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras and the mighty serpents stationed themselves in the sky.

राममुक्तास्तु बाणौघान्राक्षसस्त्वच्छिनद्रणे
रक्षोमुक्तांस्तु रामो वै नैकधा प्राच्छिनच्छरैः

rāmamuktāstu bāṇaughānrākṣasastvacchinadraṇe
rakṣomuktāṁstu rāmo vai naikadhā prācchinaccharaiḥ

They were wounded with the discharged by each other and their strength was doubled. And they began to fight in that battlefield one attacking and the other withstanding the attack. And in that conflict the Raksasa artOWS sundered the shafts discharged by Rama. And likewise Rama severed into several pieces the arrows shot by the Raksasa.

बाणौघवितताः सर्वा दिशश्च विदिशस्तथा
संछन्ना वसुधा चैव समन्तान्न प्रकाशते

bāṇaughavitatāḥ sarvā diśaśca vidiśastathā
saṁchannā vasudhā caiva samantānna prakāśate
All the quarters were covered with arrows and nothing on earth or in the sky was visible.

ततः क्रुद्धो महाबाहुर्धनुश्चिच्छेद रक्षसः
अष्टाभिरथ नाराचैः सूतं विव्याध राघवः
भित्त्वा शरै रथं रामो रथाश्वान्समपातयत्

tataḥ kruddho mahābāhurdhanuściccheda rakṣasaḥ
aṣṭābhiratha nārācaiḥ sūtaṁ vivyādha rāghavaḥ
bhittvā śarai rathaṁ rāmo rathāśvānsamapātayat
Thereupon being excited with ire, Raghava of long arms sundered his (Raksasa's) bow in conflict and with eight Naracas pierced the charioteer.

विरथो वसुधां तिष्ठन्मकराक्षो निशाचरः
अतिष्ठद्वसुधां रक्षः शूलं जग्राह पाणिना
त्रासनं सर्वभूतानां युगान्ताग्निसमप्रभम्

viratho vasudhāṁ tiṣṭhanmakarākṣo niśācaraḥ
atiṣṭhadvasudhāṁ rakṣaḥ śūlaṁ jagrāha pāṇinā
trāsanaṁ sarvabhūtānāṁ yugāntāgnisamaprabham

He then again rose up with a dart in his hand creating terror to all creatures and resembling the Fire of Dissolution in resplendence. It was a terribly huge dart conferred on him by Siva, shining in the sky in its native brilliance and like to another weapon of destruction.* *This refers to the weapon used by Siva for destruction-for Siva, according to the Hindu Mythology is the God of destruction.

विभ्राम्य च महच्छूलं प्रज्वलन्तं निशाचरः
स क्रोधात्प्राहिणोत्तस्मै राघवाय महाहवे

vibhrāmya ca mahacchūlaṁ prajvalantaṁ niśācaraḥ
sa krodhātprāhiṇottasmai rāghavāya mahāhave
Beholding which dart even the celestials fly away in fear to different quarters. And taking up that huge flaming dart, the night-ranger, being excited with ire, hurled it at the high-souled Raghava.

तमापतन्तं ज्वलितं खरपुत्रकराच्च्युतम्
बाणैस्तु त्रिभिराकाशे शूलं चिच्छेद राघवः

tamāpatantaṁ jvalitaṁ kharaputrakarāccyutam
bāṇaistu tribhirākāśe śūlaṁ ciccheda rāghavaḥ
Raghava, with four shafts, sundered that dart, in the sky, flaming and hurled at him by the son of Khara.

सच्छिन्नो नैकधा शूलो दिव्यहाटकमण्डितः
व्यशीर्यत महोक्लेव रामबाणार्दितो भुवि

sacchinno naikadhā śūlo divyahāṭakamaṇḍitaḥ
vyaśīryata mahokleva rāmabāṇārdito bhuvi
That flaming dart, feathered in gold, being splintered into several pieces by Rama's arrows fell down on earth like a huge fire-brand.

तच्छूलं निहतं दृष्ट्वा रामेणाद्भुतकर्मणा
साधु साध्विति भूतानि व्याहरन्ति नभोगताः

tacchūlaṁ nihataṁ dṛṣṭvā rāmeṇādbhutakarmaṇā
sādhu sādhviti bhūtāni vyāharanti nabhogatāḥ
Beholding that dart beffled thus by Rama of unwearied actions all those, stationed in the welkin began to shout, “Well done! Well done!"

तद्दृष्ट्वा निहतं शूलं मकराक्षो निशाचरः
मुष्टिमुद्यम्य काकुत्स्थं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्

taddṛṣṭvā nihataṁ śūlaṁ makarākṣo niśācaraḥ
muṣṭimudyamya kākutsthaṁ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
Beholding his dart thus sundered, the nightranger Makaraksa clenching his fist spoke to Kakutstha, saying, "Stay! Stay!"

स तं दृष्ट्वा पतन्तं वै प्रहस्य रघुनन्दनः
पावकास्त्रं ततो रामः संदधे स्वशरासने

sa taṁ dṛṣṭvā patantaṁ vai prahasya raghunandanaḥ
pāvakāstraṁ tato rāmaḥ saṁdadhe svaśarāsane
Seeing him advance thus, the descendant of Raghu, smiling, fixed a fiery arrow on his bow.

तेनास्त्रेण हतं रक्षः काकुत्स्थेन तदा रणे
संछिन्नहृदयं तत्र पपात च ममार च

tenāstreṇa hataṁ rakṣaḥ kākutsthena tadā raṇe
saṁchinnahṛdayaṁ tatra papāta ca mamāra ca
With that arrow the Raksa was slain by Kakutstha in battle. And having his heart pierced he fell down and died.

दृष्ट्वा ते राक्षसाः सर्वे मकराक्षस्य पातनम्
लङ्कामेव प्रधावन्त रामबालार्दितास्तदा

dṛṣṭvā te rākṣasāḥ sarve makarākṣasya pātanam
laṅkāmeva pradhāvanta rāmabālārditāstadā
Beholding Makaraksa thus slain all the Raks asas, being afraid of Rama's arrows, proceeded towards Lanka.

दशरथनृपपुत्रबाणवेगै; रजनिचरं निहतं खरात्मजं तम्
ददृशुरथ च देवताः प्रहृष्टा; गिरिमिव वज्रहतं यथा विशीर्णम्

daśarathanṛpaputrabāṇavegai; rajanicaraṁ nihataṁ kharātmajaṁ tam
dadṛśuratha ca devatāḥ prahṛṣṭā; girimiva vajrahataṁ yathā viśīrṇam
Seeing that night-ranger, the son of Khara, slain by Rama's arrows, like to a mountain clept by a thunder-bolt, the celestials were greatly delighted.

मकराक्षं हतं श्रुत्वा रावणः समितिंजयः
आदिदेशाथ संक्रुद्धो रणायेन्द्रजितं सुतम्

makarākṣaṁ hataṁ śrutvā rāvaṇaḥ samitiṁjayaḥ
ādideśātha saṁkruddho raṇāyendrajitaṁ sutam
Being thus angered, and thinking within himself what steps to take, he ordered his son Indrajit to proceed to the battle-field.

जहि वीर महावीर्यौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
अदृश्यो दृश्यमानो वा सर्वथा त्वं बलाधिकः

jahi vīra mahāvīryau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
adṛśyo dṛśyamāno vā sarvathā tvaṁ balādhikaḥ
O hero, gifted with great prowess as you are, do you, hidden (in clouds) or appearing before them, slay the two heroic brothers Rama and Laksmana.

त्वमप्रतिमकर्माणमिन्द्रं जयसि संयुगे
किं पुनर्मानुषौ दृष्ट्वा न वधिष्यसि संयुगे

tvamapratimakarmāṇamindraṁ jayasi saṁyuge
kiṁ punarmānuṣau dṛṣṭvā na vadhiṣyasi saṁyuge
You did defeat in conflict Indra of unequalled prowess. Shall you then neglect to slay men as they are?

तथोक्तो राक्षसेन्द्रेण प्रतिगृह्य पितुर्वचः
यज्ञभूमौ स विधिवत्पावकं जुहुवे न्द्रजित्

tathokto rākṣasendreṇa pratigṛhya piturvacaḥ
yajñabhūmau sa vidhivatpāvakaṁ juhuve ndrajit
Being thus addressed by the lord of the Raks asas and obeying his father's command, Indrajit proceeded towards the sacrificial ground to satisfy Fire (with oblations).

जुह्वतश्चापि तत्राग्निं रक्तोष्णीषधराः स्त्रियः
आजग्मुस्तत्र संभ्रान्ता राक्षस्यो यत्र रावणिः

juhvataścāpi tatrāgniṁ raktoṣṇīṣadharāḥ striyaḥ
ājagmustatra saṁbhrāntā rākṣasyo yatra rāvaṇiḥ
There came some she-demons with crimson turbans and waited respectfully where Ravana's son was offering oblations to Fire.

शस्त्राणि शरपत्राणि समिधोऽथ विभीतकाः
लोहितानि च वासांसि स्रुवं कार्ष्णायसं तथा

śastrāṇi śarapatrāṇi samidho'tha vibhītakāḥ
lohitāni ca vāsāṁsi sruvaṁ kārṣṇāyasaṁ tathā
Arms served for Kasa and Bibhitakas for fuel; and there were red cloths and a ladle made black iron.

सर्वतोऽग्निं समास्तीर्य शरपत्रैः समन्ततः
छागस्य सर्वकृष्णस्य गलं जग्राह जीवतः

sarvato'gniṁ samāstīrya śarapatraiḥ samantataḥ
chāgasya sarvakṛṣṇasya galaṁ jagrāha jīvataḥ
Spreading fire on all sides with sare leaves and Tomaras, (Indrajit) caught a living goat, all black, by the neck.

चरुहोमसमिद्धस्य विधूमस्य महार्चिषः
बभूवुस्तानि लिङ्गानि विजयं दर्शयन्ति च

caruhomasamiddhasya vidhūmasya mahārciṣaḥ
babhūvustāni liṅgāni vijayaṁ darśayanti ca
The fire, with oblations of sara, became greatly blazed and devoid of smoke. There were visible many good omens indicating victory.

प्रदक्षिणावर्तशिखस्तप्तहाटकसंनिभः
हविस्तत्प्रतिजग्राह पावकः स्वयमुत्थितः

pradakṣiṇāvartaśikhastaptahāṭakasaṁnibhaḥ
havistatpratijagrāha pāvakaḥ svayamutthitaḥ
The flame of the fire was like to gold, and moving Southwards began to receive offerings of clarified butter.

हुत्वाग्निं तर्पयित्वाथ देवदानवराक्षसान्
आरुरोह रथश्रेष्ठमन्तर्धानगतं शुभम्

hutvāgniṁ tarpayitvātha devadānavarākṣasān
āruroha rathaśreṣṭhamantardhānagataṁ śubham
Thus offering oblations to fire and to celestials, Danavas and Raksasas, he ascended in excellent car and soon disappeared.

स वाजिभिश्चतुर्भिस्तु बाणैश्च निशितैर्युतः
आरोपितमहाचापः शुशुभे स्यन्दनोत्तमे

sa vājibhiścaturbhistu bāṇaiśca niśitairyutaḥ
āropitamahācāpaḥ śuśubhe syandanottame
It was drawn by four horses and a huge bow, set with sharp arrows, appeared beautiful on that excellent car.

जाज्वल्यमानो वपुषा तपनीयपरिच्छदः
शरैश्चन्द्रार्धचन्द्रैश्च स रथः समलंकृतः

jājvalyamāno vapuṣā tapanīyaparicchadaḥ
śaraiścandrārdhacandraiśca sa rathaḥ samalaṁkṛtaḥ
The chariot was brilliant with its own native resplendence, adorned with gold and painted with the figures of deer and a cresent.

जाम्बूनदमहाकम्बुर्दीप्तपावकसंनिभः
बभूवेन्द्रजितः केतुर्वैदूर्यसमलंकृतः

jāmbūnadamahākamburdīptapāvakasaṁnibhaḥ
babhūvendrajitaḥ keturvaidūryasamalaṁkṛtaḥ
It was encircled on all sides with golden bracelets, adorned with flags made of viadurja and was like to the flaming fire.

तेन चादित्यकल्पेन ब्रह्मास्त्रेण च पालितः
स बभूव दुराधर्षो रावणिः सुमहाबलः

tena cādityakalpena brahmāstreṇa ca pālitaḥ
sa babhūva durādharṣo rāvaṇiḥ sumahābalaḥ
Being thus well protected with Brahma weapons resembling the Sun in brilliance, the mighty son of Ravana became invincible.

सोऽभिनिर्याय नगरादिन्द्रजित्समितिंजयः
हुत्वाग्निं राक्षसैर्मन्त्रैरन्तर्धानगतोऽब्रवीत्

so'bhiniryāya nagarādindrajitsamitiṁjayaḥ
hutvāgniṁ rākṣasairmantrairantardhānagato'bravīt
Offering oblations to Fire in accordance with demoniac incantations and thus obtaining the power of hiding himself, that hero, ever victorious in battle, issued out of the city and said.

अद्य हत्वाहवे यौ तौ मिथ्या प्रव्रजितौ वने
जयं पित्रे प्रदास्यामि रावणाय रणाधिकम्

adya hatvāhave yau tau mithyā pravrajitau vane
jayaṁ pitre pradāsyāmi rāvaṇāya raṇādhikam
Slaying these two brothers in battle, who have uselessly wandered away into the forest, shall I crown my father Ravana with victory.

कृत्वा निर्वानरामुर्वीं हत्वा रामं सलक्ष्मणम्
करिष्ये परमां प्रीतिमित्युक्त्वान्तरधीयत

kṛtvā nirvānarāmurvīṁ hatvā rāmaṁ salakṣmaṇam
kariṣye paramāṁ prītimityuktvāntaradhīyata
Destroying Rama and Laksmana, and clearing the monkeys off the earth, shall I satisfy my sire greatly. Saying this, he disappeared from their view.

आपपाताथ संक्रुद्धो दशग्रीवेण चोदितः
तीक्ष्णकार्मुकनाराचैस्तीक्ष्णस्त्विन्द्ररिपू रणे

āpapātātha saṁkruddho daśagrīveṇa coditaḥ
tīkṣṇakārmukanārācaistīkṣṇastvindraripū raṇe
Thereupon that fearful foe of the lord of celestials appeared in the battle-field, excited with wrath, armed with bow and sharp Naracas and commissioned thus by the Ten-necked one.

स ददर्श महावीर्यौ नागौ त्रिशिरसाविव
सृजन्ताविषुजालानि वीरौ वानरमध्यगौ

sa dadarśa mahāvīryau nāgau triśirasāviva
sṛjantāviṣujālāni vīrau vānaramadhyagau
He beheld there those two heroes discharging flaming arrows and surrounded by the monkeys like to the fearful three-hooded serpent in the midst of other serpents.

इमौ ताविति संचिन्त्य सज्यं कृत्वा च कार्मुकम्
संततानेषुधाराभिः पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्

imau tāviti saṁcintya sajyaṁ kṛtvā ca kārmukam
saṁtatāneṣudhārābhiḥ parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān
Thinking "these must be both brothers, Rama and Laksmana," and stretching his bow he began showering arrows like to clouds.

स तु वैहायसं प्राप्य सरथो रामलक्ष्मणौ
अचक्षुर्विषये तिष्ठन्विव्याध निशितैः शरैः

sa tu vaihāyasaṁ prāpya saratho rāmalakṣmaṇau
acakṣurviṣaye tiṣṭhanvivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
He was seated in a car in the welkin and hidden from the human gaze and began to assail! Rama and Laksmana with sharp shafts.

तौ तस्य शरवेगेन परीतौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
धनुषी सशरे कृत्वा दिव्यमस्त्रं प्रचक्रतुः

tau tasya śaravegena parītau rāmalakṣmaṇau
dhanuṣī saśare kṛtvā divyamastraṁ pracakratuḥ
Being hurt with the arrows, Rama and Laks mana, fixing arrows on their bows, began to discharge celestial shafts.

प्रच्छादयन्तौ गगनं शरजालैर्महाबलौ
तमस्त्रैः सुरसंकाशौ नैव पस्पर्शतुः शरैः

pracchādayantau gaganaṁ śarajālairmahābalau
tamastraiḥ surasaṁkāśau naiva pasparśatuḥ śaraiḥ
Those two highly powerful heroes could not even touch his person with their arrows resembling the Sun albeit they covered the whole welkin therewith.

स हि धूमान्धकारं च चक्रे प्रच्छादयन्नभः
दिशश्चान्तर्दधे श्रीमान्नीहारतमसावृतः

sa hi dhūmāndhakāraṁ ca cakre pracchādayannabhaḥ
diśaścāntardadhe śrīmānnīhāratamasāvṛtaḥ
And clouding the whole sky with smoke that effulgent one, enveloped in frost, his himself from their gaze.

नैव ज्यातलनिर्घोषो न च नेमिखुरस्वनः
शुश्रुवे चरतस्तस्य न च रूपं प्रकाशते

naiva jyātalanirghoṣo na ca nemikhurasvanaḥ
śuśruve caratastasya na ca rūpaṁ prakāśate
There was not audible the twang of kis bow, the sound of the wheels, or the noise of the steeds. Nor was he seen by any.

घनान्धकारे तिमिरे शरवर्षमिवाद्भुतम्
स ववर्ष महाबाहुर्नाराचशरवृष्टिभिः

ghanāndhakāre timire śaravarṣamivādbhutam
sa vavarṣa mahābāhurnārācaśaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
In that terrible darkness of clouds that one of mighty arms began to make a downpour of Naracas and arrows like hail storms.

स रामं सूर्यसंकाशैः शरैर्दत्तवरो भृशम्
विव्याध समरे क्रुद्धः सर्वगात्रेषु रावणिः

sa rāmaṁ sūryasaṁkāśaiḥ śarairdattavaro bhṛśam
vivyādha samare kruddhaḥ sarvagātreṣu rāvaṇiḥ
In that encounter, Ravana's son, inflamed with ire, wounded Rama, with shafts, resembling the Sun and obtained by him as a boon.

तौ हन्यमानौ नाराचैर्धाराभिरिव पर्वतौ
हेमपुङ्खान्नरव्याघ्रौ तिग्मान्मुमुचतुः शरान्

tau hanyamānau nārācairdhārābhiriva parvatau
hemapuṅkhānnaravyāghrau tigmānmumucatuḥ śarān
Being hurt with Narachas, like to mountains wet with rain, those two foremost of men, began to discharge shafts feathered in gold.

अन्तरिक्षं समासाद्य रावणिं कङ्कपत्रिणः
निकृत्य पतगा भूमौ पेतुस्ते शोणितोक्षिताः

antarikṣaṁ samāsādya rāvaṇiṁ kaṅkapatriṇaḥ
nikṛtya patagā bhūmau petuste śoṇitokṣitāḥ
Reaching the son of Ravana in the sky and soaked in blood those golden arrows, fell down on earth.

अतिमात्रं शरौघेण पीड्यमानौ नरोत्तमौ
तानिषून्पततो भल्लैरनेकैर्निचकर्ततुः

atimātraṁ śaraugheṇa pīḍyamānau narottamau
tāniṣūnpatato bhallairanekairnicakartatuḥ
Those two best of men, hurt with his arrows, became more effulgent and beffled the shafts discharged by the Raksasa.

यतो हि ददृशाते तौ शरान्निपतिताञ्शितान्
ततस्ततो दाशरथी ससृजातेऽस्त्रमुत्तमम्

yato hi dadṛśāte tau śarānnipatitāñśitān
tatastato dāśarathī sasṛjāte'stramuttamam
Thereupon Rama and Laksmana began to aim their sharp shafts to the direction whence the arrows came down.

रावणिस्तु दिशः सर्वा रथेनातिरथः पतन्
विव्याध तौ दाशरथी लघ्वस्त्रो निशितैः शरैः

rāvaṇistu diśaḥ sarvā rathenātirathaḥ patan
vivyādha tau dāśarathī laghvastro niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
And stationed in his chariot that mighty carwarrior disturbed all quarters with his arrows and pierced Dasaratha's sons with sharp shafts won by him.

तेनातिविद्धौ तौ वीरौ रुक्मपुङ्खैः सुसंहतैः
बभूवतुर्दाशरथी पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ

tenātividdhau tau vīrau rukmapuṅkhaiḥ susaṁhataiḥ
babhūvaturdāśarathī puṣpitāviva kiṁśukau
Being greatly hurt with those sharp-pointed and terrible arrows Rama and Laksmana appeared like blossoming kingsukas.

नास्य वेद गतिं कश्चिन्न च रूपं धनुः शरान्
न चान्यद्विदितं किंचित्सूर्यस्येवाभ्रसंप्लवे

nāsya veda gatiṁ kaścinna ca rūpaṁ dhanuḥ śarān
na cānyadviditaṁ kiṁcitsūryasyevābhrasaṁplave
Like to the sun hidden in clouds they could see neither his countenance and motion, nor his bow and arrows.

तेन विद्धाश्च हरयो निहताश्च गतासवः
बभूवुः शतशस्तत्र पतिता धरणीतले

tena viddhāśca harayo nihatāśca gatāsavaḥ
babhūvuḥ śataśastatra patitā dharaṇītale
Being wounded with those arrows hundreds of monkeys died and fell down on the earth.

लक्ष्मणस्तु सुसंक्रुद्धो भ्रातरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
ब्राह्ममस्त्रं प्रयोक्ष्यामि वधार्थं सर्वरक्षसाम्

lakṣmaṇastu susaṁkruddho bhrātaraṁ vākyamabravīt
brāhmamastraṁ prayokṣyāmi vadhārthaṁ sarvarakṣasām
Thereupon Laksmana, being excited with wrath, spoke to his brother, saying-"To slay all the Raksasas shall I discharge today Brahma weapon.'

तमुवाच ततो रामो लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्
नैकस्य हेतो रक्षांसि पृथिव्यां हन्तुमर्हसि

tamuvāca tato rāmo lakṣmaṇaṁ śubhalakṣaṇam
naikasya heto rakṣāṁsi pṛthivyāṁ hantumarhasi
Thereupon Rama spoke to Laksmana, gifted with auspicious. marks, saying.-"It does not behove you to clear all the Raksasas off the earth for the folly of one individual.

अस्यैव तु वधे यत्नं करिष्यावो महाबल
आदेक्ष्यावो महावेगानस्त्रानाशीविषोपमान्

asyaiva tu vadhe yatnaṁ kariṣyāvo mahābala
ādekṣyāvo mahāvegānastrānāśīviṣopamān

You should not slay him, who has retired from battle, has hidden himself, has sought your shelter, has stood before you with joined palms, has fled away or who is bewildered. O you of mighty-arms, let us try to slay him (Indrajit). And to accomplish it I shall use the weapons gifted with great impetuosity and resembling the serpents.

तमेनं मायिनं क्षुद्रमन्तर्हितरथं बलात्
राक्षसं निहनिष्यन्ति दृष्ट्वा वानरयूथपाः

tamenaṁ māyinaṁ kṣudramantarhitarathaṁ balāt
rākṣasaṁ nihaniṣyanti dṛṣṭvā vānarayūthapāḥ
He is hidden from the public gaze so we must slay him, had he been fighting openly the leaders of the monkey hosts could have slain that Raks asas.

यद्येष भूमिं विशते दिवं वा; रसातलं वापि नभस्तलं वा
एवं निगूढोऽपि ममास्त्रदग्धः; पतिष्यते भूमितले गतासुः

yadyeṣa bhūmiṁ viśate divaṁ vā; rasātalaṁ vāpi nabhastalaṁ vā
evaṁ nigūḍho'pi mamāstradagdhaḥ; patiṣyate bhūmitale gatāsuḥ
Truly he shall be burnt to death with my shafts and fall down on the earth albeit he entered the regions under the earth of the abode of the celestials.

इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महात्मा; रघुप्रवीरः प्लवगर्षभैर्वृतः
वधाय रौद्रस्य नृशंसकर्मण;स्तदा महात्मा त्वरितं निरीक्षते

ityevamuktvā vacanaṁ mahātmā; raghupravīraḥ plavagarṣabhairvṛtaḥ
vadhāya raudrasya nṛśaṁsakarmaṇa;stadā mahātmā tvaritaṁ nirīkṣate

Having said these words pregnant with a high significance, the high-souled and heroic descendant of Raghu, being surrounded by monkeys, began to concert various plans for the destruction of that terrible Raksasa of wicked deeds.

विज्ञाय तु मनस्तस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः
संनिवृत्याहवात्तस्मात्प्रविवेश पुरं ततः

vijñāya tu manastasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
saṁnivṛtyāhavāttasmātpraviveśa puraṁ tataḥ
Having read the intention of that high-souled Raghava, he retired from the battle-field and entered into the city of Lanka.

सोऽनुस्मृत्य वधं तेषां राक्षसानां तरस्विनाम्
क्रोधताम्रेक्षणः शूरो निर्जगाम महाद्युतिः

so'nusmṛtya vadhaṁ teṣāṁ rākṣasānāṁ tarasvinām
krodhatāmrekṣaṇaḥ śūro nirjagāma mahādyutiḥ
And remembering the destruction of many a। quick-paced Raksasa, his eyes were rendered coppery with ire; and that hero, the son of Ravana, issued out of the city again.

स पश्चिमेन द्वारेण निर्ययौ राक्षसैर्वृतः
इन्द्रजित्तु महावीर्यः पौलस्त्यो देवकण्टकः

sa paścimena dvāreṇa niryayau rākṣasairvṛtaḥ
indrajittu mahāvīryaḥ paulastyo devakaṇṭakaḥ
That highly powerful, Indrajit, a descendant of Pulasta and an enemy of the celestials, issued out, encircled by the Raksasas, by the western gate.

इन्द्रजित्तु ततो दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
रणायाभ्युद्यतौ वीरौ मायां प्रादुष्करोत्तदा

indrajittu tato dṛṣṭvā bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
raṇāyābhyudyatau vīrau māyāṁ prāduṣkarottadā
Then beholding the heroic brothers Rama and Laksmana prepared for fight, Indrajit spread illusions.

इन्द्रजित्तु रथे स्थाप्य सीतां मायामयीं तदा
बलेन महतावृत्य तस्या वधमरोचयत्

indrajittu rathe sthāpya sītāṁ māyāmayīṁ tadā
balena mahatāvṛtya tasyā vadhamarocayat
Placing an illusory figure of Sita on the car, encircled by a huge army he began to make arrangements for her destruction.

मोहनार्थं तु सर्वेषां बुद्धिं कृत्वा सुदुर्मतिः
हन्तुं सीतां व्यवसितो वानराभिमुखो ययौ

mohanārthaṁ tu sarveṣāṁ buddhiṁ kṛtvā sudurmatiḥ
hantuṁ sītāṁ vyavasito vānarābhimukho yayau
Desiring to charm all with his illusions, that one of wicked intent, preparing himself to slay Sita, proceeded towards the monkeys.

तं दृष्ट्वा त्वभिनिर्यान्तं नगर्याः काननौकसः
उत्पेतुरभिसंक्रुद्धाः शिलाहस्ता युयुत्सवः

taṁ dṛṣṭvā tvabhiniryāntaṁ nagaryāḥ kānanaukasaḥ
utpeturabhisaṁkruddhāḥ śilāhastā yuyutsavaḥ
Beholding him thus proceed, the monkeys, inflamed with ire, desirous of fighting and with crags in their hands, moved on.

हनूमान्पुरतस्तेषां जगाम कपिकुञ्जरः
प्रगृह्य सुमहच्छृङ्गं पर्वतस्य दुरासदम्

hanūmānpuratasteṣāṁ jagāma kapikuñjaraḥ
pragṛhya sumahacchṛṅgaṁ parvatasya durāsadam
And preceded them all, Hanuman, the foremost of the monkeys, with a huge mountaintop in his hand.

स ददर्श हतानन्दां सीतामिन्द्रजितो रथे
एकवेणीधरां दीनामुपवासकृशाननाम्

sa dadarśa hatānandāṁ sītāmindrajito rathe
ekaveṇīdharāṁ dīnāmupavāsakṛśānanām
He beheld there, on Indrajit's car, Sita, deprived of all joy, poorly, greatly reduced with fasts and wearing a single braid.

परिक्लिष्टैकवसनाममृजां राघवप्रियाम्
रजोमलाभ्यामालिप्तैः सर्वगात्रैर्वरस्त्रियम्

parikliṣṭaikavasanāmamṛjāṁ rāghavapriyām
rajomalābhyāmāliptaiḥ sarvagātrairvarastriyam
Raghava's beloved spouse wore a piece of soiled cloth, and though highly beautiful, the grace of her person was greatly spoiled with dirt.

तां निरीक्ष्य मुहूर्तं तु मैथिलीमध्यवस्य च
बाष्पपर्याकुलमुखो हनूमान्व्यथितोऽभवत्

tāṁ nirīkṣya muhūrtaṁ tu maithilīmadhyavasya ca
bāṣpaparyākulamukho hanūmānvyathito'bhavat
That daughter of Janaka, was not seen by him for a long time. And beholding her and deciding instantly that she is the daughter of Mithila, (he became greatly sorry).

किं समर्थितमस्येति चिन्तयन्स महाकपिः
सह तैर्वानरश्रेष्ठैरभ्यधावत रावणिम्

kiṁ samarthitamasyeti cintayansa mahākapiḥ
saha tairvānaraśreṣṭhairabhyadhāvata rāvaṇim

Seeing her on the car, innocent, poor, deprived of joy and brought under the influence of the son of the lord Raksasas that great monkey thought within himself— 'What must be the intention of Indrajit?' and accompanied by heroic monkeys advanced towards the son of Ravana.

तद्वानरबलं दृष्ट्वा रावणिः क्रोधमूर्छितः
कृत्वा विशोकं निस्त्रिंशं मूर्ध्नि सीतां परामृशत्

tadvānarabalaṁ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
kṛtvā viśokaṁ nistriṁśaṁ mūrdhni sītāṁ parāmṛśat
Beholding that monkey host, Ravana's son became beside himself with ire and unsheathing his weapon Nistrinsha, caught her by the hair.

तं स्त्रियं पश्यतां तेषां ताडयामास रावणिः
क्रोशन्तीं राम रामेति मायया योजितां रथे

taṁ striyaṁ paśyatāṁ teṣāṁ tāḍayāmāsa rāvaṇiḥ
krośantīṁ rāma rāmeti māyayā yojitāṁ rathe
The Raksasa addressed himself to strike her in the presence of all those monkeys and that illusory figure of Sita began to bewail saying, “O Rama! O Rama!”

गृहीतमूर्धजां दृष्ट्वा हनूमान्दैन्यमागतः
दुःखजं वारिनेत्राभ्यामुत्सृजन्मारुतात्मजः
अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं क्रोधाद्रक्षोऽधिपात्मजम्

gṛhītamūrdhajāṁ dṛṣṭvā hanūmāndainyamāgataḥ
duḥkhajaṁ vārinetrābhyāmutsṛjanmārutātmajaḥ
abravītparuṣaṁ vākyaṁ krodhādrakṣo'dhipātmajam
Seeing her thus caught by the head, Hanuman, the son of Maruta, greatly sorry, began to shed tears.

दुरात्मन्नात्मनाशाय केशपक्षे परामृशः
ब्रह्मर्षीणां कुले जातो राक्षसीं योनिमाश्रितः
धिक्त्वां पापसमाचारं यस्य ते मतिरीदृशी

durātmannātmanāśāya keśapakṣe parāmṛśaḥ
brahmarṣīṇāṁ kule jāto rākṣasīṁ yonimāśritaḥ
dhiktvāṁ pāpasamācāraṁ yasya te matirīdṛśī
It is for your destruction, O Vicious-souled one! that you have touched her hair. Being descended from that great Brahma ascetic you are born as a Raksasa.

नृशंसानार्य दुर्वृत्त क्षुद्र पापपराक्रम
अनार्यस्येदृशं कर्म घृणा ते नास्ति निर्घृण

nṛśaṁsānārya durvṛtta kṣudra pāpaparākrama
anāryasyedṛśaṁ karma ghṛṇā te nāsti nirghṛṇa
O! cursed are you, since you have cherished such a desire and engaged in such a vicious deed. O vile! O wicked! O! cruel and dishonourable wight! O you having vice for your prowess!

च्युता गृहाच्च राज्याच्च रामहस्ताच्च मैथिली
किं तवैषापराद्धा हि यदेनां हन्तुमिच्छसि

cyutā gṛhācca rājyācca rāmahastācca maithilī
kiṁ tavaiṣāparāddhā hi yadenāṁ hantumicchasi

O shameless! Are you not ashamed of perpetrating such an inhuman deed. What has Maithili done by you, O cruel one! that you are ready to slay her—She has been banished from her home, territory and has been separated from her lord.

सीतां च हत्वा न चिरं जीविष्यसि कथंचन
वधार्हकर्मणानेन मम हस्तगतो ह्यसि

sītāṁ ca hatvā na ciraṁ jīviṣyasi kathaṁcana
vadhārhakarmaṇānena mama hastagato hyasi
O you worthy of being slain, destroying Sita, you shall not live long as you have been brought under me.

ये च स्त्रीघातिनां लोका लोकवध्यैश्च कुत्सिताः
इह जीवितमुत्सृज्य प्रेत्य तान्प्रतिलप्स्यसे

ye ca strīghātināṁ lokā lokavadhyaiśca kutsitāḥ
iha jīvitamutsṛjya pretya tānpratilapsyase
You shall after the death reach the place which is occupied by those who murder women, a place which is avoided even by those who commit every sort of crime punishable by law.

इति ब्रुवाणो हनुमान्सायुधैर्हरिभिर्वृतः
अभ्यधावत संक्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रसुतं प्रति

iti bruvāṇo hanumānsāyudhairharibhirvṛtaḥ
abhyadhāvata saṁkruddho rākṣasendrasutaṁ prati
Saying this Hanuman, accompanied by monkeys armed with weapons, and excited with ire, proceeded towards the son of the lord or Raksasas.

आपतन्तं महावीर्यं तदनीकं वनौकसाम्
रक्षसां भीमवेगानामनीकेन न्यवारयत्

āpatantaṁ mahāvīryaṁ tadanīkaṁ vanaukasām
rakṣasāṁ bhīmavegānāmanīkena nyavārayat
Beholding the highly powerful monkeys advance thus the Raksasas, inflamed with wrath, obstructed them.

स तां बाणसहस्रेण विक्षोभ्य हरिवाहिनीम्
हरिश्रेष्ठं हनूमन्तमिन्द्रजित्प्रत्युवाच ह

sa tāṁ bāṇasahasreṇa vikṣobhya harivāhinīm
hariśreṣṭhaṁ hanūmantamindrajitpratyuvāca ha
Assailing the monkey-hosts with thousands of arrows, Indrajit spoke to that foremost of monkeys, Hanuman, saying.

इमां हत्वा ततो रामं लक्ष्मणं त्वां च वानर
सुग्रीवं च वधिष्यामि तं चानार्यं विभीषणम्

imāṁ hatvā tato rāmaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ tvāṁ ca vānara
sugrīvaṁ ca vadhiṣyāmi taṁ cānāryaṁ vibhīṣaṇam
Today I shall slay before you all Vaidehi, for whom you, Sugriva and Rama have come. Slaying her, O monkey, I shall afterwards kill you, Rama, Laksmana and Sugriva and the dishonourable Vibhisana.

न हन्तव्याः स्त्रियश्चेति यद्ब्रवीषि प्लवंगम
पीडा करममित्राणां यत्स्यात्कर्तव्यमेत तत्

na hantavyāḥ striyaśceti yadbravīṣi plavaṁgama
pīḍā karamamitrāṇāṁ yatsyātkartavyameta tat

O monkey, about not destroying women, of which you were speaking (I might say) that we must always do what pains our enemies."* *There is one sloka intervening according to some texts, but it has been omitted by many. The reasons for this omission are best known to them. The purport is:-"Why did Rama slay Taraka before? And I shall therefore slay his spouse the daughter of king Janaka.” Hear in Indrajit attempts to justify himself and wants to prove that Rama is equally blameable for this.)

तमेवमुक्त्वा रुदतीं सीतां मायामयीं ततः
शितधारेण खड्गेन निजघानेन्द्रजित्स्वयम्

tamevamuktvā rudatīṁ sītāṁ māyāmayīṁ tataḥ
śitadhāreṇa khaḍgena nijaghānendrajitsvayam
Saying this, Indrajit with a sharp sword, himself killed the illusory Sita thus bewailing.

यज्ञोपवीतमार्गेण छिन्ना तेन तपस्विनी
सा पृथिव्यां पृथुश्रोणी पपात प्रियदर्शना

yajñopavītamārgeṇa chinnā tena tapasvinī
sā pṛthivyāṁ pṛthuśroṇī papāta priyadarśanā
Being sundered by him obliquely in a way in which a sacred thread lies on one's own person, the innocent (Sita) having beautiful countenance fell down on the earth.

तामिन्द्रजित्स्त्रियं हत्वा हनूमन्तमुवाच ह
मया रामस्य पश्येमां कोपेन च निषूदिताम्

tāmindrajitstriyaṁ hatvā hanūmantamuvāca ha
mayā rāmasya paśyemāṁ kopena ca niṣūditām
Slaying her Indrajit spoke to Hanuman,“Behold I have slain (before you) with my sword Rama's beloved. And Vaidehi being thus slain, all your labours have been rendered useless."

ततः खड्गेन महता हत्वा तामिन्द्रजित्स्वयम्
हृष्टः स रथमास्थाय विननाद महास्वनम्

tataḥ khaḍgena mahatā hatvā tāmindrajitsvayam
hṛṣṭaḥ sa rathamāsthāya vinanāda mahāsvanam
a Destroying her with his own hand by means of a huge sword, Indrajit, greatly pleased ascended his car and began to emit dreadful roars.

वानराः शुश्रुवुः शब्दमदूरे प्रत्यवस्थिताः
व्यादितास्यस्य नदतस्तद्दुर्गं संश्रितस्य तु

vānarāḥ śuśruvuḥ śabdamadūre pratyavasthitāḥ
vyāditāsyasya nadatastaddurgaṁ saṁśritasya tu
The monkeys stationed near heard that terrible roar and saw him enter the castel.* *The castle built by Indrajit by means of his illusory power in the air.

तथा तु सीतां विनिहत्य दुर्मतिः; प्रहृष्टचेताः स बभूव रावणिः
तं हृष्टरूपं समुदीक्ष्य वानरा; विषण्णरूपाः समभिप्रदुद्रुवुः

tathā tu sītāṁ vinihatya durmatiḥ; prahṛṣṭacetāḥ sa babhūva rāvaṇiḥ
taṁ hṛṣṭarūpaṁ samudīkṣya vānarā; viṣaṇṇarūpāḥ samabhipradudruvuḥ
And slaying Sita that wicked-minded son of Ravana became greatly pleased. And beholding him thus delighted the monkeys being greatly sorry fled away.

श्रुत्वा तं भीमनिर्ह्रादं शक्राशनिसमस्वनम्
वीक्षमाणा दिशः सर्वा दुद्रुवुर्वानरर्षभाः

śrutvā taṁ bhīmanirhrādaṁ śakrāśanisamasvanam
vīkṣamāṇā diśaḥ sarvā dudruvurvānararṣabhāḥ
Hearing that dreadful uproar resembling the sound of Indra's thunder-bolt, the monkeys, casting their looks on all sides fled away.

तानुवाच ततः सर्वान्हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
विषण्णवदनान्दीनांस्त्रस्तान्विद्रवतः पृथक्

tānuvāca tataḥ sarvānhanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
viṣaṇṇavadanāndīnāṁstrastānvidravataḥ pṛthak
Thereupon Hanuman, the son of Maruta, spoke to them, poorly, terrified and of a sorrowful countenance, saying.

कस्माद्विषण्णवदना विद्रवध्वं प्लवंगमाः
त्यक्तयुद्धसमुत्साहाः शूरत्वं क्व नु वो गतम्

kasmādviṣaṇṇavadanā vidravadhvaṁ plavaṁgamāḥ
tyaktayuddhasamutsāhāḥ śūratvaṁ kva nu vo gatam
O monkeys, why do you look so melancholy and why are you flying away? Why have you renounced your earnest desire for fight? And where is your heroism gone?

पृष्ठतोऽनुव्रजध्वं मामग्रतो यान्तमाहवे
शूरैरभिजनोपेतैरयुक्तं हि निवर्तितुम्

pṛṣṭhato'nuvrajadhvaṁ māmagrato yāntamāhave
śūrairabhijanopetairayuktaṁ hi nivartitum
Do you remain behind me, I shall go first in the battle. It is improper for heroes of noble descent to escape from battle field.

एवमुक्ताः सुसंक्रुद्धा वायुपुत्रेण धीमता
शैलशृङ्गान्द्रुमांश्चैव जगृहुर्हृष्टमानसाः

evamuktāḥ susaṁkruddhā vāyuputreṇa dhīmatā
śailaśṛṅgāndrumāṁścaiva jagṛhurhṛṣṭamānasāḥ
Being thus addressed by that highly intelligent son of the Wind-god, they were greatly excited with wrath and being pleased took up trees and। crags in their hands.

अभिपेतुश्च गर्जन्तो राक्षसान्वानरर्षभाः
परिवार्य हनूमन्तमन्वयुश्च महाहवे

abhipetuśca garjanto rākṣasānvānararṣabhāḥ
parivārya hanūmantamanvayuśca mahāhave
Roaring thus the leading monkeys advanced towards the Raksasas and stood encircling Hanuman in the battle-field.

स तैर्वानरमुख्यैस्तु हनूमान्सर्वतो वृतः
हुताशन इवार्चिष्मानदहच्छत्रुवाहिनीम्

sa tairvānaramukhyaistu hanūmānsarvato vṛtaḥ
hutāśana ivārciṣmānadahacchatruvāhinīm
Being surrounded on all sides by leading monkeys, Hanuman began to burn down enemy's host like to fire spreading its flames.

स राक्षसानां कदनं चकार सुमहाकपिः
वृतो वानरसैन्येन कालान्तकयमोपमः

sa rākṣasānāṁ kadanaṁ cakāra sumahākapiḥ
vṛto vānarasainyena kālāntakayamopamaḥ
Being encircled by monkey-hosts that mighty monkey resembling death himself began to grind the Raksasas.

स तु शोकेन चाविष्टः क्रोधेन च महाकपिः
हनूमान्रावणि रथे महतीं पातयच्छिलाम्

sa tu śokena cāviṣṭaḥ krodhena ca mahākapiḥ
hanūmānrāvaṇi rathe mahatīṁ pātayacchilām
Being overwhelmed with grief and wrought up with ire, that monkey Hanuman, threw a huge crag on the car of that son of Ravana.

तामापतन्तीं दृष्ट्वैव रथः सारथिना तदा
विधेयाश्व समायुक्तः सुदूरमपवाहितः

tāmāpatantīṁ dṛṣṭvaiva rathaḥ sārathinā tadā
vidheyāśva samāyuktaḥ sudūramapavāhitaḥ
Beholding that crag about to fall down on the car, the charioteer moved his horses and it was speedily brought at some distance.

तमिन्द्रजितमप्राप्य रथथं सहसारथिम्
विवेश धरणीं भित्त्वा सा शिलाव्यर्थमुद्यता

tamindrajitamaprāpya rathathaṁ sahasārathim
viveśa dharaṇīṁ bhittvā sā śilāvyarthamudyatā
And not reaching Indrajit stationed on the car and the charioteer, that crag, uselessly hurled, fell down on the earth.

पतितायां शिलायां तु रक्षसां व्यथिता चमूः
तमभ्यधावञ्शतशो नदन्तः काननौकसः

patitāyāṁ śilāyāṁ tu rakṣasāṁ vyathitā camūḥ
tamabhyadhāvañśataśo nadantaḥ kānanaukasaḥ
As the crag falling down the army of the Raksasas were violently crushed.

ते द्रुमांश्च महाकाया गिरिशृङ्गाणि चोद्यताः
चिक्षिपुर्द्विषतां मध्ये वानरा भीमविक्रमाः

te drumāṁśca mahākāyā giriśṛṅgāṇi codyatāḥ
cikṣipurdviṣatāṁ madhye vānarā bhīmavikramāḥ
Thereupon hundreds of huge-bodied monkeys, emitting cries and taking up crags and trees proceeded towards him (Indrajit) and hurled them at him.

वानरैर्तैर्महावीर्यैर्घोररूपा निशाचराः
वीर्यादभिहता वृक्षैर्व्यवेष्टन्त रणक्षितौ

vānarairtairmahāvīryairghorarūpā niśācarāḥ
vīryādabhihatā vṛkṣairvyaveṣṭanta raṇakṣitau
The grim-visaged night-rangers were assailed with trees in that field by the terrible monkeys.

स्वसैन्यमभिवीक्ष्याथ वानरार्दितमिन्द्रजित्
प्रगृहीतायुधः क्रुद्धः परानभिमुखो ययौ

svasainyamabhivīkṣyātha vānarārditamindrajit
pragṛhītāyudhaḥ kruddhaḥ parānabhimukho yayau

Beholding his army thus distressed by the monkeys, Indrajit, excited with wrath, and taking up his dart, proceeded towards the enemies, and encircled by his soldiers showered terrible shafts upon them. And that one of dreadful prowess slew many a leading monkey by means of darts, Asanis, swords, pattisas and clubs.

सस्कन्धविटपैः सालैः शिलाभिश्च महाबलैः
हनूमान्कदनं चक्रे रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्

saskandhaviṭapaiḥ sālaiḥ śilābhiśca mahābalaiḥ
hanūmānkadanaṁ cakre rakṣasāṁ bhīmakarmaṇām
The highly powerful monkeys destroyed his retinue, with crags, stones and trees having strong trunks. And Hanuman thus crushed many a Raksasa of terrible deeds.

स निवार्य परानीकमब्रवीत्तान्वनौकसः
हनूमान्संनिवर्तध्वं न नः साध्यमिदं बलम्

sa nivārya parānīkamabravīttānvanaukasaḥ
hanūmānsaṁnivartadhvaṁ na naḥ sādhyamidaṁ balam
Obstructing the Raksasas (for some time) Hanuman spoke to monkeys, saying, “Stay, we should not fight now.

त्यक्त्वा प्राणान्विचेष्टन्तो राम प्रियचिकीर्षवः
यन्निमित्तं हि युध्यामो हता सा जनकात्मजा

tyaktvā prāṇānviceṣṭanto rāma priyacikīrṣavaḥ
yannimittaṁ hi yudhyāmo hatā sā janakātmajā
That daughter of Janaka has been slain, for whom we have engaged in fight, renouncing all hope of life and desiring to accomplish Rama's satisfaction.

इममर्थं हि विज्ञाप्य रामं सुग्रीवमेव च
तौ यत्प्रतिविधास्येते तत्करिष्यामहे वयम्

imamarthaṁ hi vijñāpya rāmaṁ sugrīvameva ca
tau yatpratividhāsyete tatkariṣyāmahe vayam
Let us now go and inform Rama and Sugriva of it. And we shall do as we shall be commanded by them.

इत्युक्त्वा वानरश्रेष्ठो वारयन्सर्ववानरान्
शनैः शनैरसंत्रस्तः सबलः स न्यवर्तत

ityuktvā vānaraśreṣṭho vārayansarvavānarān
śanaiḥ śanairasaṁtrastaḥ sabalaḥ sa nyavartata
Saying this and desisting all the monkeys from encounter that foremost of monkeys proceeded undaunted and heroically.

स तु प्रेक्ष्य हनूमन्तं व्रजन्तं यत्र राघवः
निकुम्भिलामधिष्ठाय पावकं जुहुवे न्द्रजित्

sa tu prekṣya hanūmantaṁ vrajantaṁ yatra rāghavaḥ
nikumbhilāmadhiṣṭhāya pāvakaṁ juhuve ndrajit
Beholding Hanuman proceed thus where Raghava was that wicked-minded one (Indrajit) with a view to offer oblations to fire entered the sacrificial altar Nikumbhila.

सोऽर्चिः पिनद्धो ददृशे होमशोणिततर्पितः
संध्यागत इवादित्यः स तीव्राग्निः समुत्थितः

so'rciḥ pinaddho dadṛśe homaśoṇitatarpitaḥ
saṁdhyāgata ivādityaḥ sa tīvrāgniḥ samutthitaḥ
Reaching there Indrajit lighted up fire and began to pour oblations therein. And the fire blazed up receiving oblations of blood, and being satisfied assumed the appearance of the setting sun.

अथेन्द्रजिद्राक्षसभूतये तु; जुहाव हव्यं विधिना विधानवत्
दृष्ट्वा व्यतिष्ठन्त च राक्षसास्ते; महासमूहेषु नयानयज्ञाः

athendrajidrākṣasabhūtaye tu; juhāva havyaṁ vidhinā vidhānavat
dṛṣṭvā vyatiṣṭhanta ca rākṣasāste; mahāsamūheṣu nayānayajñāḥ

Indrajit conversant with all ceremonials, offered oblations in due form for the welfare of the Raksasas. And they all stood there watching the result and desirous of ascertaining the success of the battle.* *This Sloka has been left off in some editions.

राघवश्चापि विपुलं तं राक्षसवनौकसाम्
श्रुत्वा संग्रामनिर्घोषं जाम्बवन्तमुवाच ह

rāghavaścāpi vipulaṁ taṁ rākṣasavanaukasām
śrutvā saṁgrāmanirghoṣaṁ jāmbavantamuvāca ha
Hearing the terrible war-cry of the Raksasas and monkeys Raghava spoke to Jambavan, saying.

सौम्य नूनं हनुमता कृतं कर्म सुदुष्करम्
